title: [bug] A fact's id is hashed from Row.Label while row_label publishes PrintedLabel(): two-anchor rows collide
description:
internal/fact/fact.go builds the published RowLabel from PrintedLabel() but
hashes the ID from the BARE Label:

  RowLabel:  v.Row.PrintedLabel()          // Label + " " + LabelTail
  ID:        MakeID(..., v.Row.Label, ...) // Label only

So a fact's id is keyed on a string that is NOT the row_label it publishes. Two
rows sharing a Label and differing only in LabelTail -- exactly the case
Row.LabelTail was added for -- produce the SAME id.

CONFIRMED, not theoretical. internal/mapping/testdata/transfers-p76.yaml rule
p76-transfers-in-enterprise-a carries the two rows p76 prints as

  Transfer From Wastewater   to Stormwater             ...
  Transfer From Wastewater   to Wastewater Replacement ...

Both hash to fisc-f-e638ee25b997 for FY2026. CheckUniqueIDs then fails the
build.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A DUPLICATE. The whole point of Row.LabelTail (landed
2026-08-21, "a row may be named by two published anchors") was to make p76
mappable, and Row.Identity() already exists and returns Label + "\x1f" +
LabelTail precisely because "uniqueness is enforced on this rather than on
Label, because two rows may legitimately share a source fund and differ only in
their destination" (internal/mapping/rule.go:330-334). The resolver knows this.
The fact model does not.

It also contradicts the fact-id-needs-the-row-label memory, which records that
row_label is in the id tuple BECAUSE a category is not unique within a rule. The
id currently carries a label that is not the published one, so the property that
memory asserts does not hold for any two-anchor row.

BLOCKS fisc-5gk.3.1 -- publishing p76 is the thing LabelTail was built for and
it cannot succeed until this is fixed.

WHAT TO DECIDE, and it is not obvious which way: MakeID should take
PrintedLabel() (matching what is published) or Identity() (matching what the
resolver enforces uniqueness on). They differ in the separator only, but the id
is content-addressed and permanent, so the choice is a published claim. Note
either choice CHANGES NO EXISTING FACT ID: no row in
mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml carries a label_tail, so
facts.jsonl must stay byte-identical -- and that is the test.

Found by /code-review over the 8 commits ahead of origin/main, 2026-08-22, and
confirmed by reading fact.go and rule.go.
acceptance_criteria: two rows differing only in label_tail get distinct ids; the transfers-p76 fixture builds without a CheckUniqueIDs failure; facts.jsonl is byte-identical because no shipped rule uses label_tail; the choice between PrintedLabel() and Identity() is recorded with its reason
close_reason: Landed in 3589fa2 with a fifth site neither bead named (canonicalRows pairing on Label, colliding RowIndex with omissions). MakeID takes PrintedLabel(); the reasoning and its accepted cost are in the doc comment.

comments.author: Jon Crussell
comments.text:
DECIDED: MakeID takes Row.PrintedLabel(), not Row.Identity() and not Row.Label.
fact.FromValues now passes v.Row.PrintedLabel(), which is the same string the
record publishes as row_label. The reasoning is written into fact.MakeID's doc
comment; in short:

1. AN ID MUST BE RECOMPUTABLE FROM THE RECORD IT NAMES. facts.jsonl is the
   audit trail and the id is a content address; a reader holding one line has
   to be able to re-derive its id from the fields printed on that line.
   Identity() is not one of those fields, and it cannot be recovered from
   row_label either -- "A B" could be one anchor or two. Hashing Identity()
   would leave the id keyed on a string that appears nowhere in the corpus.

2. THE TUPLE SEPARATOR MUST NOT OCCUR INSIDE A COMPONENT. That is the invariant
   MakeID's own comment rests on ("joining on a character that occurs in the
   data would let two different tuples hash identically"), and the
   fact-id-needs-the-row-label memory records the \x1f join as deliberate.
   Identity() carries a \x1f of its own; PrintedLabel() joins its anchors with
   a space and cannot.

The counter-argument -- "the resolver enforces uniqueness on Identity(), so the
id should use it" -- is answered by noticing the two uniqueness properties are
different questions asked in different places. The resolver needs "no two rows
of this rule are the same row on the page"; the id needs "no two published facts
are indistinguishable to a reader of facts.jsonl". They can disagree exactly
once: two rows with distinct identities that print the same label, e.g.
{label: "A B"} and {label: "A", label_tail: "B"}. Those two facts publish one
row_label and are indistinguishable in the data WHATEVER their ids are, so that
is a defect to refuse, not to route around. parse.go now refuses it directly
("two rows print as %q"), with CheckUniqueIDs as the backstop, and both notions
are enforced in the place each belongs.

Also fixed: fact.go's comment claiming "the label ... the parser already
enforces as unique" -- true of Identity() only -- now states both properties.

EVIDENCE. Mutating the call site back to v.Row.Label:
  TestTwoAnchorRowsGetDistinctIDs: p76 facts collide: id fisc-f-1057b78cfb78 is
  claimed twice: rule "p76-transfers-in-enterprise-a" p76 says $0.00, rule
  "p76-transfers-in-enterprise-a" p76 says $1,056,357.00 (both are
  livermore-budget-fy2026-2027 transfers/in enterprise FY2024 actual)
  TestIDIsBuiltFromTheLabelTheFactPublishes: id = fisc-f-d416a4715f4c, want
  fisc-f-2213cf22723f: the id must be a function of the published row_label
  "Transfer From Wastewater to Stormwater"

The colliding pair is rows 2 and 4 of p76-transfers-in-enterprise-a, both
labelled "Transfer From Wastewater" -- to Stormwater and to LAVWMA / Wastewater.
(The description named "to Wastewater Replacement"; that row carries no source
in the fixture, so it was never the second half of the collision.) The fixture
now builds with distinct ids, FY2026:
  fisc-f-ddd73cd88b5d  "Transfer From General Fund to Stormwater"
  fisc-f-61c80098e07b  "Transfer From Wastewater to Stormwater"
  fisc-f-20865cc38977  "to Wastewater Replacement"
  fisc-f-d042561b60b7  "Transfer From Wastewater to LAVWMA / Wastewater"

facts/facts.jsonl is byte-identical to the committed file (no shipped rule
carries a label_tail), and fisc verify is 20 passed / 0 failed / 5 vacuous /
1 skipped.

title: pp.167-170 have no decided scope either: fisc-aes's gap, one schedule over
description:
fisc-aes exists because fisc-u2v's 2026-08-21 decision covers pp.127-140 and the
scope `revenue-by-fund` ONLY, and never names a scope for p76. THE SAME GAP
EXISTS FOR pp.167-170 AND NOBODY FILED IT.

VERIFIED: `bd search scope` returns eight beads -- fisc-aes, fisc-u2v,
fisc-1wr.4, fisc-gkv, fisc-5gk.3.1, fisc-5gk.6, byob-security.5, byob-config.1
-- and not one of them decides a scope string for the department x object
schedule.

WHAT IS THERE INSTEAD IS AN ASSUMPTION. fisc-1wr.2's 2026-08-21 note says
"Once the scope axis exists, fisc-5gk.2's pp.167-170 facts carry their own
scope and are NOT IN THE SPINE GRAPH AT ALL". That sentence is load-bearing for
three separate conclusions in this backlog -- it is why fisc-1wr.2's expenditure
clause is declared blinded, why the netCells refusal (internal/project/sankey.go
:531-538) is NOT a fisc-5gk.2 blocker, and why 196 department-bearing facts are
expected not to reach the spine graph. All three rest on a scope nobody chose.

THE FAILURE IT ALLOWS is fisc-u2v's mechanism on the expenditure side, and it
is the same quiet one. pp.167-170's 49 object rows tie to the p66 spine EXACTLY
per object category in all four columns -- Wages & Benefits 81,801,011 /
83,825,633, Services & Supplies 62,849,791 / 65,188,946, total 144,650,802 /
149,014,579. That exactness is what makes doubling silent: an author writing
`scope: all-funds-gross` gets a General Fund expenditure of 289,301,604 with
every check green, because netCells keys on (kind, category, fundGroup) and the
spine cell and the detail cell are the same key.

WHAT TO SETTLE, mirroring fisc-aes:
- the scope string (e.g. expenditure-by-department), and its unprojectedScopes
  entry with a reason;
- that its reconciliation is a TIER 1 ZERO-TOLERANCE identity, not a tolerance:
  the four object categories tie to the cent, so expenditure-detail-ties-to-spine
  is the same shape as revenue-detail-ties-to-spine and needs the same
  union-of-keys and kind-restriction treatment (fisc-u2v DEFECTs 1 and 2);
- whether the department axis affects the scope at all, or whether department is
  purely a row_path component within one scope. netCells refuses a
  department-bearing fact outright today, so the answer determines whether that
  refusal is reachable.

Found while planning the backlog waves, 2026-08-22, by checking whether
fisc-aes's argument generalises. It does.
acceptance_criteria: a scope string for pp.167-170 is decided and recorded here with its unprojectedScopes reason; its reconciliation against the spine is declared tier 1 zero tolerance; whether department participates in the scope axis is answered; a test asserts GF Wages & Benefits publishes 81,801,011 and not 163,602,022
notes:
2026-08-23 THE unprojectedScopes REASON TEXT THIS BEAD WROTE OVERSTATES ITS OWN CHECK, corrected when the entry landed (fisc-5gk.2).

SECTION (1) SPECIFIES: 'expenditure-detail-ties-to-spine reconciles all 196 facts against spine facts that ARE graph-checked.'

IT RECONCILES 98. The schedule publishes 49 object rows x 4 columns, and pp.66-67 print only the two ADOPTED columns -- this bead's own section (2) says so ('only FY2026 and FY2027 adopted are RECONCILED against the spine, because pp.66-67 print no actual or revised column'), so the two halves of the decision disagreed. The FY2023-24 actual and FY2024-25 revised facts reconcile against the schedule's own printed totals at build time and against nothing on the spine.

It matters more than a normal wording slip because fisc verify PRINTS THE REASON STRING VERBATIM on the facts-are-projected line, so the overstatement was published on every run. The landed text now says '98 of its 196' and names why the other half has nothing to tie to.

A SECOND CORRECTION, to a sentence this bead inherited from fisc-u2v (3): 'for each (fiscal_year, basis) present in BOTH scopes'. Read as an intersection -- which is the natural reading and the one an implementer writes -- that lets the DETAIL opt out of a column by dropping it. Measured with a spine carrying two years and a detail carrying one: the check passes, one cell examined, a whole year of General Fund expenditure unreconciled. That is fisc-u2v's own DEFECT 2 (union of keys, never a skip) at the pair level rather than the category level.

THE RULE, as landed: THE SPINE DECIDES WHICH PAIRS MUST BE RECONCILED. A spine column with no detail behind it is a gap in the MAPPING and fails. A detail column with no spine column is a gap in the DOCUMENT and is reported in the summary as unreconciled. The asymmetry runs one way only. fisc-5gk.1 and fisc-5gk.3.1 must not copy the 'present in both' wording.
close_reason: Decided: scope expenditure-by-department for pp.167-170, department is a row_path component and not a scope axis, tier-1 zero-tolerance reconciliation restricted to kind=expenditure AND fund_group=general. Joint note with fisc-aes recorded 2026-08-23; 49 object rows re-summed off the pages. Test clause moved to fisc-5gk.2.

title: p76 transfers have no scope: fisc-u2v decided revenue only
description:
fisc-5gk.3.1 lists as its blocker on fisc-u2v: "The scope axis, the same
question as fisc-u2v but for transfers rather than revenue detail, and it must
reconcile AGAINST the spine rather than sum with it."

fisc-u2v's 2026-08-21 decision covers pp.127-140 and the scope `revenue-by-fund`
ONLY. It never names a scope for p76. fisc-4rh's decision of the same date
covers fact shape, id collision and the pairing id -- not scope. So bd reports
fisc-5gk.3.1's blocker as satisfied when the question it depends on is
unanswered.

THE FAILURE THIS ALLOWS, and it is quiet.

An author finding no scope decision reads Options.Scope's doc and writes
`scope: all-funds-gross`. p76's 176 facts join the spine projection. fisc-5gk.3
ALREADY PROVED every destination fund group ties to p66-67's TRANSFER IN cell
exactly -- which is precisely what makes the doubling silent. netCells sums
them: (transfer_in, transfers/in, general) 480,400 -> 960,800; transfer_out
general 10,037,797 -> 20,075,594; and the published transfer_residual_cents
moves from $38,086,737 to roughly double.

headline-transfer-residual and link-values-tie-to-facts both stay GREEN -- they
tie the graph to the facts it was built from, not to the document. That is
fisc-u2v's mechanism verbatim, one schedule over.

AND THE ONE CHECK THAT WOULD SEE IT IS EXEMPT THERE. fisc-u2v's
revenue-detail-ties-to-spine declares exactly one exception:
(transfer_in, transfers/in, general), because pp.127-130 print no GF Transfers
In row. That is the SAME KEY the doubled GF leg lands on.

WHAT TO SETTLE
- the scope string (e.g. transfers-by-fund), and its unprojectedScopes entry
  with a reason;
- its own reconciliation against the spine -- p76 ties to the cent on both
  budget columns and to the spine's TRANSFER IN / TRANSFER OUT rows exactly
  (fisc-5gk.3), so like the revenue side this is a TIER 1 ZERO-TOLERANCE
  identity, not a tolerance;
- and consequently that fisc-u2v's acceptance test D ("unprojectedScopes holds
  exactly the one entry") is reworded to "exactly the entries declared, one per
  mapped non-spine schedule, each with a reason". As written it collides with
  this bead and with fisc-5gk.2's.

Found in peer review of the landing plan, 2026-08-21.
acceptance_criteria: p76 has a decided scope string recorded here; it reconciles against the spine as a tier-1 identity; fisc-u2v's exactly-one-entry test is reworded; a test asserts the GF transfer-in leg is 480,400 and not 960,800
notes:
2026-08-24 CORRECTION, found in peer review of the p76 landing plan and
re-derived off testdata/pages/budget-p0076.txt against data/funds.yaml. Two
claims in section (2) are wrong. The DECISION stands; the reasoning under it
does not.

(1) THE OUT-SIDE TABLE CONFLATES CAPITAL INTO SPECIAL REVENUE. It gives FY2026
special-revenue 1,028,200 and capital 0. But Traffic Impact Fee (510), County
Measure D (550) and State - Gas Tax (560) are type: capital in data/funds.yaml,
and p76 lists all three as payers. The true detail split is:

  FY2026   capital 211,150      special-revenue 817,050    (sum 1,028,200)
  FY2027   capital 217,485      special-revenue 800,550    (sum 1,018,035)

data/funds.yaml's own header already said this -- "the capital funds Transfers
Out (181,971 / 210,500 / 211,150 / 217,485) is exactly p76 Traffic Imp Fee +
State Gas Tax + Measure D each year" -- so the table contradicts a figure this
repository had already derived.

(2) "IN FY2026-27 IT IS IMPOSSIBLE" IS FALSE. The bead says p76 itemises
1,018,035 of special-revenue-sourced transfers against a p67 special-revenue
TRANSFER OUT of 900,550, "which would require a NEGATIVE to-CIP of -117,485".
1,018,035 is the NON-MAJOR total, not the special-revenue part. Both years split
cleanly:

  FY2026   capital 28,584,740 - 211,150 = 28,373,590
           special-revenue 1,137,050 - 817,050 = 320,000     sum 28,693,590
  FY2027   capital 36,047,736 - 217,485 = 35,830,251
           special-revenue 900,550 - 800,550 = 100,000       sum 35,930,251

and those sums are p0073.txt:56 and p0075.txt:56 exactly.

CLAUSE (c) STILL STANDS, ON A DIFFERENT AND BETTER GROUND. pp.72-75 print
to-CIP per major fund and then ONE aggregate line for all non-major funds, so a
per-group constant would be DERIVED by difference from p67 while the pair is
PUBLISHED. That is this project's own rule, not an impossibility claim -- and it
is the stronger argument, because it does not depend on an arithmetic that turns
out to be wrong.

WHERE THE ERROR HAD SPREAD. docs/sankey-contract.md shipped the wrong
decomposition as a table, with the sentence "Capital and Internal Service pay
nothing p76 lists". mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml claimed the city
"itemises nowhere" what pp.72-75 print under a heading.
internal/mapping/transfers_p76_test.go carried it in a comment. All three
corrected in 19bb265, together with the arithmetic that was missing:
TestP76SourcesDecomposeTheResidualByFundType resolves every payer through
registry.FundByLabel and asserts spine_TRANSFER_OUT == p76_paid + to_CIP for all
six groups in both budget years. Proven failable -- restoring the shipped pair
reddens it, and the sum-to-residual clause stays green, because the error moved
money between two rows of one total. That is why nothing caught it for four
commits.

(3) THE unprojectedScopes REASON IN SECTION (1) OVERSTATES, which is the exact
failure mode the memory detail-ties-to-spine-shape (4) warns about and which
fisc-brx already committed once. It says the check "reconciles every fact
against spine facts that ARE graph-checked". The IN side does. The OUT side
reconciles only after adding a hand-typed constant read off pp.72-75, which are
not mapped and not fixtures; and the permanent in-leg is "reconciled" as a
published zero against an absent spine column. verify prints that string
verbatim on every run. Re-word it before it lands.
close_reason: Decided: scope transfers-by-fund for p76, tier-1 zero-tolerance reconciliation in three clauses, unprojectedScopes entry lands with fisc-5gk.3.1. Joint note with fisc-brx recorded 2026-08-23; figures re-verified off the pages. Test clause moved to fisc-5gk.3.1.

title: Revenue-detail scope: pp.127-140 double-count the spine unless the scope axis is decided
description:
Mapping pp.127-140 the obvious way publishes DOUBLE the city's General Fund
revenue, and every check stays green. This bead must be decided before any YAML
is written for fisc-5gk.1.

THE MECHANISM

internal/project/sankey.go:545 keys cells on (kind, category, fundGroup).
data/taxonomy.yaml holds 25 slugs, ALL category-level -- there is no slug for a
revenue line item. So each of p127's thirteen property-tax detail rows must
carry category: taxes/property, fund_group: general, which is the SAME cellKey
as the p66 spine fact. netCells sums them.

They are the same money. Verified:
  p0066.txt:13  Property Taxes (General Fund) FY2025-26 = 64,143,762
  p0127.txt:37  Total Property Taxes          FY2025-26 = 64,143,762

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT

- headline-ties-to-facts and link-values-tie-to-facts tie the graph to the facts
  it was built FROM, not to the document.
- Build-time CheckTotals is per-part; the p66 part and the p127 part each pass
  against their own printed totals.
- The result is a plausible wrong value, which is the exact defect class this
  project exists to prevent.

THE TWO OPTIONS, BOTH WITH A COST

(a) scope: all-funds-gross -- silently doubles GF revenue. Unacceptable.
(b) A new scope string -- facts-are-projected (internal/check/coverage.go:98-127)
    then FAILS unless the scope is added to unprojectedScopes (coverage.go:25,
    currently empty). That is a Go change, not a YAML change.

coverage.go's own doc comment records the precedent: "Moving twenty facts to a
mistyped `all-funds-gross-detail` took over half the city's revenue out of the
published chart, and every check still passed."

WHAT THIS BEAD MUST SETTLE

- the scope string for revenue detail;
- whether line items get their own taxonomy slugs or a sub-category axis;
- how the detail RECONCILES AGAINST the spine rather than adding to it.

This is the revenue lane's counterpart to fisc-28s and fisc-o15, which the
department lane has and this lane did not. Found in peer review of the landing
plan, 2026-08-18.
acceptance_criteria: the scope string is decided and recorded here; line-item identity (own slugs vs sub-category axis) is decided; the detail reconciles against the spine rather than summing with it; a test asserts the published GF property-tax figure is 64,143,762 and NOT 128,287,524
notes:
2026-08-21 DECIDED. All four points this bead asks to settle, plus the
measurement that makes the answer cheap. Figures below were computed by a design
pass and then VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY off the committed pages before this note was
written; the verification is recorded at the end.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGES THE SHAPE OF THE ANSWER

pp.127-140 are not "some detail". Summed and keyed the way netCells keys cells
(internal/project/sankey.go:339), they reproduce THE ENTIRE REVENUE SIDE of
pp.66-67 exactly -- all six fund groups, both budget years:

  fund group        detail FY2026 / FY2027      p66-67 printed
  general           157,873,470 / 164,358,147   identical
  enterprise         67,514,261 /  70,308,250   identical
  capital            27,145,882 /  26,888,254   identical
  debt-service                0 /           0   identical
  special-revenue    28,465,560 /  20,892,522   identical
  internal-service   18,969,834 /  19,995,870   identical

Per category too: special-revenue FY2026 taxes/property 5,315,652, taxes/other
170,000, intergovernmental 6,824,835, charges-for-services 2,129,297,
use-of-money-and-property 741,132, contributions-outsourced 1,934,000,
miscellaneous-revenue 11,350,644 -- each equal to its printed p67 cell to the
cent.

So the detail is a COMPLETE, EXACT, ALTERNATIVE DECOMPOSITION of the spine's
revenue side. The reconciliation is therefore a TOTAL IDENTITY -- tier 1, zero
tolerance -- not a partial cross-check needing a document-derived tolerance. That
single fact drives every decision below.

TWO BOUNDED ASYMMETRIES, both accounted for rather than waved at:
- pp.127-130 print NO General Fund "Transfers In" row. p130's "Total General
  Fund" is TOTAL REVENUES, not TOTAL SOURCES. The spine's GF transfer-in 480,400
  has no detail counterpart. This is the ONE declared exception.
- pp.131-140 print a Permanent Funds section (p134) that pp.66-67 have no column
  for (fisc-u8o). Transfers-only and ZERO in both budget years, so it cannot
  break the tie. Measurement appended to fisc-u8o on this date.

SIZE, re-measured: 231 data rows x 4 columns = 924 FACTS. Not the ~1,600 a row
count suggests. The other 81 printed rows are `Total <category>` / `Total <fund>`
lines, which become total_row ASSERTIONS rather than facts -- the document
checking our work on 81 separate blocks.

(1) THE SCOPE STRING: `revenue-by-fund`, covering ALL of pp.127-140.

Not two scopes. Not all-funds-gross. And emphatically NOT `all-funds-gross-detail`
-- that string is verbatim the incident recorded in internal/check/coverage.go
:10-23, and adopting it would make that doc comment read as describing the real
scope rather than the near-miss it warns about.

Options.Scope's own doc (internal/project/project.go:82-88) already says scope
"selects the schedule a fact came from" and is "the guard that keeps a second
schedule's facts out of a projection built for the citywide spine". This applies
existing semantics; it does not invent an axis.

No `/` in the string: fact.ColumnPath (internal/fact/fact.go:160-176) falls back
to the rule's scope when a column carries no fund dimension, so a scope with a
slash would be indistinguishable from a column path. Every detail column will
carry a fund so the fallback never fires -- but the near-miss should not exist.

WHY pp.131-140 SHARE THE SCOPE WITH pp.127-130. They cannot double-count each
other: the General Fund has no section on pp.131-140 and pp.127-130 have no other
fund -- disjoint BY FUND, not by convention. And only TOGETHER do they reproduce
all six spine columns; split them and neither half can state completeness, and
the reconciliation degrades into two partial claims with a gap between them where
a third schedule could land unnoticed.

Counter-argument, stated fairly: the row semantics genuinely differ. A p127 row
is a line item BELOW a category; a p133 row IS a category. That is real, and it
is why someone would split the scope. It is answered by fields that already
exist -- the difference is carried by row_label vs category and by fund, both in
MakeID's tuple. Promoting it to a scope puts a guard where there is no hazard,
costs the six-group tie, and by the same logic would force a third scope for the
single `Oth Financing Source` row on p139.

(2) LINE-ITEM IDENTITY: NEITHER new taxonomy slugs NOR a sub-category axis.

The line item is the fact's row_label. Its category stays one of the ten spine
slugs. data/taxonomy.yaml ALREADY DECIDED THIS in prose -- its HIERARCHY section
says the hierarchy is "deliberately NOT used below the ten revenue categories...
Those detail lines are a rule's `label`, not a `category`. Giving each one a slug
would invent a classification the city does not make and would double the surface
on which two spellings of the same thing can drift apart." fact.MakeID's doc
comment (internal/fact/fact.go:118-125) already anticipates the thirteen p127
lines sharing one category and being told apart by label. Both were written for
this bead. RATIFIED, not relitigated.

THE DECISIVE ARGUMENT AGAINST THE SUB-CATEGORY AXIS is that it does not solve
this bead's problem and makes it worse. Add `subcategory` to cellKey and property
tax becomes FOURTEEN cells -- the spine's one plus thirteen -- all in the graph,
all summed into AllFundsGrossRevenueCents. The published headline is STILL
128,287,524, and now the node list is wrong too. Line-item identity is ORTHOGONAL
to the double-count. Only the scope axis closes it.

Verified no coverage gap: every row label on pp.131-140 resolves to an existing
taxonomy slug or alias -- zero unknowns across all ten pages, including
`Use of Money & Prop`, `ContributionsOutSrce`, `Miscellaneous Rev` and
`Oth Financing Source`.

(3) HOW THE DETAIL RECONCILES AGAINST THE SPINE: a new TIER 1 check,
`revenue-detail-ties-to-spine`, reading Subject.Facts directly rather than any
graph, registered immediately after &factsAreProjected{} (internal/check/check.go
:179).

For each (fiscal_year, basis) present in BOTH scopes -- today FY2026 and FY2027
adopted only; pp.66-67 print no actual or revised column, so the detail's
FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 columns have no counterpart and are NOT reconciled --
group both scopes' facts by {kind, category, fund_group} and assert the sums are
EQUAL.

Three properties make this the right shape:
- The key IS cellKey's tuple, so the check is visibly the mechanism's negative:
  it asserts equality on precisely the tuple the collision would have happened on.
- A key present on only one side must sum to ZERO, which disposes of the ~40
  empty cells (p67 prints a dash for taxes/property under capital; pp.131-140
  print no such row) without a table of exceptions.
- Exactly ONE declared exception, in Go, with its reason:
  (transfer_in, transfers/in, general), for the missing GF Transfers In row.

TIER 1, NOT TIER 2. Every reconciled figure ties exactly; there is nothing
document-derived to tolerate. p127's known +$1 (fisc-2sd) is in the FY2023-24
actual column, which this check never reconciles and which stated_total_deltas
already absorbs at build time.

This is a strictly STRONGER form of fisc-1wr.2's promoted clause for the revenue
side -- per cell rather than per total. fisc-1wr.2's EXPENDITURE clause is
unaffected and is still the only thing that would catch the same mechanism in the
pp.167-183 lane. It stays P0.

(4) unprojectedScopes GAINS EXACTLY ONE ENTRY -- forced, not chosen.

A projection landing WITH the facts was the preferred answer and it cannot be
had: fisc-gxa.2 DEPENDS ON fisc-5gk.1, and fisc-oxf (schema v2, finest-grain
links) is where a fund-tier graph belongs. The facts must land before anything
draws them. Inverting that edge to keep the map empty would be worse than the
entry.

What makes the entry an honest declaration rather than a hole: coverage.go's own
comment says exempted facts are "still checked by everything above the projection
line", and here that is not a consolation but the whole coverage --
revenue-detail-ties-to-spine ties all 924 facts, cell by cell, to spine facts
that ARE graph-checked. The declaration exempts them from the graph checks and
hands them to a stronger one. describeDeclared (coverage.go:145-156) prints the
count and reason on every fisc verify run, so it is loud.

ADD THE STALE-DECLARATION FAILURE IN THE SAME CHANGE. factsAreProjected consults
the map only for UNPROJECTED facts, so the moment fisc-gxa.2 projects this scope
the declaration goes silent and becomes a false claim about the corpus. Same
direction as fisc-2sd's third failure mode (a declared delta that now ties
exactly must fail, telling the author to remove the declaration). Fail any entry
that declared zero facts, distinguishing "the scope has no facts" from "the scope
is now projected". That retires the entry automatically instead of leaving a
924-fact exemption for whoever forgets.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS -- four, and B is what makes A failable

A. TestRevenueDetailDoesNotEnterTheSpine (internal/project/sankey_test.go; the
   harness exists -- facts(t, specs...), buildGraph, linkBetween in
   fixture_test.go). Spine facts ++ the thirteen p127 property-tax facts at
   revenue-by-fund. Assert the revenue/taxes/property -> fund-group/general link
   is 6,414,376,200 cents; that it cites EXACTLY ONE fact id (the spine's); and
   that Build is BYTE-IDENTICAL to testdata/sankey.golden.json. The byte-identity
   clause is the strongest form available -- it says 924 new facts moved nothing
   in the published document, and it fails on ten links rather than one if the
   scope guard breaks.

B. TestDetailAtSpineScopeWouldDoubleTheGeneralFund -- the same facts with Scope
   mutated to PublishedScope; assert 12,828,752,400. Pinning the WRONG number by
   name is this repo's house style (transfers_p76_test.go pins the $38,086,737
   residual; statedtotaldelta_test.go carries the +$1). It converts "every check
   stays green" from a hazard in a bead into a named fact about the machinery.

C. internal/mapping/revenue_detail_test.go, mirroring transfers_p76_test.go: the
   full six-group, ten-category tie for FY2026 and FY2027 with BOTH SIDES READ
   FROM THE PAGES and no figure typed in except the page's own printed total;
   plus permanent-funds zero in both budget years and non-zero in FY2024, so the
   check reddens if the page stops evidencing fisc-u8o rather than absorbing it.

D. A test asserting unprojectedScopes holds exactly the one entry, and that a
   scope which becomes projected trips the stale-declaration branch.

HOW THIS COULD STILL GO WRONG -- four routes, three mitigated

1. A third schedule enters the scope (someone maps pp.68-75 at revenue-by-fund
   because "it's by fund"). Mitigated structurally: the tie requires the scope's
   per-cell sums to EQUAL the spine's, so over-inclusion fails immediately. This
   is why the tie must be equality in both directions, never "detail <= spine".
2. A printed total row mapped as a data row -- pp.127-140 print 81 of them.
   Build-time CheckTotals cannot see it (no declared total to compare against);
   the tie check fails at exactly 2x. Covered only because the reconciliation is
   a CHECK and not merely a build-time assertion.
3. Transfers In counted as revenue to make the eleven mixed fund totals tie
   without Row.Kind. Enterprise revenue becomes 80,761,261 against 67,514,261 --
   caught. Exposes a real hole filed as fisc-f0k: nothing asserts a fact's kind
   is among its category's declared kinds.
4. THE ONE THAT SURVIVES -- a fund number mis-assigned WITHIN THE CORRECT FUND
   TYPE. Filed as fisc-u54, blocking fisc-5gk.1. Not hypothetical: p134's
   `Doolan Canyon Preserve Endow` truncates to within one word of its same-type
   sibling `Doolan Canyon Open Space` (470 and 471, both permanent).

Also found while verifying coverage, both now filed:
- fisc-nne: `Police Evidence` (p136, $25,000 / $31,000) has NO data/funds.yaml
  entry in any spelling. Blocks fisc-5gk.1.
- fisc-8dz gains six more cases, all on pp.131-140: Cal Home Reuse (205, case),
  California Begin Program (206), Asset Seizure - Dep of Justice (221, one
  letter), Transferable Development Cred (582), Doolan Canyon Preserve Endow

CONSEQUENCE FOR fisc-uli, which was deferred and should not be: eleven funds on
pp.131-140 print revenue rows AND a Transfers In row inside ONE printed
`Total <fund>`. Rule.Kind is per rule and CheckTotals is per (rule, part), so

CONSEQUENCE FOR fisc-5gk.4: its 2026-08-18 note is correct and now arithmetically

VERIFICATION OF THIS NOTE'S OWN FIGURES, done independently of the design pass
before recording:
  p0130.txt:40  "Total General Fund  $142,028,002 $148,800,148 $157,873,470 $164,358,147"
  budget-p0066.txt:23  "TOTAL REVENUES: $157,873,470 $164,358,147 $67,514,261 $70,308,250"

All six fund groups and both budget years agree with the table above.
2026-08-21 CORRECTION FROM PEER REVIEW, same day. The decision above stands;
its CHECK SPECIFICATION was wrong in a way that cannot pass, and one figure in
it needs qualifying. Recorded here rather than silently fixed at implementation
time, because the spec above is what an implementer would have built.

WHAT SURVIVED. The six-fund-group measurement was independently re-derived by
SUMMING THE DETAIL ROWS off data/extracted (not by reading the printed Total
lines, which is all the first verification did). All twelve figures hold. An
independent reproduction of the proposed grouping over {category, fund_group}
for FY2026 and FY2027 yields EXACTLY ONE mismatched cell -- (general,

too: pp.131/132 sum to 13,247,000 (spine enterprise), p134's three to 6,984,597

DEFECT 1 -- THE CHECK AS SPECIFIED CANNOT PASS ON A CORRECT CORPUS.

"group both scopes' facts by {kind, category, fund_group} and assert the sums
are equal" has no KIND RESTRICTION. The spine scope is not a revenue schedule:
at all-funds-gross FY2026 it also carries (expenditure, wages-and-benefits,
general) 8,180,101,100, (expenditure, services-and-supplies, general)
6,284,979,100, (transfer_out, transfers/out, capital) 2,858,474,000,
(fund_balance, fund-balance/beginning, capital) 11,071,354,500 and ~30 more.
pp.127-140 print revenue and Transfers In ONLY -- zero Transfers Out rows across
pp.131-140. Every one of those keys is "present on only one side" with a large
non-zero sum, so the check fails at ~$254M of expenditure before it reaches any
revenue.

FIX: restrict to kind IN {revenue, transfer_in}, as a NAMED CONSTANT carrying
the reason. The restriction is not cosmetic -- see defect 2.

DEFECT 2 -- THE OBVIOUS WAY TO WRITE THE RESTRICTION HIDES A SILENT DROP.

The natural implementation is "iterate the keys the DETAIL scope produces and
compare each to the spine". Do that and omitting a whole revenue block becomes
invisible: drop p128's Licenses & Permits rules entirely, the key (revenue,
licenses-and-permits, general) never appears on the detail side, nothing is
compared, and $7,252,799 of General Fund revenue sits unreconciled with every
check green. That is verbatim the converse failure coverage.go:10-23 records --
the mistyped all-funds-gross-detail that took half the city's revenue out of the
chart.

FIX: iterate the UNION of keys within the kind restriction. A spine key inside
the restriction with NO detail counterpart is a FAILURE, never a skip. Add
TestDroppingARevenueCategoryFromTheDetailFails, mutating the RULE FILE rather
than the fact slice -- the point is that a missing rule is caught, and a fact-
slice mutation would not exercise that path.

DEFECT 3 -- "one of the ten spine slugs" IS ELEVEN.

p139 prints an `Oth Financing Source` row (Police Donations) which needs
`other-financing-sources` -- data/taxonomy.yaml:266-285, marked derived: true
with a source_note that is explicitly UNGROUNDED ("which of the ten p66
categories absorbs this line ... is not printed anywhere"). It is zero in both
budget years so the tie survives, but the rule author WILL write a category
outside the ten, and acceptance test C's "ten-category" wording would fail a
correct read. Say eleven, and note the eleventh is the one whose grounding the
taxonomy itself doubts.

DEFECT 4 -- "81 printed Total rows become total_row assertions" IS NOT
ACHIEVABLE FOR ALL 81, and the cheap workaround is dangerous.

Part.Page is a single int and CheckTotals(rule, p) sums one part over one page
(internal/mapping/resolve.go:746-760). Six blocks STRADDLE a page break, so
their rows are in two parts and their printed total in only one: Other Taxes
(p127->128), Contributions Outsourced (p129->130), State - Gas Tax (p133->134),
City Street Sweeping Fee (p137->138), Open Space Acquisition & Mgmt (p138->139),
General Liability (p139->140). For each, the part carrying the total sums only
the tail and CheckTotals FAILS; the other returns ErrNoStatedTotals.

Worse, p140's `Total Sources` is not assertable at all: printed
201,271,189 / 219,927,720 / 219,633,968 / 216,596,302 against a sum of every
fund total on pp.131-140 of 142,497,640 / 161,091,271 / 163,141,134 /
159,222,794 -- short by a DIFFERENT amount per column ($56.5M in FY2025-26), and
the figure appears nowhere else in the corpus.

THE HAZARD: the author's cheapest escape is a stated_total_deltas entry equal to
the head page's sum -- a FABRICATED declaration of "the city's rounding"
absorbing a structural gap. fisc-2sd catches a STALE declaration (one that now
ties exactly) but has no way to catch a FICTIONAL one. Either budget rule-level
multi-part CheckTotals into fisc-5gk.1, or declare the ~7 unassertable totals
per part and route them through the existing ErrNoStatedTotals reporting channel
(pkg/cmd/build/report.go:100,118), which is checkable. Do not put the gap in a
commit message. Corrected figure: ~74 assertable, not 81.

DEFECT 5 -- THE stated_total_deltas COUNT. The plan and this bead inherited
fisc-2sd's page list. Measured block by block, pp.127-140 have SEVEN discrepant
blocks, not the five the page list implies: p127 Total Property Taxes -1; p128
Total Other Taxes -1; p128 Total Licenses & Permits +2; p129 Total Use of Money
And Property -1; p130 Total Miscellaneous Revenue +1; p131 Total Airport -1;
p135 Total Low Income Housing Fund -1. All in FY2023-24 Actual, all |d| <= $2.
Note p128 has TWO and the inherited list counts pages, not blocks; p130 is
missing from it entirely.

STILL UNDECIDED AND OWED BY THIS BEAD'S DEPENDENTS: fisc-5gk.3.1 lists "the
scope axis, the same question as fisc-u2v but for transfers" as its blocker on
THIS bead, and the decision above covers pp.127-140 only. p76 has no scope. That
is filed separately rather than stretched into this note.
2026-08-22 CORRECTION TO ACCEPTANCE TEST D, required by fisc-aes and now also
by fisc-brx. The decision above stands unchanged; one acceptance test as
written collides with two later decisions and would fail a correct corpus.

TEST D READ: "A test asserting unprojectedScopes holds exactly THE ONE ENTRY,
and that a scope which becomes projected trips the stale-declaration branch."

IT NOW READS: "A test asserting unprojectedScopes holds EXACTLY THE ENTRIES
DECLARED -- one per mapped non-spine schedule, each with a non-empty reason --
and that a scope which becomes projected trips the stale-declaration branch."

WHY. Section (4) of the decision above is correct that revenue-by-fund forces
exactly one entry; it is the count of entries IN THE MAP that was over-specified.
On 2026-08-22 two more scopes were decided, each forced by the same argument
and each needing its own entry:

  revenue-by-fund             pp.127-140  fisc-u2v  (this bead)      924 facts
  transfers-by-fund           p76         fisc-aes                    88 facts
  expenditure-by-department   pp.167-170  fisc-brx                   196 facts

fisc-5gk.2's schedule is the third; fisc-aes's description anticipated the
collision with fisc-5gk.3.1's and fisc-5gk.2's and it has now arrived from both
directions. A test pinning the literal count would go red the moment the second
schedule lands, and the cheapest way to make it green again is to delete the
assertion -- which retires the only test that reads the map at all.

WHAT THE REWORDED TEST STILL HAS TO ASSERT, so the relaxation does not cost the
property the original was protecting: every entry has a NON-EMPTY reason (a
bare `"scope": ""` is a hole with a name), no two entries share a reason string
(copy-paste is how a declaration stops describing its own schedule), and every
declared scope is one that some rule actually writes -- the stale-declaration
branch this bead already specifies covers the converse, a scope that has become
projected. The invariant is "the map is a list of DECIDED exemptions", not "the
map has one row".

Nothing else in the decision or in the five defect notes changes.
2026-08-23 CORRECTION TO SECTION (3)'S DECLARED EXCEPTION, required by deciding
fisc-aes and fisc-brx together. The decision above stands; the exception needs a
condition it does not currently carry.

SECTION (3) READS: "Exactly ONE declared exception, in Go, with its reason:
(transfer_in, transfers/in, general), for the missing GF Transfers In row."

IT NOW READS: the same exception, PLUS the name of the scope that covers the key
instead -- `transfers-by-fund` (fisc-aes) -- and revenue-detail-ties-to-spine
FAILS if that scope carries no fact on that key.

WHY. p76 prints the General Fund Transfers In row pp.127-130 omit: 480,400 /
486,735, which is p0066.txt:24 to the cent. So the key is not unreconciled, it is
reconciled BY ANOTHER SCOPE, and fisc-aes's transfers-detail-ties-to-spine has
zero exceptions on the IN side. Left unconditional, the exemption survives
fisc-5gk.3.1 being deferred or dropped, and 480,400 of General Fund transfers in
becomes a cell no check reconciles -- the same key fisc-aes names as where a
doubled General Fund leg would land.

VERIFIED, and it also confirms this note's own six-group table from a second
direction: pp.131-140's Transfers In rows sum by destination group to enterprise
13,247,000, debt-service 6,984,597, special-revenue 814,000, so 21,045,597 of
p76's 21,525,997 FY2026 total is decomposed TWICE by two printed schedules and
the two agree to the cent. No scope-to-scope check is owed -- transitivity
through the spine already gives it, and a second statement of the same claim is
a second place for it to drift.

The general rule, recorded on fisc-aes and fisc-brx: any exception declared by a
detail-ties-to-spine check names the scope that covers the key, and fails if that
scope has no fact there; if no scope covers it, the exception must say in words
that the cell is unreconciled. The corpus-wide exception budget across the three
scopes is therefore ZERO, not one.

Nothing else in the decision or in the six earlier correction notes changes.
2026-08-24 CORRECTION TO DEFECT 5, plus two count corrections and one reading of
this bead's own text that a landing plan got wrong. The decision stands; three of
its measurements do not. Recorded here rather than fixed silently at
implementation time, because DEFECT 5 in particular is a table an implementer
would copy verbatim into YAML.

(1) ALL SEVEN stated_total_deltas SIGNS IN DEFECT 5 ARE INVERTED.

DEFECT 5 READS: "p127 Total Property Taxes -1; p128 Total Other Taxes -1; p128
Total Licenses & Permits +2; p129 Total Use of Money And Property -1; p130 Total
Miscellaneous Revenue +1; p131 Total Airport -1; p135 Total Low Income Housing
Fund -1."

StatedTotalDelta.Cents is STATED MINUS MAPPED (internal/mapping/rule.go:385-393),
and fisc-2sd's close note fixes the convention with the one worked example:
p127's thirteen rows sum to 58,179,467 against a printed 58,179,468, "so it
declares 100". Measured block by block across all fourteen pages -- summing the
rows and subtracting from the printed total, every column:

  block                                    delta_cents
  p127 Total Property Taxes                      +100
  p128 Total Other Taxes                         +100
  p128 Total Licenses & Permits                  -200
  p129 Total Use of Money And Property           +100
  p130 Total Miscellaneous Revenue               -100
  p131 Total Airport                             +100
  p135 Total Low Income Housing Fund             +100

Every one is the negation of what DEFECT 5 records. The SET is right, DEFECT 5's
two structural observations are right (p128 carries TWO discrepant blocks, and
p130 is missing from fisc-2sd's inherited page list because that list counts
pages and not blocks), and all seven are FY2023-24 Actual with the other three
columns tying exactly. Only the signs were wrong. A YAML author copying the table
would have had every one of the seven rejected by CheckTotals with the correct
figure printed in the failure message -- loud rather than silent, which is why
this is a correction and not an incident.

The same sweep confirms what the rest of the schedule does: of the 81 printed
Total rows on pp.127-140, the other 72 tie EXACTLY in all four columns.

(2) THE ROW AND FACT COUNTS ARE RIGHT; THE TOTAL-ROW COUNT AND DEFECT 4's
ASSERTABLE COUNT ARE NOT.

231 data rows confirmed (92 on pp.127-130, 139 on pp.131-140), so 924 facts
confirmed. But "The other 81 printed rows are `Total <category>` / `Total <fund>`
lines" double-counts: there are 81 printed Total rows ALTOGETHER, of which 79 are
rule-level totals (10 category totals on pp.127-130, 69 fund totals on
pp.131-140) and 2 are cross-rule ROLLUPS -- Total General Fund (p0130.txt:40) and
Total Sources (p0140.txt:52).

DEFECT 4's "~74 assertable, not 81" is now stale in the other direction, because
fisc-w0o landed rule-level multi-part CheckTotals. The count is 80 OF 81: all 79
rule totals, plus the p130 rollup, and only p140's Total Sources unassertable
(fisc-wev, settled 2026-08-24 -- see also that bead for a second, independent
reason the rollup channel is the only one available here).

DEFECT 4's straddle list is also over-counted. It names six blocks; only FOUR
have rows on two pages -- Other Taxes (p127->128), State - Gas Tax (p133->134),
Open Space Acquisition & Mgmt (p138->139), General Liability (p139->140). The
other two are different shapes and need different rules:

  - Contributions Outsourced: its heading and its ONE row are both on p129; only
    the printed total is on p130 (p0130.txt:8, immediately after that page's
    column header). It needs total_spans_parts with a bearer part that maps ZERO
    active rows -- a path nothing in the tree exercises today.
  - City Street Sweeping Fee: its heading is on p137 but its rows AND its printed
    total are both on p138 (p0138.txt:12). It is an ORDINARY single-part p138
    rule, and its section anchor cannot be its own heading.

So five rules need total_spans_parts, not six.

(3) "THE ~40 EMPTY CELLS" IS 62, AND THE COUNT MATTERS BECAUSE IT IS LOAD-BEARING.

Section (3) says "A key present on only one side must sum to ZERO, which disposes
of the ~40 empty cells". Measured against the committed spine facts, keyed on
{kind, category, fund_group} for FY2026 and FY2027 adopted inside the
{revenue, transfer_in} restriction: ZERO value differences, and 62 one-sided keys
-- 58 spine-only keys publishing a zero fact, 2 spine-only keys publishing real
money (the declared exception, at FY2026 480,400 and FY2027 486,735), and 4
detail-only keys, all zero: (revenue, other-financing-sources, special-revenue)
in both years and (transfer_in, transfers/in, permanent) in both years.

The number is worth correcting because a landing plan reached the opposite
conclusion from it. Reading DEFECT 2's "iterate the UNION of keys" together with
"~40", one plan proposed testing PRESENCE BEFORE VALUE so a zero-vs-absent cell
would be reported. Do not: that turns all 62 into findings, including the
permanent-funds cell fisc-u8o exists to tolerate and the eleventh category, which
has no spine counterpart in any year. Section (3)'s own sentence is the
instruction -- compare values first, and a one-sided key ties at zero. If the
asymmetry is worth surfacing it belongs in the check's SUMMARY as a count, which
is where the landed expenditure check puts its unreconciled pairs.

(4) THE DECLARED EXCEPTION IS TWO KEYS, AND THE 2026-08-23 CORRECTION IS NOT
BLOCKING.

The exception is (transfer_in, transfers/in, general) in BOTH reconciled years --
FY2026 480,400 and FY2027 486,735 -- not one key.

And the same plan read the 2026-08-23 correction as making revenue-detail-ties-
to-spine unlandable before fisc-5gk.3.1: "FAILS if that scope carries no fact on
that key" was taken to mean fisc verify is red until p76 lands. That reads only
the first branch. The correction's own closing sentence gives the second: "if no
scope covers it, the exception must say in words that the cell is unreconciled."
No scope covers it today, so the compliant declaration today is the words, naming
transfers-by-fund (fisc-aes / fisc-5gk.3.1) as what tightens it into a
cross-scope assertion when it lands. Nothing about this bead blocks on that one.

Worth strengthening while writing it, and checkable today: the exception should
also assert the DETAIL side is absent on that key. Left as a bare exemption it
would silently excuse a detail-side General Fund transfers-in fact, which is the
half of the hole the unconditional form leaves open.

Nothing else in the decision or in the four earlier correction notes changes. The
six-fund-group measurement was re-derived a THIRD time for this note, by summing
the 69 printed fund totals by fund group against p0063.txt:16-21's Table 2:
FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 tie exactly in all six groups. See fisc-wev for the two
FY2024-25 discrepancies (fisc-zl9, fisc-94b), neither of which touches a column
this bead's check reconciles.

Decided and now landed with fisc-5gk.1 (13751ff). All four points this bead asked

straddles is four, because Contributions Outsourced and City Street Sweeping Fee

Also recorded there: the exception is two keys and not one, and the 2026-08-23

title: Structural remainder: cell relocation and dropped-column detection
description:
fisc-1wr.5 lands in two pieces. The parent's artifact/registry drift and the cross-language Normalize agreement are implementable at spine-only coverage and land in Wave A. These two want a settled resolver, so they land after the geometry column guard (fisc-yqv.2) and the coverage lanes.

CELL RELOCATION -- independently re-resolve each fact by its identity tuple (doc_id, rule_id, row_path, row_label, column_path, fiscal_year, basis) and assert the resolved position equals the recorded one. This is the check that replaced a tautological earlier draft: hashing a fact's token and then asserting the token matches can never fail. Asking the RULES where that cell is TODAY is a question the committed file cannot answer for itself. Two outcomes worth distinguishing: an id absent from the re-resolved index means the cell this fact names no longer exists; an id present at a different page/offset/token means the table moved, and the finding names both positions.

Reuses the resolver memoization from fisc-uv6, so verify still resolves each part once rather than a third time.

DROPPED COLUMN -- if a page's text carries a longer numeric run on a mapped row's label line than the table has columns, fail with 'possible dropped column'. ACFR p34 loses one silently. Note this overlaps with fisc-yqv.2's column_headers, which catches a dropped column at resolve time; this catches it over already-built facts, which is the case where the rules were not re-run.
acceptance_criteria: a fact whose row moved is reported with both positions and is distinguishable from a fact whose cell no longer exists; the relocation pass adds no additional resolve of any part; ACFR p34's shape is a test case
notes:
2026-08-18 NOTE from fisc-yqv.2. This bead's dropped-column half cites ACFR p34
as the page that loses a column silently, and says the overlap with
fisc-yqv.2's column_headers is that the resolver catches it at resolve time
while this catches it over already-built facts.

Measured: ACFR p34 is one of the 124 pages where the -layout line structure and
the geometry clustering disagree, so the resolver's column guard can NEVER run
there. It refuses the page rather than catching the drop. The overlap is smaller
than it looks and this bead is the only thing that would catch ACFR p34's shape.
See fisc-gmx.
2026-08-18 DEFERRED, landing plan -- but revisit immediately after fisc-5gk.2. Cell relocation is worth little over 240 facts from 2 pages; after both coverage lanes land there are roughly 1,580 facts across 18 more pages, which is when 'independently re-resolve each fact and assert the position matches' starts earning its keep. This bead's own note calls it the only thing that would catch ACFR p34's shape.

title: Re-anchor the spine: 7 anchor edits across 5 of 10 parts
description:
The claim that -layout lets the section_ordinal/stop_at workarounds go is WRONG. section_ordinal: 4 is still needed (still four occurrences of 'FY 2026-27'); stop_at: '$' is still needed (p67 still prints no TOTAL REVENUES: label); and 'line anchors' describes a resolver feature that does not exist -- anchor is a raw strings.Index (resolve.go:206) and nothing in internal/mapping is line-aware.

What breaks, all fail-closed, 5 of 10 parts:
1. MULTI-SPACE HEADER ANCHORS (3 parts: spine-expenditures p67, spine-transfers-out p67, spine-fund-balance p67). -layout prints 'Capital Funds' + 15 spaces + 'Debt Service Funds'; the single-spaced section string no longer occurs. Re-anchor to section: 'Internal Service Funds', section_ordinal: 2.
2. PAGE FOOTERS (4 parts). xberg's strip_repeating_text deleted them; -layout emits 'BUDGET FY 2025-27      Page 62'. Every part with no stop_at now swallows it. The footer carries a bare '62' which amount.Parse accepts as $62, so this is corpus-wide: every 'runs to end of page' part needs an explicit stop_at.

The mapping file's ~80-line prose preamble describes the xberg single-line shape throughout and needs rewriting, not patching.
acceptance_criteria: 240 facts, 24 columns tied, every amount_cents identical to the pre-migration values
notes: DONE (working tree, uncommitted). 7 anchor edits across 5 of 10 parts, exactly as the bead predicted. (1) spine-expenditures p67, (2) spine-transfers-out p67, (3) spine-fund-balance p67: section 'Capital Funds Debt Service Funds Special Revenue Funds Internal Service Funds' -> 'Internal Service Funds\n', section_ordinal 2 unchanged. The bead's suggested fix was right but incomplete: the trailing newline matters, because it turns 'the last name on the header line' from a hope into a claim -- without it a fifth fund group would resolve to a start mid-header, with it the anchor disappears and fails closed. (4) spine-transfers-out p66, (5) spine-transfers-out p67, (6) spine-fund-balance p66, (7) spine-fund-balance p67: added stop_at 'BUDGET FY 2025-27'. section_ordinal 4 and stop_at '$' both re-verified as still required: p67 prints 'FY 2026-27' exactly 4 times and 'TOTAL REVENUES:' zero times. ~80-line preamble rewritten, not patched. PROOF: 240 facts / 240 distinct ids / sum(amount_cents)=255588874000, id sequence and every amount_cents byte-identical to HEAD baseline; only offset (all 240) and token (10, all '\\-' -> '-' zero cells on p67 capital FY2027) differ. 4 of 10 parts tie, 24 columns, parts_unchecked unchanged at the 6 no-total_row parts. All 240 offsets land on their token in the new page file and every token is a whole whitespace-delimited page token (no fragments). All five control totals re-derive by hand from the new page text. fisc export reproduces sankey.golden.json byte for byte apart from metadata.generated_by. go test ./... green, golangci-lint 0 issues, gofmt clean. Also corrected now-false prose in internal/mapping/rule.go (SectionOrdinal doc claimed the schedule is on one line of extracted text), testdata/README.md and docs/agents/conventions.md. Cannot bd close: blocked by open fisc-yqv.3.

Three p67 parts moved off a spelled-out header string (-layout spaces it 14/15/9 on one half and 15/14/9 on the other) to section: 'Internal Service Funds\n' + ordinal 2.
