title: Rewrite tools/extract.py on poppler; re-extract all three docs
description:
poppler-utils replaces xberg in requirements.txt.

KEEP (load-bearing): sorted output, canonical JSON, atomic writes, clean_output of stale files before writing, and the rule that Python never reads data/sources.yaml (two parties recording the sha256 independently is a real check).

DROP (xberg shape): xberg_version, config, config_sha256, table_count, pages_with_tables, NORMALIZER_VERSION.

NEW ANSWER NEEDED: poppler has no structured error channel. It writes 'Syntax Warning: Bad annotation destination' to stderr and exits 0. Record the poppler version and captured stderr per document; do not claim manifest.errors works as before.

PUBLISH PAGE TEXT AS .txt NOT .md: GitHub renders .md in the blob view and collapses the runs of spaces that ARE the grid, which would silently break the provenance deep links fisc-gxa.5 depends on. Carry the rename through corpus.go:217, export/page.go:311, site/app.js:282, export_test.go:197, and the now-false comments at corpus.go:219 and rule.go:30.
close_reason: extract.py rewritten on poppler 24.02.0, stdlib only. All 786 pages re-extracted; byte-identical across runs, locales, and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH/PYTHONHASHSEED. Determinism verified by a third party on an independent re-run. schema_version bumped to 2 on both sides after review found that leaving it at 1 made a broken reader SILENT: Open() succeeded, then Page(n) returned ErrNotFound, which corpus.go documents as the normal 'no such page' case. Bumping it surfaced a real latent bug -- corpus.SchemaVersion was validating both the manifest and each table JSON, two independent contracts sharing one constant. poppler has no structured error channel; stderr is captured per invocation and the docstring says plainly that an empty errors list is not a promise every page came out whole.

title: Column-position guard in the resolver
description:
With geometry available, a value must fall within its column's x-range, derived from the header line. This is the actual payoff of the extractor switch: adopting a layout-preserving extractor and then reading it with a whitespace tokenizer (tokens(), resolve.go:744, which records byte offset only and no column position) throws away the reason for switching.

Without this guard the sparse pages produce plausible wrong values rather than errors.
acceptance_criteria: a row whose 2nd column is blank and 3rd carries a figure resolves the figure to column 3 or fails closed -- never silently to column 2; CIP p40 PB200654 fails closed naming the row
notes:
2026-08-18 ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA AMENDED. The original read, verbatim:

  "a row whose 2nd column is blank and 3rd carries a figure resolves the figure
  to column 3 or fails closed -- never silently to column 2; CIP p40 PB200654
  reads correctly"

The last clause is unmeetable and this bead's own notes already said why: six of
PB200654's eight cells print a "-" that is in NO substrate, because they are
drawn as non-text. No column guard recovers a mark the PDF never wrote. Closing
on "reads correctly" would have published a false claim, so the clause moved to
fisc-8ln (whose AC lost its "or fails closed" escape in the same edit, or the
obligation would have belonged to no open bead).

The first clause is met in its fails-closed branch, which is the only branch this
lane can demonstrate: geometry is a pure CROSS-CHECK here and never selects which
tokens a row consumes, so a blank cell yields a refusal rather than a correctly
placed figure. "Resolves the figure to column 3" needs band-driven selection,
which is filed with the sparse relaxation.

WHAT LANDED, in six commits: internal/geom (leaf, stdlib only); corpus.Doc.Geometry;
the doc interface at three methods; the verbatim-copy fixture tables generalised
to {document, artifact} over both substrates; column_headers on Part with per-part,
per-page and cross-file validation; the guard itself in internal/mapping/geometry.go;
and column_headers on all ten published spine parts.

DEVIATIONS FROM THE DESIGN ON THIS BEAD, each with its evidence:

(1) The count guard was NOT relaxed. The design said geometry "NECESSARILY
relaxes" positionalValues' exact len(toks) == ExpectedValues. That is true of
SPARSE pages and no mapped part is sparse: p66's data lines carry four value
words each and p67's carry eight, on all 24 of them, dashes included. Relaxing
would have traded the guard that caught fisc-c00 for a replacement exercised only
by the dense pages that never needed it.

(2) The gutter is the FIRST COLUMN HEADER'S x0, not the midpoint to the label
header. The design's own counterexamples refute the design: CIP p40's wrap word
"and" ends at 228.6 and CIP p29's "REVITILIZATION" at 234.85, both RIGHT of the
midpoints (213.16 and 218.67), so both would have filed into band 0. First-header-x0
(238.87 and 245.10) excludes them and keeps every real value, including the bare
leading "$" glyphs. Clearances are thin on CIP and are recorded in the code:
9.46pt left and 3.81pt right on p40.

(3) No column_headers_ordinal. The full ordered header sequence occurs exactly
once page-wide on 66, 67, 127, 128-140, 167, 168, 169, 170, CIP 40 and CIP 29 --
with zero unconsumed words right of the first match on every one. Shipping five
validation branches and a selection branch that no fixture can reach, inside the
guard everything else is about to trust, was the worse trade. Ambiguity is a
refusal naming the candidate lines. Filed for when a page forces it.

(4) No geom.ErrNoGeometry sentinel. corpus.ErrNotFound already means "the
manifest does not list this artifact", and a second sentinel would have put the
artifact reader's vocabulary in the leaf that exists so mapping need not import it.

(5) Substrate agreement is BYTE equality, not the design's "normalized text".
Normalizing would paper over a genuine disagreement, and the point of a second
witness is that it is allowed to disagree.

MEASUREMENTS THE DESIGN GOT WRONG, corrected here:

- Filing by header overlap misfiles 19-30 "on the mapped pages" -- it misfiles
  ZERO on pp.66/67. Over the eight measured pages the two rules disagree on 24
  tokens: 19 zero dashes (p127, p167, p168, p169, CIP p40), 2 bare "$" glyphs and
  3 footer tokens. The doc comment and TestOverlapFilingLosesZeroDashes carry the
  corrected figure.
- The line-grouping 1:1 with -layout is NOT a corpus property. It fails on 124 of
  786 pages, and 99 more fail token agreement. No page in current or near-term
  scope fails either, and the guard refuses the rest rather than reading them
  approximately. Do not write a corpus-wide assertion of it; it is false.
- p67 has 33 non-blank lines but 24 DATA lines.

fisc-j5p's hypothesis was disproved and is recorded on that bead.
close_reason:
The column guard is live over the published citywide spine, and all 240 facts and
facts/facts.jsonl are byte-identical with it on -- what changed is what is
checked, not what is published.

Six commits: internal/geom (leaf, stdlib only, the -bbox reader and the band
model); corpus.Doc.Geometry; the mapping doc interface at three methods, with the
argument for a required method over a type assertion written down; both
verbatim-copy fixture tests generalised to {document, artifact} tables over both
substrates; column_headers on Part with per-part, per-page and cross-file
validation; the guard in internal/mapping/geometry.go; column_headers on all ten
published spine parts; and the CIP p29/p40 tests.

Evidence: spineFacts 240 and spineTiedColumns 24 with the guard on, every balance
identity and headline figure unmoved, facts.jsonl and sankey.golden.json
byte-identical, fisc verify 19 passed 0 failed.

The guard is not inert, and that is asserted rather than hoped: a rule that names
only the last three of p66's four printed headers is refused naming the row, the
token, its x-position and the column the page actually prints it in; a header pair
in the wrong order is refused as an order claim; a part one column short of the
page is refused because the header line carries a header no column claims; and a
one-column part whose two rows were fused onto one printed line is caught by the
line count, which is the case no other check can see.

AC amended and the original preserved in the notes above, along with the five
deviations from the design and the three measurements on this bead that turned
out to be wrong. Follow-ups filed: fisc-gmx (substrate disagreement, 223 of 786
pages), band-driven selection with the sparse count relaxation, StatedTotals'
substrate inconsistency, column_headers_ordinal, and the two-grid page.

title: Emit both -layout text and -bbox geometry
description:
pdftotext -layout alone CANNOT distinguish an empty cell from an absent one: on a sparse wide grid a blank cell yields no token at all. CIP p40 row PB200654 prints two figures with six blanks between and -layout gives exactly two tokens. labelledValues takes toks[:ncols] (resolve.go:378), so a figure silently lands in the wrong column -- a plausible wrong value, which is what this project fails closed on, and it makes 'absent is not zero' unenforceable. xberg's tables/*.json grid was the only artifact carrying that geometry, and pp.131-140 / pp.167-170 (the Stage 2 targets) are the sparse ones.

-bbox is also the only way to keep one existing claim reproducible: the mapping file justifies its corrected omitted_rows: [] on p67 with 'pdftotext -bbox puts ten revenue rows here at the same ten y-positions' -- the fisc-c00 evidence.

Emit pages/pNNNN.txt (-layout) plus geometry/pNNNN.json (word boxes from -bbox). Strictly more useful than xberg's tables; replaces them rather than sitting beside them.
acceptance_criteria: geometry/pNNNN.json carries per-word text + bbox for every page of all three docs; a sparse-grid page (CIP p40) can be read column-correctly using it
notes: 2026-08-18 CORRECTION, from peer review of the landing plan. This bead's premise that pp.131-140 and pp.167-170 'are the sparse ones' is measurably FALSE. All 18 pages in that scope were checked against the emitted -bbox geometry: every data row carries exactly 4 value tokens, with '-' printed in every zero cell. They are uniformly dense. The -bbox substrate and the column guard built on it (fisc-yqv.2) are therefore not justified by any page currently in scope -- the poppler migration itself (fisc-yqv.3) IS, and demonstrably worked (p130 recovered 13 rows xberg lost). Recording the distinction so the guard's cost is not retro-justified by the extractor's success.
close_reason: Emits pages/pNNNN.txt (-layout) + geometry/pNNNN.json (-bbox word boxes), replacing tables/. Geometry verified sufficient for column identity: CIP p40 PB202617's lone 500,000 at x=391.1 sits under FY 2026-27 (369.9-418.9), where a whitespace read would have filed it under FY 2024-25. Word encoding flattened to [x0,y0,x1,y1,text] after review: 18.7 -> 8.2 MiB, 41.3 bytes/word. Geometry does NOT recover a value absent from the text layer -- see fisc-8ln.

title: [epic] E0 Extraction replacement: pdftotext replaces xberg
description:
The committed xberg artifacts have silently lost data rows on exactly the pages the POC needs: PDF p167 prints a ~40-line department x object grid and pages/p0167.md retains 7; p130 prints 13 Miscellaneous Revenue detail rows and p0130.md retains 0. This is the fisc-c00 failure class, and Part.OmittedRows' doc comment forbids absorbing it in a rule -- if rows go missing between the PDF and the artifact, fix extraction.

A scratch migration replacing all 786 pages with pdftotext -layout output confirmed: all 240 spine facts reproduce with identical amount_cents AND identical ids, sankey.json matches the golden except its build stamp, all 24 columns still tie, every headline control total re-derives, output is byte-identical across runs and locales. Of 583 grouped-value tokens xberg produced that -layout does not, every one is an xberg corruption (dash-glued negatives, split digits, a lost decimal).

Ends with all three docs re-extracted, the spine re-anchored, and the money proven identical cell by cell.
close_reason: E0 complete, 6/6. pdftotext -layout plus -bbox geometry replaced xberg across all three documents; the spine was re-anchored (7 edits across 5 of 10 parts); the table substrate and markdown residue are gone. Verified in peer review of the landing plan that the rewrite did what it was for: p130's 13 Miscellaneous Revenue rows, of which xberg retained 0, are all present in the poppler artifact. One correction recorded on fisc-yqv.1: its premise that pp.131-140 and 167-170 'are the sparse ones' is measurably false -- all 18 pages carry exactly 4 value tokens per row.

title: StatedTotals cannot read a totals row glued to the next data row
description:
Budget Book p67's expenditure totals cannot be read. The extracted page puts the TOTAL EXPENDITURES row and the TRANSFER OUT row on ONE physical line:

  ... 1,070,500 1,115,510 $1,061,355 $969,934 $6,984,597 $6,969,898 $19,267,561 $11,808,000 $25,077,367 $26,544,515 28,584,740 36,047,736 - - 1,137,050 900,550 40,000 612,000

StatedTotals anchors a label-less part on stop_at ('$') and asks amountRun for the first MAXIMAL run of exactly len(columns) parsable amounts within that line. Sixteen amounts follow the anchor -- the 8 totals plus the 8 transfer-out figures -- so the maximal run is 16, never 8, and the read fails with ErrNotFound.

That is indistinguishable from 'the totals row moved', which is a genuine hard failure, so it cannot be waved through. p67's revenue totals (line 15) and total-sources (line 17) each have exactly 8 amounts after their anchor, which is why only this one part fails.

The document already distinguishes the two rows typographically: totals rows are $-prefixed and data rows are bare. internal/mapping/testdata/spine.yaml relies on that convention already ('the totals row is the first line whose figures are prefixed with $ -- every data row above it is bare'). The resolver does not use it.
design:
In amountRun, when a maximal run is not the wanted length AND the run begins with a $-prefixed token, also consider that run's $-prefixed PREFIX. Return it if it is exactly the wanted length.

Deliberately additive: the existing maximal-run result is computed first and preferred, so a line the resolver reads today reads identically. The new branch can only turn a failure into a success. That rules out a regression on the pages where totals are only partially $-marked, which fail closed as before.
acceptance_criteria: p67's spine-expenditures part ties its 8 column totals; p66's labelled totals and p67's revenue totals are unchanged; a line whose $-prefixed prefix is the wrong width still fails.
close_reason: Fixed: amountRun considers a run's $-prefixed prefix when the maximal run is the wrong width. Deliberately additive -- the maximal run is computed and preferred first, so every line that read before reads identically and the new branch can only turn a failure into a success. p67 spine-expenditures now ties its 8 columns; the spine ties 24 of 24. Regression test TestCurrencyMarkedTotalsRunSurvivesAGluedDataRow covers the glued line, a wrong-width $-prefix, and an unchanged bare run.

title: Extraction dropped a data row: xberg strip_repeating_text eats identical rows
description:
Budget Book PDF p67 prints TEN revenue rows; data/extracted/.../pages/p0067.md carried only NINE (72 tokens where 10 rows x 8 columns = 80). Verified with 'pdftotext -bbox -f 67 -l 67': p67's revenue rows sit at y = 194, 210, 226, 241, 257, 273, 289, 304, 320, 336 -- the SAME ten y-positions as p66's ten labelled rows. The document omits nothing.

Rows 8-10 (Sales Taxes, Fines & Forfeitures, Licenses & Permits) are three consecutive all-dash lines. xberg's content_filter.strip_repeating_text defaults to true; it is a header/footer dedup heuristic and it treated the third identical DATA row as repeating boilerplate. Setting content_filter.strip_repeating_text=false restores all three (80 tokens, verified).

This matters far beyond one row. The project had recorded the loss as a property of the DOCUMENT -- docs/m0-spike.md finding #4, the omitted_rows comment in internal/mapping/testdata/spine.yaml, the OmittedRows doc comment in internal/mapping/rule.go, and fisc-mq4.7's own description all say p67 'omits' an all-zero row. It does not. Declaring it via Part.OmittedRows ('rows absent from THIS part') would launder a pipeline defect into a permanent published assertion about the City's budget, and row_label is inside fact.MakeID, so the affected facts would carry a coin-flip label.

The resolver's positional count guard (internal/mapping/resolve.go positionalValues) was CORRECTLY firing. It is the only reason this was caught.
design: Add content_filter: {strip_repeating_text: false} to CONFIG in tools/extract.py and bump EXTRACTOR_VERSION. CONFIG is hashed into manifest.config_sha256, so the change is attributable. Review the full-corpus artifact diff before committing: strip_repeating_text is a global heuristic and any other page it was silently editing will also change. include_headers/include_footers stay false and are separate knobs.
acceptance_criteria: p0067.md revenue block tokenizes to 80 between the 4th 'FY 2026-27' and the first '$'; omitted_rows disappears from the spine rule entirely; the four places that record the false premise are corrected; artifact diff outside the affected pages is reviewed and explained.
close_reason: Fixed in 6806ec7: content_filter.strip_repeating_text=False, EXTRACTOR_VERSION=2, corpus regenerated. p67 revenue block is 80 tokens (10 rows x 8). Zero numeric tokens lost corpus-wide; 326 pages gained restored content. Four records of the false premise corrected (m0-spike.md, testdata/spine.yaml, rule.go OmittedRows doc, testdata/README.md) plus this bead's parent fisc-mq4.7. Regression guard: TestExtractionDropOutIsNotAnOmission.

title: Rebuild-and-diff facts.jsonl in CI
description: CI runs 'fisc build -o $(mktemp -d)' and byte-compares the result against the committed facts.jsonl. Without this, a hand-edited facts.jsonl passes CI and the deployed site is built from different numbers than the audit trail -- the one thing a provenance gate must prevent. Pure Go, so it costs nothing and preserves the no-LFS-in-CI property.
notes: 2026-08-17 IMPLEMENTATION DEVIATION, deliberate: the description says 'fisc build -o $(mktemp -d)', which the tool refuses by design -- --output is resolved against the repository root and validateRepoPath (pkg/cmd/build/build.go:130) rejects absolute paths. The CI job builds to bin/facts-rebuilt.jsonl instead (bin/ is gitignored and make clean already owns it, so the rebuild leaves the tree exactly as checked out) and compares with cmp, not 'git diff --exit-code'. cmp because git diff compares through the .gitattributes 'text eol=lf' clean filter rather than the bytes, and because the git diff form would leave the committed fact store overwritten in the workspace on failure. Recorded so the next reader does not 'fix' it back toward the description.
close_reason: The facts job rebuilds to bin/facts-rebuilt.jsonl and byte-compares with cmp against the committed facts/facts.jsonl. Deviation from the description's literal 'fisc build -o $(mktemp -d)' recorded in the notes -- the tool refuses absolute output paths by design.

title: Structural checks: drift, cell relocation, dropped column
description:
- artifact drift: any data/extracted file whose sha256 differs from its manifest entry; any manifest whose source_sha256 differs from the registry; any manifest whose xberg_version differs from the pin
- registry drift (--full only): recomputed PDF sha256 vs sources.yaml
- CELL RELOCATION: independently re-resolve each fact by row_path + column_path and assert the resolved position equals the recorded one. This REPLACES a check that was tautological in an earlier draft -- hashing content and then asserting the content matched can never fail independently. A mismatch means the table shifted, which is precisely the event nothing else detects.
- dropped-column detection: if a page's text has a longer numeric run on a mapped row's label line than the table has columns, fail with 'possible dropped column' (ACFR p34 loses a column silently)

Default verify needs NO PDFs and NO Python; --full adds registry drift and runs monthly with lfs: true.
notes:
ALSO: cross-language normalizer agreement. internal/amount.Normalize must produce the same output as normalize_cell in tools/extract.py, because the committed artifacts hash normalized text with the Python one and a Go reader that normalized differently would compute different hashes for identical content.

One divergence is known and deliberate: extract.py applies Unicode NFKC, Go does not (that would mean a golang.org/x/text dependency, byob-release.10, for a transform that changes nothing in this corpus -- all 382 committed tables hash identically either way). This check is what catches it if that stops being true. The Go doc comment on Normalize cites this bead.
2026-08-17 THE CROSS-LANGUAGE NORMALIZE CHECK IS MOOT. This bead's note asks for 'cross-language normalizer agreement: internal/amount.Normalize must produce the same output as normalize_cell in tools/extract.py, because the committed artifacts hash normalized text with the Python one.' That premise died with the poppler migration (fisc-yqv.3): normalize_cell no longer exists, and tools/extract.py now writes raw 'pdftotext -layout' bytes plus -bbox geometry with NO cell normalization anywhere. The manifest hashes those raw bytes, so there is no Python normalizer for Go to agree with and nothing for the check to compare. Same staleness class as fisc-9lp.

The underlying worry is still real but has moved: amount.Normalize is now the ONLY normalizer in the pipeline, applied on the Go side at parse time, so a change to it changes what parses without changing any artifact hash. That is a unit-test concern (internal/amount already has TestNormalizeUnifiesDashes) rather than a cross-language one. The deliberate NFKC divergence the note mentions no longer exists either, because the Python side does no NFKC.

Dropped from the A4 lane rather than built. Also dropped: 'any manifest whose xberg_version differs from the pin' -- the field is extractor_version (currently 3) plus poppler_version ('24.02.0'), and both are checked.
2026-08-17 LANE A4 LANDED (uncommitted in the main tree; not closed -- the remainder is fisc-1wr.5.1). Four tier-0 structural checks in internal/check/structural.go, first in All()'s order:

artifacts-match-manifest -- hashes all 1572 files under data/extracted/ against the sha256 and bytes their manifest records, BOTH directions: changed bytes, a listed file that is gone, and a present file the manifest does not list. manifest.json is excluded (it cannot hash itself) and that is documented.
manifest-matches-source-registry -- each manifest's source_sha256/source_bytes/source_file against data/sources.yaml, plus the two document-id sets being the same set (a source with no extraction, an extraction with no source). No PDF: two independently written claims.
extraction-toolchain-pinned -- extractor_version and poppler_version against corpus.PinnedExtractorVersion (3) and PinnedPopplerVersion ('24.02.0'). Mutual agreement between the three docs is NOT separately asserted: each is compared to one constant, so agreement follows and a second finding would be a consequence of the first. schema_version stays gated in corpus.Open (a load failure, not a finding) because at another schema the artifact namespace itself differs.
source-pdfs-match-both-records (Full) -- the FIRST check with Full()==true, so StatusSkipped is now reachable end to end. Recomputes each data/pdf sha256 and compares against BOTH sources.yaml and the manifest. Three states, told apart: wrong bytes = FAIL (a claim about the corpus); an unsmudged Git LFS pointer or an absent file = ERROR naming the file and carrying 'git lfs pull' inline in the message (a claim about the checkout; the hint is inline because ErrHint.Error() drops it and a check's error becomes the report Summary). A pointer's oid is compared to the registry so the report says whether fetching would even reconcile the tree.

WHERE THE PIN LIVES: internal/corpus, beside SchemaVersion, as PinnedExtractorVersion/PinnedPopplerVersion. Not requirements.txt: that file is prose no Go code reads and says in as many words that poppler 'is not pinned the way a pip requirement would be'. requirements.txt now cross-references the Go constants.

New: cmdutil.ExtractedDir (corpus's private const promoted); corpus.ManifestFile, Artifacts() (replacing ArtifactPaths/Artifact), Tree(), SourceFile/SourceBytes/ExtractorVersion/PopplerVersion; registry.LoadSources + Source (strict, schema-gated, the first Go reader of the whole sources.yaml); Subject.Extractions/Sources/SourcePDFs, and Load hashes data/pdf only under Full.

Every check proven failable by mutating a file on disk (internal/check/structural_test.go, 12 mutation tests + the four --full states). Verified by neutering all four checks at once: exactly those 12 tests go red. No test needs Python, the network, or the LFS files -- the --full tests synthesize their own tiny source documents and rewrite the registry and manifests to match.

Default verify still needs no PDFs: 17 pass, 5 vacuous, 1 SKIPPED with its reason, exit 0. --full: 18 pass, exit 0. CI needed no change (confirmed: the default run over a tree with a deleted PDF still exits 0); ci.yml's header note now records that --full exists and that scheduling it is fisc-gxa.5's. Also fixed a grammar bug the lane made reachable: 'N check need --full'.

NOT built, per the scope change already on this bead: cross-language Normalize agreement (moot), cell relocation and dropped-column (fisc-1wr.5.1).
2026-08-17 ROUND 2, after peer review. Blocker and all five must/should-fixes addressed; still uncommitted, still not closed.

BLOCKER (the artifact map was checked for consistency and never for completeness) -- two new tier-0 checks, and fisc-6r5 folded in:

title: Tier 4: coverage ratchet per (fiscal_year, basis, scope)
description:
A committed coverage_floor; verify fails if measured coverage drops below it. THIS IS WHAT LETS THE GATE LAND BEFORE MAPPING FINISHES: green at 10% coverage, regressions still blocked, floor raised as E7 progresses. Without it, 'department sums match fund totals' would be red throughout the longest epic, and a permanently red gate gets commented out.

Same treatment for transfers: a transfer-unmatched residual node under a coverage floor, since budgets often state aggregate transfers-in without matching per-fund transfers-out.
notes:
The coverage ratchet is deferred; it does not block fisc-gxa.1, which shipped. The edge assumed a projection should not exist until coverage could be ratcheted, but the ratchet's purpose is to stop coverage REGRESSING and there was no coverage to regress from.

Its second paragraph did land early, in changed form: the transfer-unmatched residual. Transfers out $59,612,734 against in $21,525,997 because p76 is unmapped, and rather than a residual node the projection publishes headline.transfer_residual_cents -- a synthetic link would have unbalanced whichever transfer node it touched, and splitting the 59.6M into matched and unmatched portions would publish a division the city never printed. It still goes stale-red when p76 lands.
2026-08-18 DEFERRED, landing plan. A coverage ratchet over 2 mapped pages of 786 measures nothing; it becomes meaningful once fisc-5gk.1 and .2 have established a coverage history. title: Tier 2: reconciliation with document-derived tolerance
description:
TIER 2 IS THE TIER FOR A COMPARISON AGAINST A FIGURE THE DOCUMENT PRINTED AT A
COARSER PRECISION THAN THE CENT. There an exact gate can NEVER go green: the
ACFR's MD&A tables are captioned "(in Millions)" and footnoted "Due to rounding
amounts may differ from what's reported on the financial statements"
(p0034.txt:32 and :56; p0036.txt:7 and :47 says it again as "Numbers might not
tie to financial statements due to rounding"). So any comparison against a
number PRINTED in such a source takes its tolerance from that source's own
declared precision.

THE TOLERANCE RULE. 0.5 x unit x n_terms, or ceil(n_terms/2) cents for
dollar-precision tables. Rules carry units: dollars|thousands|millions.

The tolerance is COMPUTED FROM THE PAGE -- from the printed unit and the number
of terms in the sum -- and is never a number an author picks. Two boundaries
keep it honest, and both are already load-bearing elsewhere:

  - `unit` is the LEAST SIGNIFICANT PRINTED DIGIT, not the caption's word. The
    ACFR MD&A says "(in Millions)" and prints tenths, so unit is $100,000. Read
    the caption instead and a four-term sum would carry $2,000,000 of slack.
  - The dollar-precision branch is deliberately far too tight to absorb the
    corpus's real dollar-level discrepancies, and must not be widened to. Budget
    Book p127's Total Property Taxes is a 13-row sum off by $1; ceil(13/2) is 7
    CENTS. That $1 is the city's arithmetic and is carried by fisc-2sd's
    stated_total_deltas -- a named declaration -- not by this tolerance. The two
    mechanisms are disjoint on purpose; neither is an escape hatch for the other.

THE TWO CHECKS.

1. MAPPED ROWS SUM TO THE TABLE'S STATED TOTAL ROW.
2. THE COMPUTED FUND-BALANCE RESIDUAL EQUALS THE DOCUMENT'S STATED CHANGE IN
   FUND BALANCE. This is the clause that turns a tautology into a real
   cross-check: sources minus uses is arithmetic over facts we mapped, while the
   printed CHANGE IN WORKING CAPITAL is a figure the city published independently
   of them. Nothing in internal/check does this today.

WHAT ACTUALLY NEEDS A DOCUMENT-DERIVED TOLERANCE TODAY: ONLY THE ACFR, AND THE
ACFR IS UNMAPPED. Measured off data/extracted 2026-08-22.

  - The Budget Book (268 pages) and the CIP (323 pages) contain ZERO occurrences
    of "(in millions)", "(in thousands)" or the word "rounding". Only the ACFR
    declares a coarser unit: seven MD&A pages captioned "(in Millions)" (p0034,
    p0036, p0039, p0041, p0042, p0045, p0046) and one Statistical Section page,
    p0170:8 "(In thousands)", Taxable Sales by Category, which belongs to
    fisc-4ua.4 and is blocked there on the non-amount-column decision.
  - The MD&A really does need it. ACFR p0034 Table 1, governmental activities
    2025: 729.2 + 38.2 - 280.1 - 3.5 = 483.8 against a printed total net position
    of 483.9. The Total column likewise: 1,085.6 + 43.1 - 321.5 - 14.2 = 793.0
    against 793.1. Four terms at unit 0.1 gives a 0.2 tolerance and the observed
    error is 0.1. The other four columns of the same table tie exactly, which is
    what makes these two the document's rounding rather than a misread.
  - The mapped corpus does not need it. The spine (pp.66-67, all 240 published
    facts) ties EXACTLY: both total_row rules -- "TOTAL REVENUES:" and "TOTAL
    EXPENDITURES:" -- pass at zero tolerance today, and the fund-balance residual
    ties in all twelve (fund group x budget year) cells. FY2026: general
    158,353,870 - 159,388,024 = -1,034,154 against the printed CHANGE IN WORKING
    CAPITAL; enterprise 3,894,384; capital -2,500,213; debt-service 0;
    special-revenue 8,874,949; internal-service -6,147,533. FY2027: 2,351,098 /
    1,410,280 / -10,129,416 / 0 / 9,021,972 / -7,160,645. So check 2 is
    implementable on today's facts at ZERO tolerance.
  - pp.127-140 tie exactly in both budget columns (fisc-u2v, re-derived twice).
    pp.167-170: the 49 object rows sum to the printed General Fund Total Expenses
    in ALL FOUR columns (123,228,190 / 141,120,420 / 144,650,802 / 149,014,579)
    and the FY2026/FY2027 category sums equal p66's Wages & Benefits
    81,801,011 / 83,825,633 and Services & Supplies 62,849,791 / 65,188,946, with
    Capital Outlay and Debt Services 0/0. Six INTERMEDIATE stated totals are off
    by exactly $1, all in the FY2023-24 Actual column: p168 Finance +1 and
    ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES TOTAL +1, p169 Planning -1 and COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
    TOTAL -1, p169 Public Works Administration +1, p170 Environmental Services -1
    (the last two cancel, so PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT TOTAL ties). Those are
    stated_total_deltas material, not tolerance material -- see the ceil(13/2)
    argument above.

CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLICIT. On the corpus as mapped, both
surviving checks are TIER 1 -- exact, zero tolerance. The tolerance machinery
this bead is named for has no consumer until an ACFR page is mapped, and no bead
proposes mapping the MD&A. Under this epic's own governing rule (verification
work happens only when a page being mapped demands it) that makes this bead's
P0 wrong: it should be P2 and deferred behind an ACFR mapping bead that does not
yet exist. What is P0-shaped is the fund-balance residual check at zero
tolerance over pp.66-67, which is a genuinely new claim about the corpus and
could land in the tier-1 lane (fisc-1wr.1.1) tomorrow.

SCOPE OF WORK, IF WORKED AS WRITTEN. Units on Rule; a tolerance derived per
comparison from unit and n_terms; the two checks above registered at their real
tier; and a test that a tolerance one unit too tight goes red and one unit too
loose is refused rather than accepted. There is no code in this bead for the
expenditure side of the spine -- see the 2026-08-21 and 2026-08-22 notes.
notes:
2026-08-18 ONE DEPENDENT DROPPED: fisc-5gk.3 (p76 transfers) no longer depends on this. That page ties to the CENT on both budget columns and to the spine's TRANSFER IN/OUT rows exactly, so it needs no tolerance at all. This bead's promoted clause -- 'sum(external expenditure links) equals the published all-funds expenditure total from p66-67' -- is unaffected and is still the only recorded check that would catch fisc-u2v.
2026-08-21 THE PROMOTED CLAUSE IS ARITHMETICALLY FALSE, and after fisc-u2v it
cannot fire in the direction it was promoted for. From peer review of the
landing plan. Three separate problems.

(a) OFF BY EXACTLY THE INTERNAL SERVICE FUNDS. The clause reads "sum(external
expenditure links) equals the published all-funds expenditure total from
p66-67". boundaryKind (internal/project/sankey.go:588-593) classifies an
internal-service fund group as KindInternalService, NOT KindExternal. Verified
against a live run at 4259d58:

  PASS  headline-naive-expenditure  sankey FY2026 ... (external $229,018,045.00 ...)

and the p66-67 printed TOTAL EXPENDITURES cells sum to $254,095,412
(144,650,802 + 57,053,730 + 1,061,355 + 6,984,597 + 19,267,561 + 25,077,367).
The difference is 25,077,367 -- precisely the internal-service column. As
written the check is RED the day it lands, and the only way to green it is a
$25M tolerance, which would swallow every error this project exists to catch.

(b) fisc-u2v BLINDS IT. selectFacts filters on f.Scope == o.Scope with exact
equality. Once the scope axis exists, fisc-5gk.2's pp.167-170 facts carry their
own scope and are NOT IN THE SPINE GRAPH AT ALL -- so "sum(external expenditure
links)" cannot see them, doubled or not. The very mechanism that fixes fisc-u2v
removes this clause's ability to catch the same defect on the expenditure side.
The bead's "the only recorded check that would catch fisc-u2v" framing is dead;
it was true when written and is not now.

(c) IN A SPINE-ONLY WAVE IT IS A RESTATEMENT, NOT A CHECK. The external
expenditure links are BUILT FROM the p66-67 facts whose printed total is the
comparand, and build-time CheckTotals already asserts exactly that per
(rule, part). It would report Subjects > 0, so it is not VACUOUS by the report's
definition -- but no page being mapped demands it, which is this epic's own
governing rule.

WHAT REPLACES IT. pp.167-170 tie to the p66 spine EXACTLY, per object category,
in all four columns -- Wages & Benefits 81,801,011 / 83,825,633; Services &
Supplies 62,849,791 / 65,188,946; Capital Outlay 0/0; Debt Services 0/0; total
144,650,802 / 149,014,579 -- and the 49 object rows sum to the printed grand
total in the FY2023-24 column too. So the expenditure side gets the SAME
treatment as the revenue side: a fact-level `expenditure-detail-ties-to-spine`
keyed on {kind, category, fund_group}, TIER 1, ZERO TOLERANCE, landing in
fisc-5gk.2's lane. Not a tier-2 tolerance, and not this bead.

WHAT IS LEFT OF THIS BEAD. The other two clauses -- mapped rows sum to the
table's stated total row, and the computed fund-balance residual equals the
document's STATED change in fund balance -- are untouched and still want a
document-derived tolerance for sources that declare a coarser precision (the
ACFR MD&A, "(in Millions)"). Keep those. Drop the expenditure clause, or rewrite
it against KindInternalService explicitly and say what it is for now that it is
not the u2v guard.
2026-08-22 DESCRIPTION REWRITTEN. Every figure below was re-derived off
data/extracted and a live binary before this note was written; nothing here is
taken on the 2026-08-21 review's word.

REMOVED 1 -- THE PROMOTED EXPENDITURE CLAUSE, "sum(external expenditure links)
equals the published all-funds expenditure total from p66-67". CONFIRMED
ARITHMETICALLY FALSE. boundaryKind (internal/project/sankey.go:585-593) returns
KindInternalService for fundGroupInternalService and KindExternal for everything
else, and headline accumulation (sankey.go:392-403) adds to the external figure
only when kind == KindExternal. The six printed TOTAL EXPENDITURES cells on
pp.66-67 are 144,650,802 + 57,053,730 + 1,061,355 + 6,984,597 + 19,267,561 +
25,077,367 = 254,095,412 for FY2026 (p0066.txt:32 and p0067.txt:34), while
./bin/fisc verify reports headline-naive-expenditure external $229,018,045.00.
The difference is 25,077,367 -- to the cent the internal-service column, and
nothing else. FY2027 the same shape: printed 252,854,896, external
$226,310,381.00, difference 26,544,515 = the internal-service column.

So the clause is RED THE DAY IT LANDS, and the only way to green it is a $25M
tolerance. This project exists to catch plausible wrong values; a $25,077,367
tolerance would swallow every error it is for, including the entire
double-counting defect fisc-u2v was filed about. It is not a check that needs
rewording, it is a check that cannot exist in that form.

REMOVED 2 -- THE FRAMING "the only recorded check that would catch fisc-u2v"
(2026-08-18 note). True when written, not true now. fisc-u2v's 2026-08-21
decision puts the detail schedules at their own scope and selectFacts filters
scope by exact equality, so those facts are not in the spine graph for a
link-sum to see, doubled or not. fisc-u2v's own decision note still says "fisc-
1wr.2's EXPENDITURE clause is unaffected and ... stays P0"; that sentence is
superseded by this note and by fisc-u2v's later same-day correction. The
replacement for the expenditure side is the fact-level, zero-tolerance
expenditure-detail-ties-to-spine in fisc-5gk.2's lane, which the pp.167-170
arithmetic in the new description evidences.

KEPT -- both remaining checks and the tolerance rule, with the rule tightened on
two points that came out of verifying it rather than reading it: unit is the
least significant PRINTED digit, not the caption's word (the MD&A says
"(in Millions)" and prints tenths); and the dollar-precision branch is two
orders of magnitude too tight to absorb the corpus's real $1-$2 subtotal
discrepancies, which is correct and must stay that way, because those belong to
fisc-2sd's declaration channel.

ADDED -- the answer to "what in this corpus needs a document-derived tolerance
today", which the bead never stated. Only the ACFR, and it is unmapped. The
Budget Book and CIP contain no "(in millions)", "(in thousands)" or "rounding"
anywhere in 591 pages. The ACFR MD&A does, on seven pages, and its Table 1
(p0034) genuinely fails an exact test by 0.1 in two of six columns. No bead
proposes mapping the MD&A; the one ACFR bead, fisc-4ua.4, is the Statistical
Section and is blocked on its own non-amount-column decision.

Corrected in passing: "pp.167-170 tie exactly" is true of the grand total in all
four columns and of both budget columns throughout, and FALSE of six
intermediate subtotals in the FY2023-24 Actual column, listed in the description.
They are stated_total_deltas material. fisc-2sd's page list already names p168;
it does not name p169 or p170, so those two are new and belong on fisc-5gk.2.

PRIORITY. Recommend P2 and defer, blocked behind an ACFR mapping bead that does
not exist. Not changed in this pass, because the deliverable was the description
and because the epic owner should be the one to move a P0. The argument is the
epic's own governing rule: no page being mapped demands a tolerance.

DEPENDENTS, ALL THREE RE-EXAMINED against what survives.

  fisc-1wr.3 (tier 3 reconciliations.yaml) -- THE EDGE IS UNJUSTIFIED and should
  be dropped. A reconciliations.yaml entry names any check by ID; Check.ID's own
  doc comment (internal/check/check.go:99-102) says exactly that and does not
  restrict it to a tier. Nothing in .3 needs a tolerance to exist. It is
  deferred for a different and correct reason -- it would ship with zero entries
  -- and that reason does not run through this bead.

  fisc-1wr.4 (tier 4 coverage ratchet) -- THE EDGE IS UNJUSTIFIED and should be
  dropped. A coverage floor is a count of facts inside a projection; it contains
  no arithmetic against a printed figure. This bead's own history shows the same
  pattern already corrected once, when the fisc-gxa.1 edge was removed for
  assuming an ordering nothing argued for.

  fisc-1wr.7 (the four break-it scenarios) -- THE EDGE SURVIVES, on clause 2
  only, and its scenario 3 needs rewording. Scenario 3 is "change one number so
  the cell text still parses -> tier 2 arithmetic must catch it". Both surviving
  clauses can carry it, but neither is tier 2 on the mapped corpus. Clause 1 is
  already enforced at BUILD time: the spine mapping declares total_row on "TOTAL
  REVENUES:" and "TOTAL EXPENDITURES:" and CheckTotals asserts it per (rule,
  part) at zero tolerance, so mutating one object row on p66 is caught today
  without this bead. Clause 2 is the part that does not exist yet and is the
  stronger catch, because it fires on a mutated TOTAL row -- the case where
  clause 1 moves with the error. So .7 should depend on the fund-balance
  residual check, and scenario 3 should read "the stated-total and
  fund-balance-residual checks must catch it" rather than naming a tier. The
  2026-08-19 note that repointed .7 from .4 to .2 was right in direction and
  named the wrong reason.

NOT VERIFIED OFF THE CORPUS. Nothing in the ACFR is mapped, so the tolerance
rule has never been run against a page; the 0.2-covers-0.1 arithmetic on p0034
is done by hand here and could be wrong about which four terms a rule would
actually sum. The claim that pp.127-140 tie exactly in the budget columns is
carried from fisc-u2v's two independent derivations and was spot-checked here
only at p0130:40 against p0066:23 (157,873,470 / 164,358,147).

2026-08-22 FOR THE OWNER, NOT ACTED ON. Three findings from the rewrite pass
that change this bead's place in the graph. Recorded rather than applied,
because two of them alter a P0's dependency edges and one changes its priority.

(1) PRIORITY. With the expenditure clause removed, every surviving clause wants
a document-derived tolerance, and the ONLY source in the corpus that declares
coarser precision is the ACFR MD&A -- measured: Budget Book (268 pp.) and CIP
(323 pp.) contain zero occurrences of "(in millions)", "(in thousands)" or
"rounding". No bead proposes mapping the ACFR. So the tolerance machinery has
zero consumers today, and under this epic's own governing rule -- no check
lands that no mapped page demands -- this reads P2-and-deferred rather than P0.

(2) TWO DEPENDENT EDGES LOOK UNJUSTIFIED. fisc-1wr.3 (reconciliations.yaml):
Check.ID's own doc comment says an entry names ANY check by id, so nothing in
.3 needs a tolerance to exist. fisc-1wr.4 (coverage ratchet): a coverage floor
is a fact count and contains no arithmetic against a printed figure. Neither
edge was removed, because removing an edge from a P0 chain is the owner's call
and a wrong removal un-blocks work that should stay blocked.

(3) fisc-1wr.7's EDGE SURVIVES, on clause 2 only, and its scenario needs
rewording. Scenario 3 says "tier 2 arithmetic must catch it". Clause 1 (mapped
rows sum to the stated total) is ALREADY enforced at build time -- the spine
declares total_row on both TOTAL rows and CheckTotals asserts it at zero
tolerance -- so mutating an object row is caught today without this bead. The
part that does not exist is clause 2, the fund-balance residual against the
document's stated change, and it is the stronger catch because it fires on a
mutated TOTAL row, the case where clause 1 moves with the error. Scenario 3
should name the two checks rather than a tier.

RELATED: clause 2 has been split out as its own tier-1 bead, because it needs no
tolerance, applies to a page that IS mapped, and should not wait behind an ACFR
mapping bead that does not exist.

title: Tier 1: exact, zero-tolerance checks
description: Internal to our own pipeline, so exactness is legitimate: every transfer_id has two equal legs; the graph is acyclic; every link's value_cents equals the sum of its fact_ids; every fund/department/category resolves in funds.yaml/taxonomy.yaml; facts.jsonl is sorted; no ID collisions; AGGREGATION INVARIANCE (the total at every tier depth equals the total at every other depth, which catches double-parented and orphaned nodes); and every derived:true node has a rationale and source_note.
close_reason: Tier 1 lands as 19 checks in internal/check + pkg/cmd/verify, with a five-status model (pass/fail/vacuous/skipped/error) so a check with nothing to test cannot be reported as a pass -- fisc-4rh's requirement. Real: facts sorted, ids unique, category and fund_group vocabulary, graph acyclic, derived nodes justified, link values tie to citations, counts reconcile, headline ties to facts, and two independent witnesses the first pass lacked entirely -- fact-token-reparses (amount.Parse of the fact's own token at its own units) and fact-offset-points-at-token (the provenance pointer asserted over the whole store). Coverage closed by facts-are-projected and published-projection-built after review showed a one-word scope edit could take $157M off the published chart with every check green. Vacuous today: transfer legs (fisc-4rh), aggregation invariance and constraint-tier (fisc-1wr.1.1), fund numbers (until fisc-5gk.1 emits any). Departments report an error naming the absent registry (fisc-o15). Aggregation invariance and constraint-tier remain in the child fisc-1wr.1.1.

notes:

This epic does not close in the PoC run and should not look as though it did.

2026-08-18 GOVERNING RULE agreed in the landing plan, recorded on the epic because it governs which children get worked: VERIFICATION WORK HAPPENS ONLY WHEN A PAGE BEING MAPPED DEMANDS IT.

Context. At the point this was written the repository was four days old, 42.9% of production Go was verification machinery, 240 facts from 2 pages of 786 were published, and the 14 commits since the site was built were all extraction and verification with no page mapped. The diagnosis was NOT that the checking is wrong -- docs/m0-spike.md section 4 records fail-closed preventing 16 facts publishing under wrong row_labels, and fisc-yqv exists because the checks caught silent row loss. The fault is that guards were generalised to all 786 pages before any of the pages that motivate them were attempted. fisc-gmx ('223 of 786 pages cannot carry the column guard') is the shape of the cost.

Applied this round: fisc-1wr.2 partially promoted (it alone catches fisc-u2v), .3/.4/.5.1 deferred, fisc-gmx/fisc-bau/fisc-wa0/fisc-yun measured against the pages in scope and set aside with the measurement recorded. fisc-1wr.6 and internal/amount explicitly untouched -- both are earned.

Note for whoever reads 2/7 as under-delivery: this epic's own earlier note pushes back, and it is right. fisc verify runs 26 checks, every one proven failable by input mutation. But read it beside fisc-0ux: it has never run in CI, 5 checks report VACUOUS, and ci.yml does not pass --strict.

title: Map the p66-67 spine only: all-funds control totals
description:
PROVEN: 136 facts map cleanly from Budget Book PDF pp.66-67 and all 16 column totals tie EXACTLY to the document's own printed totals (General Fund FY2025-26 expenditures $144,650,802; all-funds FY2025-26 revenues $299,969,007).

Structure: rows are 'label followed by N numbers'. p66 carries the labels and the General Fund + Enterprise columns (4 values per row). p67 carries Capital, Debt Service, Special Revenue and Internal Service (8 values per row) with NO labels -- identity is positional from p66.

CORRECTED (fisc-c00): this bead used to say p67 OMITS the all-zero 'Licenses & Permits' row and that the omission must be declared. That was wrong. pdftotext -bbox shows p67 printing all ten revenue rows at the same ten y-positions as p66's ten labelled rows; our extractor was deleting one of three identical all-dash rows. p67 declares NO omitted_rows. The M0 spike's 136 was 128 real values plus 8 invented zeros; the 136 now is 136 real printed cells.

Build the Sankey skeleton from the spine FIRST so the balance checks exist before the detail does. A working reference implementation is in docs/m0-spike/spine.py -- note it maps revenues only from p67 and skips that page's expenditure block.
close_reason: mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml: 5 rules, 10 parts, 240 facts. All 24 columns with a printed total tie exactly; the other six parts are covered by the balance identity, which reconciles all six fund groups in both years against the city's own TOTAL SOURCES and TOTAL USES.

title: fisc build emitting facts.jsonl
description: Options struct + NewCmdBuild(f, runF) + private buildRun per byob-command-shape.1; Options.Validate() first, failing with FlagErrorf before any side effects (byob-input-validation.5).

title: Fact model: content-addressed IDs, specified total order
description:
ID = fisc-f-<12 hex of sha256(doc_id|rule_id|row_path|column_path|fiscal_year|basis)>, deliberately EXCLUDING amount_cents and any row/col index -- so a corrected amount is a modified line rather than delete+add, and an upstream row insertion does not renumber the file. An ID collision is a hard build error: two rules claiming the same cell is a real bug.

facts.jsonl total order: (doc_id, page, row_path, column_path, rule_id). Struct-based emission with fixed key order, no omitempty, LF, trailing newline, .gitattributes text eol=lf. verify checks the file is sorted, which catches nondeterminism in CI for free.
close_reason: internal/fact. ID = fisc-f-<12 hex of sha256(doc_id|rule_id|row_path|row_label|column_path|fiscal_year|basis)>, unit-separator joined so component boundaries cannot shift. row_label is in the tuple because row_path is NOT unique within a rule: p127 prints 13 detail lines all classified taxes/property, and taxonomy.yaml is explicit those are a label not a category -- review caught the collision and it is now a test. Excludes amount and any index, so a corrected figure is a modified line and an inserted row renumbers nothing. Order is the specified (doc_id,page,row_path,column_path,rule_id) EXTENDED by (fiscal_year,basis,id): the specified five tie for two columns of one schedule, and a non-total order defeats the sortedness check it exists to enable. Declared omissions do NOT become facts -- absent is not zero -- so the spine is 128 published facts plus 8 declared absences. amount_cents is always as-printed and sign is presentation, never an instruction to negate.

title: Locator resolution + ambiguity errors listing candidates
description:
Locator = identity, content-INDEPENDENT. For text: {page, section, row_label, ordinal}. For tables: {page, ordinal_on_page, label_fingerprint, bbox_centroid} where label_fingerprint hashes only non-numeric tokens (strip [0-9,.$()%-]) and the centroid rounds to ~10pt.

Why this is separate from the integrity hash: 16 ACFR tables are byte-identical duplicates of another (one 12-way group across pp.12-23; the Budget Book has a 20-way group), so a content hash is NOT an identity. Resolution must require a unique best match; ambiguity or no-match is a hard error printing the top three candidates with their pages and first rows, via ErrHint (byob-errors.2).
notes:
NEXT STEP after fisc-mq4.1 (rule schema, landed). internal/mapping/testdata/spine.yaml is a working target: the M0 spike proved 136 facts come out of Budget Book pp.66-67 with all 16 column totals tying EXACTLY to the totals the document prints (General Fund FY2025-26 expenditures $144,650,802; all-funds FY2025-26 revenues $299,969,007). A reference implementation is committed at docs/m0-spike/spine.py.

Rule.ExpectedValues(part) is the count a positional read must find -- 72 on p67, not 80, because the all-zero Licenses & Permits row is omitted. A mismatch must be a hard error naming the page, never a best-effort read.
close_reason: Resolver lands in internal/mapping/resolve.go with internal/corpus as the artifact reader. Text locator is {page, section, section_ordinal, stop_at}; ordinal is mandatory because REVENUES:/EXPENDITURES: each occur twice on p66. Table locator is {ordinal, label_fingerprint, bbox_centroid}, and a (page,ordinal) miss is always ErrNotFound -- never a fingerprint search that resolves elsewhere, since ACFR p12/p13 are identical in fingerprint, content hash AND bbox. Ambiguity/not-found list up to 3 candidates with line and context via ErrHint. Proven: 128 values from pp.66-67, 16/16 column totals tie exactly.

title: Rule schema + parser (substrate: text|table|manual)
description:
Page text is the PRIMARY substrate: tables miss 46% of the Budget Book's money pages, including the spine (p66-67), the transfer schedule (p76), and revenue-by-fund (p127-140). Typed string enums, not iota, for anything crossing YAML/JSON (byob-typed-string-enums-sql).

M0 spike findings that the schema MUST accommodate:
 - a logical table can span pages, and the continuation page may carry NO row labels at all (p67 is a positional continuation of p66)
 - the continuation page OMITS rows that are all-zero across its columns, so a naive positional zip silently shifts every label after the gap. Rules need an explicit omitted_rows declaration plus a row-count assertion that fails loudly on mismatch.
 - column identity is (fund_group, fiscal_year), addressed by a column_path, not by a single header string (headers span two rows and Table.columns is always empty)
close_reason: Rule schema + parser landed with review fixes. Schema expresses the spine's label-less continuation and omitted rows; validation rejects duplicate columns, multi-document files, unclassified rows and circular block anchors.

title: tools/extract.py with a deterministic serializer
description:
Standalone Python run via 'make extract' -- Go NEVER shells out to it, so there is no embedded script and no exception to the pure-Go rule (byob-release.8).

Config verified to work offline with no model download:
  {use_cache: False, disable_ocr: True, output_format: 'markdown',
   pages: {extract_pages: True}, pdf_options: {extract_tables: True, extract_metadata: True}}

Determinism requirements (these are what make committed artifacts stable):
 - sort tables by (page_number, y0, x0); do NOT trust doc.tables order (ACFR p34 emits one logical table as three fragments in REVERSE document order)
 - format floats %.2f; sort_keys=True; fixed indent; ensure_ascii=False; LF; trailing newline
 - record n_cols per table and the page-text line each row came from
 - do NOT treat processing_warnings as a quality signal: it was empty on both documents despite a silently dropped column

Emit pages/pNNNN.md (the PRIMARY substrate) and tables/pNNNN-tNN.json.

Use the solvent-streets '#@cite' comment convention above hand-entered values. schema_version: 1.

title: internal/amount: strict fail-closed grammar + case table
description:
The most bug-prone code in the project; lands BEFORE any mapping rule exists.

Observed corruption modes that must be REJECTED or handled explicitly:
 1. digits split by whitespace: '2 40,000' for 240,000 (CIP p40) -- REJECT
 2. em-dash-as-zero glued to the next column: ACFR p54 '48,030,349 | -1,315,352 | 49,345,701' where the true reading is +1,315,352 -- REJECT a leading '-' not preceded by a column boundary
 3. '$' bleeding one cell right: p68 ['Wastewater $ ', '27,799,694 $ ', ...] -- strip orphaned $
 4. parenthesis negatives: '(71.8)' -- negative
 5. '-' means zero; '' means ABSENT -- different meanings, both occur, must not be conflated
 6. units vary (dollars/thousands/millions) and come from the rule, not the token
 7. NEW from the M0 spike: '\\-' (backslash-escaped dash) appears in the extracted markdown as a distinct zero token

Amounts are integer cents, never float. Table-driven tests with google/go-cmp per byob-testing.2, in the same commit per byob-testing.4.
close_reason: internal/amount landed: strict fail-closed grammar, all 7 corruption modes, corpus-validated. Confirmed the glued-dash corruption independently on ACFR p177 by row arithmetic.

title: A cancelled fisc verify reports every vacuity declaration stale and exits 3
description:
internal/check/vacuity.go:98,108:

  func (d Declaration) Ran() bool   { return d.Status != "" }
  func (d Declaration) Stale() bool { return d.Ran() && d.Status != StatusVacuous }

Ran() documents "did this run contain the check at all", and Stale() is
documented as "the check ran and reported something other than vacuous, so the
work it was waiting for has landed". FIVE STATUSES EXIST, and Stale() treats
three of them as landed-work: StatusPass, StatusFail and -- wrongly --
StatusSkipped and StatusError.

THE REACHABLE TRIGGER IS StatusError, AND IT IS CONTEXT CANCELLATION. run1
(internal/check/report.go:101-103) turns ctx.Err() into errored(...). So a
cancelled or timed-out `fisc verify` marks ALL THREE declarations stale, and
Report.Failed() (report.go:174-181) returns true on len(StaleDeclarations()) > 0
INDEPENDENTLY OF --strict. The run exits 3 printing, three times, "declared
vacuous and reported error; fisc-gxa.2 landed, so remove the declaration" --
about work that has not landed, in response to a Ctrl-C.

StatusSkipped is the same bug and is NOT reachable today, which is worth saying
so nobody widens the fix on a false premise: sourcePDFsMatchBothRecords
(internal/check/structural.go:675) is the only Full() == true check in the tree,
it is a tier-0 artifact check, and no one would declare it vacuous. Guard it
anyway -- the next --full check inherits the hole.

A GENUINE StatusError IS DIFFERENT AND SHOULD NOT BE SILENT. aggregation-invariance
is deliberately built to hard-error the moment any node carries a parent
(internal/check/graph.go:720-725, and its own declared reason says "it cannot be
reached by halves"). When THAT fires, the work really has landed. So the fix is
not "ignore error": it is that stale is a claim about pass/fail, and an errored
declared check needs its own wording rather than StaleReason()s "landed, so
remove the declaration".

Found by /code-review of HEAD~4..HEAD, 2026-08-24. Landed in 40943db.
acceptance_criteria: Stale() is true only for StatusPass and StatusFail; a declared check reporting StatusError or StatusSkipped does not fail the run; a cancelled verify does not report stale declarations; an errored declared check is reported with wording that does not claim its bead landed; tests cover all five statuses

title: transfers-detail-ties-to-spine needs a comparison mode detailtie.go does not have
description:
fisc-aes specifies the check in three clauses. Two of them cannot be expressed
by the machinery detailtie.go provides, and the p76 landing plan understated
both.

WHAT THE CLAUSES NEED.

(b) kind = transfer_out, fund_group in {general, enterprise, internal-service,
    debt-service}: detail sum + a named to-CIP constant == spine sum.
(c) kind = transfer_out, fund_group in {capital, special-revenue}, THE TWO
    JOINTLY: detail sum + non-major to-CIP constant == the two spine columns
    summed.

THREE GAPS.

1. detailRestriction.FundGroup is ONE string. (b) admits four groups and (c)
   two, so it needs a SET.

2. "A per-clause constant" is a scalar and the clauses need a TABLE. Measured
   off p0073.txt / p0075.txt, per (fund_group, fiscal_year):
     general           0 / 0
     enterprise        9,353,147 / 14,220,000
     internal-service  40,000 / 612,000
     debt-service      0 / 0
     non-major (joint) 28,693,590 / 35,930,251

3. AND THE HARD ONE: clause (c) needs KEY COLLAPSING. detailKey carries
   fundGroup and compareDetail compares per key, so as written (c) compares
   capital (211,150 vs 28,584,740) and special-revenue (817,050 vs 1,137,050)
   separately and the joint constant has nowhere to land. Collapsing capital and
   special-revenue into one compared cell BREAKS detailtie.go's stated invariant
   -- "IT IS A FILTER AND NOT A KEY... Collapse the two and a check whose
   schedule spans every group would compare six groups' facts under one key and
   tie on a sum that happens to match." That invariant is right and the collapse
   is a real exception to it, so it needs an argument rather than a quiet edit.
   The argument available: the collapse here is not the restriction leaking into
   the key, it is the DOCUMENT declining to print the split, and the pair is the
   finest granularity the corpus publishes.

WHY (c) IS JOINT AT ALL, corrected. fisc-aes says the FY2026-27 split is
impossible because it would need a to-CIP of -117,485. THAT IS FALSE -- see the
correction on fisc-aes. Both years split cleanly. The real reason is
published-is-not-derived: pp.72-75 print to-CIP per major fund and then ONE
aggregate line for all non-major funds, so a per-group constant would be derived
by difference from p67 while the pair is printed.

Found in peer review of the p76 landing plan, 2026-08-24. Blocks fisc-5gk.3.1.
close_reason: Landed in ced45b4. p76 publishes 88 facts at scope transfers-by-fund (22 rows x 2 budget years x 2 legs) and transfers-detail-ties-to-spine reconciles them in three clauses: IN exact with no constant, OUT-major with the printed to-CIP figures added back, OUT-non-major with capital+special-revenue+permanent collapsed. Doubling proven by measurement rather than argued: republished at all-funds-gross the GF in-leg goes 480,400 -> 960,800 while three graph checks stay green. Only the two budget columns are published. See each bead's own note for what it owed.

title: p76 prints one total for the whole schedule and a Rollup is refused twice over
description:
The second thing that must be settled before p76's YAML can be written.

p76 prints ONE grand total beneath its last section -- $29,947,677 /
$27,679,706 / $21,525,997 / $21,624,633 -- and no per-section totals. So no
single rule can carry it as total_row, and the obvious answer, a Rollup over the
section rules, is refused twice by parse.go:

(1) a covered rule with TotalRow == "" is refused, because "a rollup sums the
    totals its covered rules PRINT, so every one of them must print one". None
    of p76's sections prints one.
(2) covered rules whose Parts[0].Columns differ are refused. p76's sections
    declare DIFFERENT fund_group per column -- general, enterprise,
    debt-service, permanent, special-revenue -- so they are not the same columns
    by construction.

THE OPTIONS.

(a) Rollup.Unassertable with a reason. Precedent exists (other-funds-total-sources).
    Honest and cheap. Cost: the page's own printed total then checks nothing at
    build time, and it is the only arithmetic p76 offers against itself.

(b) A cross-rule ROW-SUM concept -- a total that sums covered rules' VALUES
    rather than their printed totals. internal/mapping/rule.go argues against
    exactly this: "a rollup summing leaves would tie or fail depending on
    whether the document's roundings happened to cancel". That argument was made
    about a different case and should be re-stated against this one rather than
    inherited, because p76's four columns tie EXACTLY on the two budget years
    (0 delta, internal/mapping/transfers_p76_test.go) so there is no rounding to
    cancel.

(c) Leave the cross-rule sum in Go, where transfers_p76_test.go already has it.
    Cost: it checks the fixture, not the published rules.

STATE THE CONSEQUENCE WHICHEVER WAY IT GOES: fisc build's parts_unchecked count
goes 6 -> 11 when p76's five sections publish without a total_row. That number is
reported by pkg/cmd/build/report.go and a jump in it should be explained by the
commit that causes it, not discovered afterwards.

Found in peer review of the p76 landing plan, 2026-08-24, which asserted a
rollup over the six in-leg rules would work.
close_reason: Landed in ced45b4. p76 publishes 88 facts at scope transfers-by-fund (22 rows x 2 budget years x 2 legs) and transfers-detail-ties-to-spine reconciles them in three clauses: IN exact with no constant, OUT-major with the printed to-CIP figures added back, OUT-non-major with capital+special-revenue+permanent collapsed. Doubling proven by measurement rather than argued: republished at all-funds-gross the GF in-leg goes 480,400 -> 960,800 while three graph checks stay green. Only the two budget columns are published. See each bead's own note for what it owed.

title: A published part needs a channel for a column the page prints no header over
description:
Budget Book p76 cannot be published until this is settled, and it is a schema
question rather than a p76 question.

THE MECHANICS, verified.

parse.go requires column_headers to carry one entry per column INCLUDING every
skip: true one, and refuses an empty entry. p76 needs five columns: four years
plus the footnote marker, which the fixture declares as {skip: true}
(internal/mapping/testdata/transfers-p76.yaml). The page prints four headers,
over the four year columns, and nothing over the footnote
(testdata/pages/budget-p0076.txt line 9). internal/mapping/geometry.go matches
all headers on ONE printed line, so there is no fifth header anywhere to name.

AND OMITTING column_headers IS NOT AN OPTION. TestPublishedPartsDeclareColumnHeaders
(internal/mapping/mappings_test.go) is a ratchet: all 120 published parts declare
them today. p76 would be the first published part with a skipped column, and the
design has no channel for it.

WHY THE SKIPPED COLUMN IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT COSMETIC. amount.Parse reads
"(10)" as NEGATIVE TEN DOLLARS, because negatives are parenthesised throughout
this corpus. Nothing downstream sees that value only because the column is
skipped. Measured: every one of p76's 22 rows carries a marker, and there are
ten distinct ones -- (1) through (10).

THE OPTIONS.

(a) Move the markers to wrapped_labels. WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS: the gap does trim
    to "(10)", but all ten distinct markers would have to be declared, and they
    are footnote REFERENCES rather than wrapped label fragments. The declaration
    would say something untrue about the page in order to satisfy a guard.

(b) Give column_headers an explicit channel for a headerless column -- a null,
    or a rule that a skip: true column takes no entry. The cost is that the
    entry count stops being a check on the column count, which is part of what
    the guard buys.

(c) Something else. Note the guard's purpose: it is the column-grid check, and
    what it defends against is a rule whose columns have silently drifted from
    the page's. Whatever lands has to keep defending that.

Found in peer review of the p76 landing plan, 2026-08-24, which had this as a
one-line bullet.
close_reason: Decided and landed (fb28394): column_headers accepts an explicit null entry, legal only opposite a skip:true column and only in the last position. Option (b) of the three on the bead. The entry count stays the column-count check, which is what the guard buys. Two things the bead did not anticipate, both found by building it: yaml.v3 drops a null element from a sequence rather than decoding it, so ColumnHeaders had to become a named slice with its own unmarshaler; and an all-null list has to be refused, because the grid IS the headers. The restriction to the LAST position is the argument that keeps the weakened guard honest -- between two headers the gap has known bounds the grid would have checked.

title: Three committed fixtures are checked by nothing: fixturePages does not have to cover testdata/
description:
testdata/pages/ and testdata/geometry/ each carry eleven fixtures.
internal/mapping/resolve_test.go:169's fixturePages lists EIGHT:

  budget: 66, 67, 76, 127, 167        committed: 66, 67, 76, 127, 167, 168, 169, 170
  cip:    29, 40                      committed: 29, 40
  acfr:   177                         committed: 177

So budget pp.168, 169 and 170 -- six files, three page-text and three geometry
-- are read by tests and checked against the extraction by NOTHING.
TestFixturesAreVerbatimCopies iterates the list, not the directory.

They landed in a430cec, which added them and did not add the rows. The doc
comment on fixtureCopies says "Adding a fixture means adding a row here and
nothing else", and that sentence is exactly the gap: it describes a convention,
and a convention is not a check.

MEASURED 2026-08-24: none of the six has drifted yet, so this is a live hole
rather than a live failure. That is the whole reason to fix it now.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSING ROW. TestFixturesAreVerbatimCopies' own doc
comment says it "is what makes every other test in this package mean anything",
and names the xberg -> poppler migration (fisc-yqv.5) as the case where fixtures
drifted from the extraction and every test reading them stayed green against a
substrate that no longer existed. Three fixtures currently sit outside that
guarantee, and every arithmetic claim proved against them -- the p168 two-level
rounding chain the whole Rollup design rests on, p170's General Fund Total
Expenses tie to the spine -- is proved against a file nothing says is real.

It also gets worse immediately: fisc-5gk.1 commits thirteen more page/geometry
pairs for pp.128-140. Adding thirteen rows by hand to a list nothing verifies is
the same coin flip twenty-six more times.

THE FIX IS NOT THE THREE ROWS, it is a test that the list COVERS THE DIRECTORY:
read testdata/pages and testdata/geometry, and fail on any file no fixtureCopy
names. That makes the convention machine-checked and turns "someone forgot" into
a red build in the commit that forgets. Same shape as unprojectedScopes'
staleDeclarations arm and fisc-2sd's remove-the-declaration branch: a
declaration that has stopped describing the tree must fail rather than go quiet.

Found while preparing fisc-5gk.1's fixtures, 2026-08-24.
acceptance_criteria: budget pp.168-170 are in fixturePages; a test reads testdata/pages and testdata/geometry and fails on any committed fixture no fixtureCopy names; that test is proven failable by removing one row from the list
close_reason:
Fixed, and the class is closed rather than the instance.

budget pp.168-170 are in fixturePages. More to the point,
TestEveryCommittedFixtureIsListed now reads testdata/pages and
testdata/geometry and fails on any committed file no fixtureCopy names, so the
list cannot fall behind the directory again. Proven failable by dropping p170
from the list: two findings, one per substrate, each naming the file and the fix.

It also refuses a vacuous pass -- a fixture directory that reads as empty is an
error rather than a loop that ran zero times, which is the failure mode a
directory-walking test invites.

fixtureCopies' doc comment said "Adding a fixture means adding a row here and
nothing else", which was the whole gap: it described a convention, and a
convention is not a check. It now names the test that enforces it and this bead.

None of the six files had drifted, so nothing that was proved against them was
wrong. What was wrong is that nothing said so.

title: CheckRollup compares only the COUNT of covered rules' columns, not which columns they are
description:
internal/mapping/resolve.go:964-985. CheckRollup takes `cols` from the FIRST covered rule's total-bearing part and then, for every later rule, checks only `len(stated) != len(sums)`.

So two covered rules whose bearer parts declare the same NUMBER of columns but DIFFERENT columns are summed against each other, column by column, without complaint. A rollup could add rule A's FY2026 general column to rule B's FY2027 enterprise column and report a clean tie.

WHY THE EXISTING GUARDS DO NOT CLOSE IT. validateRollups cross-checks units and columns at parse time, but against `Parts[0].Columns`. CheckRollup's own comment (resolve.go:958-963) explains why that is not enough -- 'which part bears the total needs the pages' -- and then does the weaker check anyway. The two halves of the argument are both present in the file; only the conclusion is missing.

NOT REACHABLE ON pp.167-170: the 23 division rules all declare the same four columns on every part, so the department lane cannot trigger it. It becomes live the moment a rollup covers rules whose bearer parts differ, which is what p130's 'Total General Fund' over pp.127-130 will be (fisc-5gk.1).

FIX: compare the bearer parts' Columns element by element (fund_group, fiscal_year, basis, skip), not their length, and name the two rules and the first differing column when they disagree.

TEST: two covered rules with same-width, differently-labelled columns must fail. A length-only test passes with the bug present, which is how it survived.

Found by /code-review of the fisc-o15 landing, 2026-08-23, and verified against the source.
close_reason: Landed in a3adb0e. fisc-7fe fixed element-wise on the EFFECTIVE basis (the Column.Basis override half was found in review of the fix); fisc-7a6 fixed at both sites, its premise corrected on the bead first; fisc-t9h guarded before both rules[0] indexes. Each test proven red against the prior code. Kind/scope left uncompared and filed separately.

title: Is one picture the product? fisc-gkv point D, and only the owner can answer it
description:
fisc-gkv decided points A, B and C -- a projection MAY select more than one scope
(Options.Scopes as a set), two scopes may NOT be selected together if a
reconciliation check relates them, and Sankey keeps exactly one scope. Those are
engineering conclusions backed by measurement and they are closed.

POINT D IS NOT AN ENGINEERING QUESTION AND fisc-gkv SAID SO. It recommends that
the finest-grain graph be a SECOND document, selecting {revenue-by-fund,
gf-department-object} and not the spine, with NO headline. Its own confidence
line reads: 'Medium on (D), the two-document split, because it trades a reader
question for a code guarantee and the reader question is not answerable from
this repository.'

THE QUESTION, in the form only the repo owner can answer: is one picture --
following a dollar from source to spend in a single view -- the product?

WHY IT CANNOT BE DECIDED BY MEASUREMENT. fisc-gxa.2's pitch is one picture. The
two-document answer means a reader cannot see $157,873,470 arrive from ~71
detail lines and leave through 11 departments without a client-side join across
two fetches, and no check covers that join. fisc-gkv's answer is that the join
is not across the two documents -- revenue-by-fund and gf-department-object are
disjoint and travel together in the tier document, so the spine document is the
citywide overview and the tier document is the drill-down. Two views, not two
halves of one view. That is a product claim, not a code claim.

WHAT IT COSTS IF THE ANSWER IS 'ONE PICTURE'. fisc-gkv (4) measured the price
and it is four changes, not one. Adding `fund` to cellKey is inert today (all
240 committed facts carry fund 0) and INSUFFICIENT tomorrow: with a tier-3
endpoint the graph builds and publishes a gross revenue of 36,411,276,900
against the golden file's 29,996,900,700, because Headline accumulates PER CELL
(sankey.go:393, 404, 412, 418) and splitting one cell into two adds both.
headline-ties-to-facts (check/graph.go:407-445) then re-sums the same facts the
headline was accumulated from and reports GREEN on the wrong number. And
revenue/taxes/property gains two outbound links carrying the same $64,143,762,
so d3 draws that node at twice its true width -- a visual double-count no
per-link check sees.

A HEADLINE IS A PROPERTY OF A SINGLE-GRAIN DOCUMENT. Once one document holds two
grains of the same money, 'the total' is ambiguous and no cell key can
disambiguate it, because the ambiguity is in the ACCUMULATION and not in the
key. So 'one picture' costs: the key, tier-aware endpoints, tier-aware headline
accumulators, and teaching headline-ties-to-facts which grain it is summing.

WHAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON IT. Nothing in the coverage lanes. fisc-5gk.1 and
fisc-5gk.2 publish facts at their own scope and are reconciled by fact-level
checks reading Subject.Facts, not any graph. Only the tier-hierarchy commit --
fisc-gxa.2, fisc-oxf, fisc-1wr.1.1, fisc-ix2 -- consumes the answer.

SO IT IS DECIDABLE LATER AT NO COST, AND BETTER DECIDED AGAINST A CHART THAT
EXISTS THAN AGAINST ONE THAT DOES NOT. That is fisc-gkv's own recommendation and
the reason this is split out rather than left blocking the wave. If the answer
turns out to be 'one picture' after the thing is drawn, the fallback is the
four-part redesign above, and fisc-gkv asks that it be re-opened deliberately
rather than improvised at the keyboard.

Split out of fisc-gkv on 2026-08-23 so that bead's decided points A/B/C could
close without this one closing with them.
acceptance_criteria: a recorded answer to whether the finest-grain view is a SECOND document or one graph carrying tiers 0-5; if two documents, the client join and its absence of checks is accepted in writing; if one graph, the four-part redesign in fisc-gkv (4) is scheduled and owned before fisc-gxa.2 starts

title: Tier 1: the computed fund-balance residual equals the document's STATED change in fund balance
description:
Extracted from fisc-1wr.2 during its 2026-08-22 rewrite. That bead's surviving
clauses all want a DOCUMENT-DERIVED TOLERANCE for a source that declares coarser
precision, and the only such source in the corpus is the ACFR MD&A, which is
unmapped. This clause wants no tolerance at all, applies to a page that IS
mapped, and is therefore tier 1 rather than tier 2 -- so it should not wait
behind an ACFR mapping bead that does not exist.

THE CLAIM: the fund-balance residual this project COMPUTES equals the change in
fund balance the document itself STATES.

WHY IT IS WORTH HAVING, and this is the part that makes it different from the
other checks in the tier: most of what fisc verify asserts ties the graph to the
facts it was built FROM. This ties a computed quantity to an INDEPENDENTLY
PRINTED one. fisc-u2v's coverage.go incident and the whole scope axis exist
because "the graph agrees with its own inputs" is a weak claim. This is a strong
one, and pp.66-67 already print both sides.

VERIFIED to tie at zero tolerance in all twelve fund-group x fiscal-year cells
during the fisc-1wr.2 rewrite. Worked example, General Fund FY2026:
  158,353,870 - 159,388,024 = -1,034,154
which equals the printed CHANGE IN WORKING CAPITAL cell exactly.

Note what this is NOT: it is not the transfer residual (that is
headline-transfer-residual, already shipping), and it is not CheckTotals, which
