is a build-time per-part assertion against a printed TOTAL row rather than a
check over the projection.

SIZE: small. Both sides are already in the fact store -- the spine's
fund_balance rules ship 48 facts -- so this is a check, not a mapping change.
acceptance_criteria: the check reports Subjects > 0 over pp.66-67 and passes at zero tolerance in all twelve fund-group x year cells; it is proven failable by mutating one fund_balance fact; it is registered in the tier-1 lane and not behind fisc-1wr.2
notes:
2026-08-23 ALREADY SATISFIED, and by a stronger assertion than this bead
proposes. Found while implementing it; verified by running the test.

internal/mapping/mappings_test.go:253 TestPublishedSpineBalancesPerFundGroup
asserts, over the same six fund groups and the same two budget years:

    sources = revenue + transfer_in + max(0, -change)
    uses    = expenditure + transfer_out + reserve_increase + max(0, change)
    sources == uses

which rearranges to exactly this bead's claim,

    revenue + transfer_in - expenditure - transfer_out - reserve_increase
        == fund-balance/change

and it then goes FURTHER than this bead asks: it pins both sides to the
printed TOTAL SOURCES / TOTAL USES control totals for all twelve cells --
rows that are mapped by no rule, which is what makes it a cross-check rather
than a restatement. This bead names no control total at all.

MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY off facts/facts.jsonl before finding the test: all 12
cells tie at zero, General Fund FY2026 = -1,034,154, this bead's worked
example to the cent.

THE ONE REAL DELTA, recorded so it is not lost: the existing assertion is a Go
test over the RESOLVED MAPPING, and `fisc verify` makes no such claim over the
committed fact store. That gap is narrower than it looks -- CI runs
`fisc build` and cmp's byte-for-byte against facts/facts.jsonl, so mapping and
artifact cannot drift -- and a mutated amount_cents or token is already caught
by fact-token-reparses and fact-offset-points-at-token, which tie every figure
to the page it was read from. What a verify-side version would add over all of
that is the axis, not the claim.

CONSEQUENCE FOR fisc-1wr.7, which this blocks: its scenario 3 must name
TestPublishedSpineBalancesPerFundGroup as the existing catch rather than wait
for a check that would duplicate it. fisc-1wr.2's 2026-08-22 note says "the
part that does not exist is clause 2, the fund-balance residual against the
document's stated change" -- that is the premise this closure corrects; it
does exist, one package over.

STILL UNASSERTED, filed separately rather than folded in here:
beginning + change - ending == 0, which also holds at zero in all 12 cells
(measured), and which neither the test above nor any check makes.
close_reason: Already satisfied by TestPublishedSpineBalancesPerFundGroup (internal/mapping/mappings_test.go:253), which asserts the same identity over the same 12 cells and additionally pins the printed TOTAL SOURCES / TOTAL USES control totals. See the 2026-08-23 note for the measurement and for the consequence to fisc-1wr.7.

title: [bug] label_tail re-keyed the row index on Identity() but omitted_rows, the total_row guard and ActiveRows still use bare Label
description:
The 2026-08-21 label_tail work re-keyed the parser's row index on
Row.Identity() (Label + "\x1f" + LabelTail) but left three sites validating and
filtering on the BARE Label. Each is a fail-open, which is the wrong direction
for this repo.

(1) omitted_rows IS UNMATCHABLE FOR A TWO-ANCHOR ROW. internal/mapping/parse.go
    validates omitted_rows entries against the bare label while the index is
    keyed on Identity(). Omitting a row that carries a label_tail errors with
    "is not one of this rule's rows", and NO YAML value can match, because the
    key contains a \x1f the author cannot type. Part.OmittedRows' own doc calls
    the declaration MANDATORY -- "without it a positional read shifts every
    label after the gap, which is a silent mismapping rather than an error". So
    a page that needs both features cannot be expressed.

(2) THE total_row "IS ALSO LISTED IN rows" GUARD IS SILENTLY DISABLED for any
    row carrying a label_tail. The guard exists to stop a printed total being
    mapped as a data row. With the key change it no longer fires, and the
    failure surfaces -- if at all -- as an unexplained CheckTotals mismatch,
    which is exactly the "row was missed" hint the resolver prints when it
    cannot tell you what actually happened.

(3) Rule.ActiveRows still filters by Label.

WHY ONE BEAD: all three are the same edit half-applied, and fixing one without
the others leaves the inconsistency somewhere else. The fact model has the same
defect from the other end -- see the fact-id bug -- but that one is a published
claim and gets its own id.

Also here, minor and in the same file: the "label_tail is blank" branch is
UNREACHABLE. A whitespace-only tail is caught by the preceding whitespace check,
so the blank branch cannot be entered and a caller who writes label_tail: ""
gets the wrong message.

Found by /code-review over the 8 commits ahead of origin/main, 2026-08-22.
acceptance_criteria: a two-anchor row can be named in omitted_rows; the total_row 'is also listed in rows' guard fires for a two-anchor row; ActiveRows filters on the same key the index uses; the unreachable blank-label_tail branch is removed or made reachable; each fix has a test that fails without it
close_reason: Landed in 3589fa2 with a fifth site neither bead named (canonicalRows pairing on Label, colliding RowIndex with omissions). MakeID takes PrintedLabel(); the reasoning and its accepted cost are in the doc comment.

comments.author: Jon Crussell
comments.text:
Fixed, plus one more site of the same defect the description did not list.

SYNTAX CHOSEN FOR omitted_rows. An entry is written the way the ROW is written:
a bare label for a row named by one anchor, the two fields for a row named by
two. Both spellings in one list.

  omitted_rows: ["Licenses & Permits"]
  omitted_rows:
    - {label: "Transfer From Wastewater", label_tail: "to Stormwater"}

Implemented as mapping.OmittedRow with an UnmarshalYAML that accepts a scalar
or a mapping. Matching is on Row.Identity(), the same key the row index uses,
so an entry addresses exactly one row and no author has to type a \x1f.
Rejected alternative: one string spelling both anchors -- that would mean
asserting the run of spaces the page prints between the fields, which is the
one thing label_tail exists in order not to do. Every existing declaration is
unchanged: the scalar form is still the scalar form.

FAIL-CLOSED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, as required:
  - names no row      -> "%q is not one of this rule's rows" (unchanged)
  - names more than one -> "Transfer From General Fund" names 3 rows, which
    differ only in their label_tail: [...]; hint: a row named by two anchors is
    omitted by naming both
  - declared twice, blank label, whitespace-padded label_tail: all refused
  - KnownFields(true) does not reach a custom unmarshaler, so unknown keys are
    refused inside UnmarshalYAML: label_tial would otherwise be dropped and the
    entry would silently name a different row

THE FOUR FIXES, each with the message its mutation produces:

(1) parse.go omitted_rows validated on Identity() [internal/mapping/parse.go]
    mutate -> rowIndex[o.Label]:
    TestATwoAnchorRowIsOmittedByNamingBothAnchors: two-anchor.yaml: rule
    "two-anchor": parts[page 76].omitted_rows: "Transfer From General Fund to
    Wastewater" is not one of this rule's rows

(2) ActiveRows + resolve.go omissions() filter on Identity() [rule.go via the
    new omittedSet helper, shared by both so they cannot drift]
    mutate -> set keyed on Label:
    TestActiveRowsDropOnlyTheRowNamed: ActiveRows (-want +got): + "Transfer
    From General Fund to Wastewater" -- i.e. one entry dropped all three rows,
    and TestATwoAnchorRowIsOmittedByNamingBothAnchors then fails at resolve
    time with: rows: row "Transfer From General Fund": second anchor "to
    Wastewater" does not occur after it

(2b) NOT IN THE DESCRIPTION: resolve.go canonicalRows() paired active rows to
    rule rows on Label too, so with an omission the surviving rows got the
    OMITTED row's RowIndex -- values and omissions then land in the same slot,
    which is exactly what Omission.RowIndex's doc says must not happen.
    mutate -> Label:
    TestATwoAnchorRowIsOmittedByNamingBothAnchors: value 2 has RowIndex 1,
    want 2

(3) total_row "is also listed in rows" guard now tests the row's Label (and its
    PrintedLabel), not rowIndex. A total_row is a plain string the author types
    and the resolver finds in the page text, so it can NEVER equal an Identity()
    carrying a \x1f -- testing the index disabled the guard outright.
    mutate -> rowIndex[r.TotalRow]:
    TestTotalRowInRowsIsRefusedForATwoAnchorRow: parsed; a total_row that is
    also a data row double-counts it

(4) the blank label_tail branch is now reachable: the blank test runs BEFORE the
    whitespace test, so "   " is reported as blank instead of as stray
    whitespace. Keeping it (rather than deleting it) is worth it because the two
    messages send the author to different places -- one to trim a character, one
    to name the anchor they meant.
    mutate -> original order:
    TestBlankLabelTailIsReportedAsBlank: error does not say the tail is blank:
    ... label_tail "   " has leading or trailing whitespace

Also: pkg/cmd/build/report.go recorded a declared omission's RowLabel as
o.Row.Label, which is ambiguous for a two-anchor row; it now reports
PrintedLabel(). No shipped output moves (the one omitted_rows in a test fixture
is tail-less).

Tests: internal/mapping/labeltail_test.go. facts.jsonl byte-identical, fisc
verify 20/0/5/1.

title: [bug] p140 Total Sources exceeds the pages it closes by ~$57M, differently per column
description:
p0140.txt:52 prints, as the closing line of the REVENUE SOURCES BY FUNDS /
OTHER FUNDS run (pp.131-140):

  Total Sources    $201,271,189   $219,927,720   $219,633,968   $216,596,302

Nothing on those pages sums to it, and the shortfall is a DIFFERENT amount in
every column, so it is not a rounding artefact and not a single omitted fund.

MEASURED off data/extracted, by summing the 69 printed `Total <fund>` lines on
pp.131-140 (all four columns, dashes excluded, no figure typed in):

  printed         summed          gap
  201,271,189     142,497,642     58,773,547   FY2023-24 actual
  219,927,720     161,091,271     58,836,449   FY2024-25 revised
  219,633,968     163,141,134     56,492,834   FY2025-26 budget
  216,596,302     159,222,794     57,373,508   FY2026-27 budget

(The FY2023-24 sum is 142,497,642 against fisc-u2v's 142,497,640; the $2 is the
document's own rounding in that column, which fisc-2sd declares per block.)

THE FIGURE APPEARS NOWHERE ELSE IN THE CORPUS. Verified:
`grep -rl "219,633,968" data/extracted` returns p0140.txt and its own
geometry/p0140.json, and nothing else across all 786 extracted pages.

WHY THIS IS A FINDING AND NOT A FOOTNOTE. fisc-5gk.1 maps these ten pages and
fisc-u2v's decision rests on them being a COMPLETE, EXACT, ALTERNATIVE
DECOMPOSITION of the spine's revenue side -- which they are, per fund group, to
the cent. A printed total on the same pages that exceeds their own contents by
~$57M is either (a) a claim about money the schedule does not itemise, or
(b) a total over a wider set than the pages it closes. Neither reading is
recorded anywhere, and fisc-u2v names it only in passing while ruling it
unassertable.

The name is the clue worth chasing: SOURCES, not REVENUES. The
headline-ties-to-revenues-not-sources memory records that on pp.66-67 TOTAL
SOURCES = revenues + transfers in, a different printed row from TOTAL REVENUES.
So the likeliest explanation is that p140's Total Sources includes a component
the fund sections do not itemise -- use of fund balance being the obvious
candidate. That is a hypothesis, NOT a finding; it has not been checked.

WHAT SETTLING IT BUYS. If the gap has a published decomposition, this row
becomes a real check on the lane. If it does not, the lane must SAY so -- via
the reason channel the cross-rule rollup bead asks for -- rather than mapping
ten pages and silently declining to mention that the page's own closing total
does not reconcile.

DO NOT resolve it with a stated_total_deltas entry. A $57M delta is not the
city's rounding, and fisc-2sd cannot catch a fictional declaration.

Found while verifying the backlog waves, 2026-08-22, from fisc-u2v DEFECT 4.
acceptance_criteria: the gap between p140's printed Total Sources and the sum of pp.131-140's fund totals is explained from published figures, or the lane declares the row unassertable through a reason channel that says the DOCUMENT prints a total this rule structure cannot reconcile; no stated_total_deltas entry absorbs it
notes:
2026-08-24 INVESTIGATED AND SETTLED, and the bead's own hypothesis is REFUTED
rather than merely unproven. Every figure below was derived by summing the pages
in data/extracted; nothing is typed in but the printed totals being tested.

THE GAP, reproduced exactly as the bead states it. Summing the 69 printed
`Total <fund>` lines on pp.131-140, all four columns:

  printed p0140.txt:52   summed 69       gap
  201,271,189            142,497,642     58,773,547   FY2023-24 actual
  219,927,720            161,091,271     58,836,449   FY2024-25 revised
  219,633,968            163,141,134     56,492,834   FY2025-26 budget
  216,596,302            159,222,794     57,373,508   FY2026-27 budget

FUND BALANCE IS NOT THE MISSING COMPONENT. The bead names "use of fund balance"
as the obvious candidate. The non-General-Fund aggregate draw on fund balance,
read off pp.68-75, is 10,849,816 / 53,470,745 / -2,938,500 / 6,607,809. In
FY2025-26 those funds COLLECTIVELY ADD $2.9M to fund balance while the gap in
that column is +$56.5M. Even the most generous reading -- summing only the
positive draws group by group and ignoring the funds that add -- gives
19,087,150 / 55,750,717 / 9,244,229 / 15,958,968, which misses every column.
The hypothesis is refuted, not open.

NOR IS IT THE GENERAL FUND. Adding p0130.txt:40's Total General Fund
(142,028,002 / 148,800,148 / 157,873,470 / 164,358,147) gives 284,525,644 /
309,891,419 / 321,014,604 / 323,580,941, which OVERSHOOTS the printed row by
83,254,455 / 89,963,699 / 101,380,636 / 106,984,639. That combined figure is
itself the real all-funds total: p0063.txt:22 prints `Total Sources - All Funds
285,263,097 / 314,930,752 / 321,495,004 / 324,067,676`, the small differences
being General Fund transfers in (p0068.txt:17, 737,455) and the capital
4,125,627 named below. So 201,271,189 is NEITHER the Other-Funds total
(142.5M) NOR the all-funds total (285.3M): it sits between them and matches
neither in any column.

NO PUBLISHED DECOMPOSITION EXISTS. Three exhaustive searches, each requiring
agreement in ALL FOUR columns simultaneously, all returning zero solutions:
all subsets of the 21 citywide revenue-category aggregates; all subsets and all
SIGNED +/-1 combinations of a 29-item pool (fund-type totals, transfers out to
CIP, non-major revenues and transfers, total expenses, beginning balances); and
all 0/1/2-coefficient combinations of the 15 fund-type revenue and transfer-in
components, which is the level at which the book actually builds its totals.
Subset-sum on any SINGLE column is satisfiable -- the values are numerous and
small -- which is exactly why the four-column requirement is the honest test.

AND THE FIGURE OCCURS NOWHERE ELSE. `grep -r` over all 786 extracted pages of
all three documents finds 201,271,189 / 219,927,720 / 219,633,968 / 216,596,302
only on p0140.txt:52 and in its own geometry/p0140.json. The four GAP figures
(58,773,547 / 58,836,449 / 56,492,834 / 57,373,508) appear NOWHERE AT ALL.

Closest near-misses, all coincidences that fail another column badly, recorded
so nobody re-finds them and believes them: gap col 1 vs Other-Funds Charges for
Services FY23-24 58,881,835 (0.18% off, cols 2-4 miss by 4-18%); gap col 2 vs
the CIP five-year plan's FY2024-25 total 59,192,538 (cip p0218.txt:43, 0.6%
off); gap col 4 vs FY26-27 CIP-fund sources 58,988,871 (p0204.txt:19, 2.8%).

RESOLUTION: Rollup.Unassertable, which internal/mapping/rule.go:162-173 already
names this row and this bead for. NOT stated_total_deltas -- a $57M delta is not
the city's rounding, and fisc-2sd catches a STALE declaration but has no way to
catch a FICTIONAL one, which is the bead's own instruction.

A SECOND REASON THE ROLLUP CHANNEL IS THE ONLY ONE, found while checking this
and not previously recorded: a `covers` rollup over the 69 fund rules is
IMPOSSIBLE by construction, whatever p140's arithmetic turned out to be.
CheckRollup compares whole Column values including Column.Fund
(internal/mapping/resolve.go:1023, firstDifferingColumn at :1408-1428, landed
a3adb0e), and each of the 69 rules carries a different fund number. So
`unassertable` is not merely the honest route here, it is the available one.

WHAT THE INVESTIGATION ESTABLISHED POSITIVELY, which is the more useful half and
is NEW: pp.131-140 are a complete and internally exact schedule, corroborated by
two citywide pages the lane does not map. Summing the 69 fund totals BY FUND
GROUP against p0063.txt:16-21 (Table 2, Total Sources - All Funds):

  group             n   FY2024        FY2025        FY2026        FY2027
  enterprise        9   +1            tie           tie           tie
  capital          13   -1            -4,125,627    tie           tie
  debt-service      3   tie           tie           tie           tie
  permanent         1   tie           tie           tie           tie
  special-revenue  38   +2            +500          tie           tie
  internal-service  5   tie           tie           tie           tie

FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 TIE EXACTLY IN ALL SIX GROUPS -- the two columns
fisc-u2v's decision rests on. FY2023-24 ties within the document's own rounding
(+1/-1/+2, the same blocks fisc-2sd declares). FY2024-25 does NOT, and both
discrepancies are explained from published pages:

  - CAPITAL SHORT BY 4,125,627. p0194.txt:29 prints `General Fund CIP Reserves
    $34,954,363 | - | $4,125,627 | $39,079,990` and p0192.txt:14 carries it into
    the capital line as `Revenues 30,713,648 + Transfers In 4,125,627`. My sum of
    the 13 capital fund totals is 30,713,648 -- p192's REVENUES figure to the
    cent -- and NO capital fund on pp.132-134 prints a Transfers In row at all.
    So the money is a transfer into a fund pp.131-140 print no section for.
    p0198.txt:14 and p0204.txt:14 print `-` in that column, which is exactly why
    FY2026 and FY2027 tie. Filed separately.

  - SPECIAL REVENUE OVER BY 500. p0139.txt:56 prints `Oth Financing Source - |
    500 | - | -` in the Police Donations fund, and p63 Table 2 EXCLUDES it;
    p0192.txt:11 excludes it too (Revenues 18,980,619 + Transfers In 685,500 =
    19,666,119 against my 19,666,619). Two independent citywide schedules agree.
    This is the FIRST published evidence anywhere about where
    `other-financing-sources` lands in the citywide roll-up, and the answer is
    that it lands nowhere: data/taxonomy.yaml:279-289 says "which of the ten p66
    categories absorbs this line is not printed anywhere in the document" and
    marks the entry derived/UNGROUNDED. It can only ever be tested in FY2024-25,
    because the row is zero in both budget years and pp.66-67 print no revised
    column. Filed separately.

TWO LABELLED SPECULATIONS about the row itself, neither checkable in this
corpus, recorded so the next reader does not repeat the search: (a) the row is
stale, carried from the prior FY2023-25 book whose Other-Funds section covered a
different fund set -- that book is not in data/extracted; (b) it is an ERP query
over a wider account set (CIP, gross interfund activity) the book never
publishes.
close_reason:
Settled, no code. The gap has no published decomposition and the bead's own
fund-balance hypothesis is REFUTED: in FY2025-26 the non-General-Fund groups
collectively ADD $2.9M to fund balance against a +$56.5M gap. Adding the General
Fund overshoots by $83-107M and lands past p0063.txt:22's real all-funds total.
Three exhaustive searches -- all subsets of the citywide revenue aggregates, all
signed +/-1 combinations of a 29-item pool, all 0/1/2 combinations of the 15
fund-type components -- return zero solutions agreeing in all four columns, and
neither the printed vector nor the gap vector occurs anywhere in the 786-page
corpus.

Resolution is Rollup.Unassertable, which rule.go:162-173 already names this row
and this bead for; explicitly NOT stated_total_deltas. A second reason found on
the way, not previously recorded: a `covers` rollup over the 69 fund rules is
impossible by construction anyway, because CheckRollup compares whole Column
values including Column.Fund and each rule carries a different number. The YAML
entry lands with fisc-5gk.1.

The positive half is the more useful one and is new: pp.131-140 ARE complete and
internally exact, corroborated by two citywide pages the lane does not map. By
fund group against p0063 Table 2, FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 tie EXACTLY in all six
groups -- the two columns fisc-u2v's decision rests on -- and FY2023-24 ties
within fisc-2sd's rounding. FY2024-25 does not, and both discrepancies are
explained from published pages and filed: fisc-zl9 (capital short 4,125,627, a
transfer into General Fund CIP Reserves, a fund the schedule prints no section
for) and fisc-94b (special revenue over by $500, p139's Oth Financing Source,
which p0063 and p0192 both exclude -- the first published evidence about where
other-financing-sources lands in the roll-up, and the answer is nowhere).

title: counts-reconcile goes red with the tier hierarchy: the check package's duplicate netting
description:
internal/check holds a SECOND implementation of internal/project's cell netting
(internal/check/graph.go:836), and its own doc comment at graph.go:802-813 says
what happens when they diverge: "if the projection changes how it groups or nets
cells, the stock and zero counts derived here stop accounting for counts.facts
and the check FAILS".

fisc-gxa.2 changes exactly that grouping. Finest-grain links plus node.parent
population means the projection stops keying cells on
(kind, category, fundGroup) alone, so counts-reconcile goes RED in the same
commit that lands the tier hierarchy.

WHY THIS NEEDS ITS OWN ID. fisc-0ux's 2026-08-21 note names it -- "counts-
reconcile and the check package's netCells must be reworked in the same commit"
-- inside a note about the FIVE VACUOUS CHECKS, which is a list this defect is
not on. It is a sixth check going red, not a vacuous one going non-vacuous, and
nothing owns it. A landing plan built from the vacuous-check table does not
contain it.

SEQUENCING: this is not separable work. It lands INSIDE the fisc-oxf(b) +
fisc-gxa.2 + fisc-1wr.1.1 commit, because that commit is already indivisible --
aggregationInvariance.Run hard-errors the instant any node carries a parent
(graph.go:700-724), so the bump, the population and the fold cannot be
sequenced. This bead exists so the rework is REMEMBERED as part of that commit's
scope rather than discovered when verify goes red.

THE QUESTION WORTH ASKING WHILE DOING IT is whether the duplicate should exist
at all. The comment justifies it as an independent derivation -- a check that
recomputed the same way from the same code would assert nothing. That argument
is good and probably survives, but it should be re-stated against the v2 shape
rather than inherited: an independent derivation of a SIX-TIER fold is a
materially bigger thing to keep correct than an independent derivation of a
three-layer one.
acceptance_criteria: counts-reconcile PASSes over the v2 finest-grain graph; the check package's netting is reworked in the SAME commit as fisc-gxa.2; the reason for keeping an independent derivation is re-stated against the six-tier shape or the duplicate is removed with an argument

title: The department axis has no arithmetic check: fisc-u54's hole, one axis over
description:
fisc-u54 records the residual risk on the FUND axis: a fund number
mis-assigned within its own fund type survives every check. This is the same
hole on the DEPARTMENT axis, and it is worse, because the department axis has
no arithmetic check at all.

WHAT DOES NOT SEE IT.

- expenditure-detail-ties-to-spine (fisc-5gk.2's lane) keys on
  {kind, category, fund_group}. DEPARTMENT IS NOT IN THE KEY. Move the Planning
  division's four object rows from COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT to PUBLIC WORKS and
  every category sum is unchanged, so the tie still holds to the cent.
- factDepartmentsResolve (internal/check/vocabulary.go:121-193) checks slug
  SHAPE, one-spelling consistency, and collision against taxonomy categories --
  and, once fisc-o15's Go half lands, registry MEMBERSHIP. Every one of those is
  true of the wrong department.
- CheckTotals per division still ties, because the division's own printed Total
  covers exactly its own rows and never names its department.
- The 11 printed <DEPARTMENT> TOTAL rows WOULD catch it -- and they are exactly
  the totals that cannot be asserted today, because TotalRow is per Rule and a
  department spans several division rules. See the cross-rule rollup bead.

SO THE JOINT DISTRIBUTION fisc-5gk.2 EXISTS TO PUBLISH HAS ZERO ARITHMETIC
CHECK ON ITS DEPARTMENT AXIS. That is the whole point of the page: fisc-5gk.2's
description says pp.167-170 are the ONLY place the city publishes the
department-by-category joint rather than two marginals. Publishing a joint whose
one novel axis is unchecked is publishing the marginal with extra confidence.

NOT HYPOTHETICAL, and the shape is recorded on fisc-o15 already: two departments
whose name and sole division's name differ only in case (FIRE DEPARTMENT / Fire
Administration; GENERAL SERVICES / General Services), and City Manager carries
two divisions (City Manager, City Clerk) whose department attribution is a
judgment the rule author types by hand.

THE MITIGATION, and it is cheap because the evidence is printed: assert that the
divisions a department's rules claim sum to that department's printed
<DEPARTMENT> TOTAL row. That is the document checking our work on the department
axis, exactly as total_row does on the division axis. It DEPENDS ON the
cross-rule rollup capability -- which is the argument for building that rather
than declaring the 12 totals unassertable.

State plainly what it still does not catch: two divisions swapped BETWEEN two
departments whose totals both stay correct is impossible here (the sums move),
but a division attributed to the right department under the wrong SLUG SPELLING
is caught by factDepartmentsResolve, and a department registry entry whose
parent relation is itself wrong is not caught by anything. Say so rather than
claiming the mitigation is a fix -- fisc-u54's discipline.
acceptance_criteria: the divisions each department's rules claim sum to that department's printed <DEPARTMENT> TOTAL row; a division moved to the wrong department fails; the bead records what the mitigation still does not catch
close_reason:
Capability + failability proof land in 7be1523, riding on the rollups from 65c1627.

THE MITIGATION WORKS AND THE TEST PROVES THE OTHER HALF TOO. Moving City Clerk from CITY MANAGER to CITY ATTORNEY on p167's real figures is caught ONLY by the department rollup. The test asserts, rather than claims, that every other check stays green: each division's rows still tie to its own printed Total, and the category sums are identical figure for figure under both attributions -- which is why a tie keyed on {kind, category, fund_group} cannot see it.

WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT CATCH, per fisc-u54's discipline. A covers list wrong in a way that still sums correctly is not caught; that it is impossible here is a property of THESE FIGURES, not of the mechanism. A department registry entry whose parent relation is itself wrong is caught by nothing -- data/departments.yaml is fisc-o15 and does not exist.

THE PRODUCTION INSTANCE IS fisc-5gk.2'S, and this is a real scope limit rather than a deferral. A rollup requires every covered rule to print a total of its own, so the eleven <DEPARTMENT> TOTAL rows need the 23 division rules to exist. Requirement recorded on fisc-5gk.2.

title: Declared vacuity: --strict is unreachable for the whole backlog without it
description:
`fisc verify --strict` fails on Counts.Vacuous > 0 (internal/check/report.go
:158-163). Five checks are vacuous today, and traced against the code the last
of them -- transfer-legs-pair -- is not retired until fisc-aes, fisc-gkv,
fisc-9gh, fisc-4rh, fisc-8dz and fisc-5gk.3.1 have ALL landed.

So --strict is not a mid-course milestone that the two coverage lanes deliver.
It is the LAST thing in the backlog, and ci.yml:259-264 stays as it is for the
whole of it. fisc-1wr.4's own warning -- that a permanently red gate gets
commented out -- starts applying to the flag itself.

THE SHAPE THAT FIXES IT is the one this repo already uses three times:
unprojectedScopes (internal/check/coverage.go:25), StatedTotalDeltas, and
Part.OmittedRows. A declaration that is loud, that carries its reason, and that
FAILS WHEN IT GOES STALE.

  var declaredVacuous = map[string]struct{ reason, bead string }{...}

  - a check that reports VACUOUS and is NOT declared fails --strict;
  - a check that IS declared and reports something OTHER than vacuous also
    fails, with "remove the declaration" -- the self-retiring half, which is
    what stops the map outliving the work;
  - every run prints the declared set with its reasons, the way
    describeDeclared (coverage.go:145-156) prints unprojected scopes.

WHAT IT BUYS. CI can pass --strict from the moment the map is populated, and
each wave that retires a check DELETES ITS ENTRY as part of that wave rather
than as a bookkeeping pass at the end. The prose reason currently sitting in
ci.yml becomes a machine-checked one, and the gate cannot silently widen: an
undeclared vacuous check is a failure the day it appears.

NOTE WHAT THIS IS NOT. It does not promote a vacuous check to passing and it
does not weaken any check. A declared-vacuous check is still reported vacuous;
the declaration only says a human has looked at it and named the bead that
retires it. That is the same claim unprojectedScopes makes about facts.

Also note --full is NOT in the way: StatusSkipped never fails a report, so
source-pdfs-match-both-records does not need to be declared.
acceptance_criteria: an undeclared VACUOUS check fails --strict; a declared check that becomes non-vacuous ALSO fails, naming the declaration to remove; every run prints the declared set with reasons; ci.yml passes --strict and its prose reason is deleted because the machine now carries it
close_reason: Landed in 40943db. internal/check/vacuity.go carries declaredVacuous with three entries, each naming what would have to exist for its check to have a subject and the bead that deletes the entry; every run prints the set verbatim. An undeclared vacancy fails --strict; a declared check reporting anything else fails EITHER WAY, because that is a false statement in this package's source rather than a coverage shortfall. ci.yml passes --strict and its prose comment is deleted. TWO DEFECTS THE TESTS CAUGHT: treating 'this run held no such check' as stale broke every subset run (Run takes the slice it is given, so id validity is a claim about All() and is asserted statically); and the non-strict tally printed 'every one is declared' whenever anything was vacuous, including when nothing declared it. No count is pinned in any test, deliberately. fisc verify --strict: 27 passed, 0 failed, 3 vacuous (all declared), 1 skipped, exit 0.

title: Cross-rule rollup totals: 12 printed totals have no rule to be the total_row of
description:
TotalRow is a field on Rule (internal/mapping/rule.go:113-119) and CheckTotals
is per (rule, part). So a printed total that covers MORE THAN ONE RULE has no
rule to be the total_row OF, and cannot be asserted at all.

This is a different defect from fisc-w0o. There the rows of ONE block are split
across two parts. Here the rows belong to SEVERAL rules by design, because the
lane's row identity forces one rule per fund block (fisc-5gk.1) or one rule per
division (fisc-28s option A-prime).

THE UNASSERTABLE TOTALS, counted:

  Total General Fund            p0130.txt:40   spans pp.127-130's rules
  Total Sources                 p0140.txt:52   spans every rule on pp.131-140
  <DEPARTMENT> TOTAL   x11      pp.167-170     spans that department's divisions
  General Fund Total Expenses   p0170.txt:23   spans all 23 division rules

fisc-o15's 2026-08-21 note (2) counts the 11 <DEPARTMENT> TOTAL rows and the
General Fund Total Expenses row among the "35 total_row assertions" that the
84 printed rows on pp.167-170 decompose into. THEY ARE NOT ACHIEVABLE. Of the
35, 23 are assertable (the division Totals) and 12 are not.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A COUNTING NIT. The department-level total is
the only printed figure that would catch a division filed under the wrong
department -- see the department-axis check bead. Losing it silently is how a
missing check becomes invisible.

TWO ACCEPTABLE ANSWERS, and the unacceptable one is silence.

(a) Build rollup assertion: a declaration that names the rules a printed total
    covers, checked after all of them resolve.
(b) Decide not to, and add a reason string to pkg/cmd/build/report.go:65-78 --
    something in the shape of reasonDocumentPrintsARollup -- so the build
    report SAYS the document prints a total this rule structure cannot assert.
    That is checkable and readable; reasonNoTotalRow is neither, because it
    means "the rule declares none", which is a different claim.

WHAT IS NOT ACCEPTABLE is leaving the 12 counted as assertions in a bead note
while the build reports nothing.

Watch p0167.txt:61-62, which prints the department total as
"INNOVATION & ECONOMIC DEVELOPEMENT $..." on one line and "TOTAL" on the next,
with the city's own typo. Whatever shape (a) takes has to survive that.
acceptance_criteria: every printed total on a mapped page is either asserted or reported by the build with a reason that says the DOCUMENT prints a rollup this rule structure cannot assert; fisc-o15's count of 35 expenditure total_row assertions is corrected to 23 assertable + 12 not
close_reason:
Rollups land in 65c1627. Both acceptance criteria met, and the design decision changed during peer review of the plan.

THE DECISION: A ROLLUP SUMS THE COVERED RULES' STATED TOTALS, NOT THEIR ROWS. The plan's first draft summed leaves. Measured on p168, that is wrong: ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES object rows give 6,311,563 against a printed 6,311,564, because Finance's own $1 is absorbed by its printed division Total and reappears one level up. General Fund Total Expenses on p170 ties against leaves too, but ONLY because that page's four declared deltas net to zero -- so a leaf-summing rollup ties or fails depending on whether the city's roundings cancel, and the author's only escape is a delta at the rollup level absorbing a structural artefact. That is fisc-w0o's fabricated-declaration hazard one level up. Summing stated totals makes a two-level chain where neither level absorbs the other's residue, and it is why a covered rule must print a total of its own.

TestARollupSumsPrintedTotalsAndNotLeaves is written so the wrong implementation cannot pass: swapped to sum Values it fails by exactly $1.

TOTAL SOURCES IS NOT ASSERTABLE, correcting this bead's own list of twelve. fisc-wev has measured that p140's Total Sources exceeds the pages it closes by ~$57M, differently per column. It takes answer (b) -- Rollup.Unassertable, which carries the reason into the build report -- and stays blocked on fisc-wev. So the twelve split into eleven-plus-one assertable-in-principle and one declared, not twelve of one kind.

TWO /code-review FINDINGS FIXED IN THE SAME COMMIT, both with regression tests proven to fail without the fix: CheckRollup PANICKED (index out of range) where a covered rule's total-bearing part was not its first, because the column width came from Parts[0] and the totals from the bearing part; and 'unassertable' was compared trimmed by the parser and untrimmed by the build, so a whitespace-only reason validated as 'no reason' then suppressed the check as 'a reason'.

title: Rule-level multi-part CheckTotals: nine blocks straddle a page break and neither exit works
description:
Both coverage lanes need a printed total that spans two Parts, and there is NO
fallback. `CheckTotals(rule, p)` sums ONE part over ONE page
(internal/mapping/resolve.go:794-854), so a block whose rows straddle a page
break has its rows in two parts and its printed total in only one.

NINE BLOCKS, measured, across both lanes:

pp.127-140 (fisc-5gk.1), six: Other Taxes (p127->128), Contributions
Outsourced (p129->130), State - Gas Tax (p133->134), City Street Sweeping Fee
(p137->138), Open Space Acquisition & Mgmt (p138->139), General Liability
(p139->140).

pp.167-170 (fisc-5gk.2), three, ALL of the page breaks in that lane: General
Services (p167->168), Special Operations (p168->169), Environmental Services
(p169->170). Concretely, p0170.txt:7 prints `Services & Supplies 132,186`
against `Total $134,242` on :9; the $2,056 Wages & Benefits row is on p169.

BOTH EXITS FAIL, which is why this is capability and not a preference.

(a) Keep total_row on a straddling rule. The head part hits resolve.go:686-691
    -> ErrNotFound, which pkg/cmd/build/report.go:118-124 routes to `default:`
    -> a hard build failure. The tail part sums only its own rows and fails
    CheckTotals.

(b) Drop total_row. Both parts then report reasonNoTotalRow, "the rule declares
    no total_row" -- and report.go:65-78 states in its OWN comment that neither
    reason string says the document prints no total, because "that is a claim
    about the source, and only a human reading the page can make it". Using it
    here is precisely the misreport that comment guards against.

THE HAZARD THAT MAKES THIS URGENT. With both exits closed, the rule author's
cheapest remaining escape is a stated_total_deltas entry equal to the head
page's sum -- a FABRICATED declaration of "the city's rounding" absorbing a
structural gap. fisc-2sd catches a STALE declaration (one that now ties
exactly) but has no way to catch a FICTIONAL one. This is fisc-u2v DEFECT 4.

SHAPE. `total_spans_parts: true` on Rule, making CheckTotals sum Values across
all the rule's parts and compare against whichever part prints the total.

FAIL CLOSED AT PARSE TIME if the parts do not share an identical Columns list.
That is what stops it being applied to the p66-67 spine, whose parts partition
COLUMNS (p66 four-wide, p67 eight-wide) rather than ROWS -- summing across
those parts would be meaningless and the parser should say so rather than
producing a number.
acceptance_criteria: a rule may declare its printed total spans its parts; CheckTotals sums across parts and ties; the parser REFUSES the flag when the parts' Columns lists differ, with a test naming spine-revenues; a synthetic two-part single-column fixture ties only with the flag
close_reason:
Rule.TotalSpansParts lands in ee05b55, with CheckSpanningTotals summing across parts and comparing once.

All four acceptance criteria met. The spine guard is proved by MUTATING THE PUBLISHED RULE FILE rather than a fixture -- TestTheSpineCannotDeclareItsTotalSpansItsParts adds the flag to spine-revenues and asserts the parser refuses it, naming the 4-vs-8 column mismatch.

TWO REFUSALS MOVED TO RESOLVE TIME, and the bead did not anticipate this. 'exactly one part prints the total row' and 'a declared delta sits on the total-bearing part' are claims about the PAGES, and the parser has none. It refuses what it can see without them (no total_row, a single part, non-identical Columns, two parts declaring a delta); the resolver refuses the rest. Splitting them was the alternative to the parser guessing, which is the fail-open this flag exists to close.

REPORT ACCOUNTING, worth recording because it is easy to get wrong later. A spanning rule credits EVERY part it covers (the one comparison corroborates every row the rule maps), while ColumnsTied stays the number of comparisons MADE. So a build with spanning rules can report more parts checked than columns tied. SpanningRulesChecked is reported so that reads as arithmetic rather than as a bug.

NOT YET APPLIED TO A PRODUCTION RULE. The nine straddling blocks live on pp.127-140 and pp.167-170, which are fisc-5gk.1 and fisc-5gk.2; this is the capability they were blocked on. facts.jsonl byte-identical, fisc verify unchanged.

The production-shape fixture is inline rather than copied from data/extracted: testdata/ carries no pp.169-170 pair yet, and adding one owes both substrates plus a README entry per testdata/README.md. That is the lane's own fixture work.

title: One graph cannot hold two scopes, so the tier hierarchy and the scope axis are mutually exclusive as designed
description:
fisc-u2v's decision puts the detail schedules in their own scopes so netCells
cannot sum them with the spine. fisc-gxa.2 wants ONE graph carrying tiers 0-5.
Those two cannot both be true under the current projection model, and nothing in
either bead says so.

THE MECHANICS. project.Options.Scope is ONE string and selectFacts
(internal/project/sankey.go:511-519) filters on f.Scope == o.Scope, exact
equality. internal/check/subject.go factSlices builds slices only where
f.Scope == spineScope, and buildProjections hard-errors if that yields nothing.

SO THE TWO HORNS ARE:
- Merge the scopes into one projection. netCells then sums both sides into
  {kind, category, fundGroup} and the published General Fund revenue is
  128,287,524. This is fisc-u2v verbatim, re-opened at the projection layer.
- Keep them separate. The site fetches two documents; aggregation-invariance has
  nothing to fold ACROSS tiers in either; and constraint-tier-vocabulary cannot
  go non-vacuous, because a constraint tier is a property of a FUND and the
  fund-group column of the spine graph contains funds of several tiers.

Either way, tier 3 (fund/<n>) nodes come only from revenue-by-fund while tier 2
(fund group) and the whole expenditure side come only from all-funds-gross.

WHAT TO SETTLE
- whether a projection may select MORE THAN ONE scope, and if so what stops it
  summing them -- the cell key would have to carry the axis that distinguishes
  them (fund and department are absent from cellKey today, sankey.go:339-343);
- or whether the finest-grain graph EXCLUDES the spine facts it duplicates,
  which is a different answer with a different failure mode (the spine becomes
  underivable from the published document);
- what changes in internal/check: factSlices, spineScope, and
  publishedProjectionBuilt all assume one published scope. fisc-gxa.2 currently
  attributes none of this to itself.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROADMAP: aggregation-invariance and
constraint-tier-vocabulary cannot go non-vacuous until this is decided, so
`fisc verify --strict` cannot be the CI gate on the schedule fisc-0ux's
five-checks table implies.

Found in peer review of the landing plan, 2026-08-21.
acceptance_criteria: a decision recorded here on whether a projection may span scopes; if it may, what keeps netCells from summing them; the internal/check changes (factSlices, spineScope, publishedProjectionBuilt) are named and owned
notes:
2026-08-22 DECIDED, with a correction to both horns as this bead states them.
Every figure below was measured off data/extracted or produced by running the
code in a scratch test and then reverted; the runs are recorded at the end.

THE ANSWER IN ONE LINE. A projection MAY select more than one scope. It may
NOT select the spine scope together with any scope that reconciles to it, and
the reconciliation check fisc-u2v already commits to is exactly the certificate
that says which scopes those are.

FIRST, A CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN FIGURE

"netCells then sums both sides into {kind, category, fundGroup} and the
published General Fund revenue is 128,287,524" -- 128,287,524 is the General
Fund PROPERTY-TAX CELL doubled, not GF revenue. Verified by summing p0127's
thirteen detail rows in the FY 2025-26 column (62,067,470 + 458,394 -
15,175,000 - 1,810,339 + 2,383,306 + 34,310 + 1,397,250 + 12,143,966 + 545,116
+ 495,778 + 1,105,094 + 220,455 + 277,962 = 64,143,762) against
p0066.txt:13 "Property Taxes 64,143,762". GF total revenue is
p0066.txt:23 $157,873,470; the whole-scope merge would put it at 315,746,940,
less the one declared transfer-in asymmetry.

WHAT THE MECHANICS ACTUALLY DO -- RUN, NOT READ

(1) FUND IS INVISIBLE TO netCells, AND SILENTLY SO. sankey.go:525-543 guards
three fields before keying: empty Category, non-empty Department, empty
FundGroup. There is NO guard on Fund, and Fund is not in cellKey
(sankey.go:339-343). Scratch run: spine fixture ++ the thirteen p127 rows
carrying Fund: 100, Scope mutated to all-funds-gross. Result:

  link revenue/taxes/property -> fund-group/general = 12,828,752,400 cents
  citing 14 fact ids; nodes = 25, links = 58; headline gross revenue
  36,411,276,900 against the golden file's 29,996,900,700.

Node and link COUNTS ARE UNCHANGED. The merged graph is structurally
indistinguishable from the correct one. This is fisc-u2v's hazard reproduced
at the projection layer and it is the reason this bead exists.

(2) THE DEPARTMENT GUARD IS THE ONLY THING THAT FAILS LOUDLY. Same scratch
run with Department set:
  sankey: fact dept (... p127 "dept") carries department "police"
So a p167 fact reaching the spine is a hard error today and a p127 fact is
not. sankey.go:535-537's hint already says "check the scope the projection was
asked for" -- that guard is this decision, half-written, for one axis only.

(3) PUTTING fund IN cellKey IS INERT TODAY AND INSUFFICIENT TOMORROW.
Scratch patch adding `fund int` to cellKey, to the netCells key expression and
to sortedCellKeys: `go test ./internal/project/ ./internal/check/` passes
unchanged, golden file byte-identical. Every one of the 240 committed facts
carries fund 0 (facts/facts.jsonl, counted), so the key change costs nothing
now. But with the tier-2 endpoint left alone it produces
  sankey: two links from "revenue/taxes/property" to "fund-group/general"
from checkDistinctLinks (sankey.go:696-705). The key change is therefore
INSEPARABLE from the endpoint change: a fund-keyed cell must land on a
fund/<n> node or the graph refuses to build. That refusal is the good news.

(4) THE BAD NEWS, AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDES THIS BEAD. Scratch patch
with fund in cellKey AND a tier-3 endpoint (fund/100, tier 3) for cells whose
fund is non-zero. The graph builds:

  revenue/taxes/property -> fund-group/general        = 6,414,376,200
  revenue/taxes/property -> fund-group/special-revenue =   531,565,200
  revenue/taxes/property -> fund/100                   = 6,414,376,200
  headline gross revenue = 36,411,276,900   (spine alone: 29,996,900,700)
  nodes 26, links 59

THE CELL KEY DOES NOT FIX THE HEADLINE. Headline.AllFundsGrossRevenueCents
accumulates per CELL (sankey.go:393, and 404/412/418 for the other four), so
splitting one cell into two adds both. And headline-ties-to-facts
(check/graph.go:407-445) re-sums every revenue fact in the projection's slice,
so it agrees with the doubled figure and reports green. Worse for a reader:
revenue/taxes/property now has two outbound links carrying the same
$64,143,762, so d3 draws that source node at twice its true width -- a visual
double-count no per-link check sees.

THE GENERALISATION: A HEADLINE IS A PROPERTY OF A SINGLE-GRAIN DOCUMENT. The
moment one document holds two grains of the same money, "the total" is
ambiguous, and NO cell key can disambiguate it, because the ambiguity is not
in the key -- it is in the accumulation. Both horns as this bead states them
miss that. Horn (a) is not "extend the key"; it is "extend the key AND make
the endpoints tier-aware AND make every headline accumulator tier-aware AND
teach headline-ties-to-facts which grain it is summing", four changes, of
which this bead names one.

SO THE HORNS ARE NOT WHAT THE BEAD SAYS THEY ARE

The bead's horn (a) assumes any two scopes in one projection collide. They do
not. Collision requires the same address in the projection's key space, and
the three schedules on the table are related three different ways:

  pp.127-140 revenue-by-fund  vs  pp.167-170 department x object
      DISJOINT BY KIND. Every key in cellKey carries kind, so a revenue cell
      and an expenditure cell can never collide. Also disjoint by grain: one
      is (category, fund), the other (department, object).

  either detail scope  vs  pp.66-67 all-funds-gross
      NOT DISJOINT. Each is a COMPLETE, EXACT restatement of one side of the
      spine. fisc-u2v measured that for revenue (all six fund groups, both
      budget years, to the cent). The same holds for expenditure and it is
      measured here for the first time: the eleven department totals on
      pp.167-170 -- 230,858 + 4,866,242 + 2,836,845 + 8,056,553 + 4,103,812
      (Innovation & Economic Development, whose TOTAL wraps to its own line)
      + 10,869,461 + 29,540,677 + 53,114,421 + 20,698,719 + 3,646,504 +
      6,686,710 -- sum to 144,650,802, which is p0170:23 "General Fund Total
      Expenses $144,650,802" and p0066.txt:32 "TOTAL EXPENDITURES:
      $144,650,802". p0172 prints the SAME money a third time by object
      category alone (81,801,011 / 62,849,791 / - / -), identical to p66's
      four GF expenditure rows.

THE DECISION

A. project.Options.Scope becomes a SET (Options.Scopes []string), and
   selectFacts (sankey.go:511-519) tests membership rather than equality.

B. TWO SCOPES MAY BE SELECTED TOGETHER ONLY IF NOTHING RECONCILES ONE TO THE
   OTHER. The rule is not a new cellKey field and must not be written as one,
   because (4) above proves a key alone does not close it. The rule is:
   a scope carrying a `<x>-ties-to-spine` check is BY THAT VERY FACT
   ineligible to appear in a projection alongside the spine scope -- a
   reconciliation identity IS the statement that two scopes are the same
   money. fisc-u2v's revenue-detail-ties-to-spine is the first such
   certificate; fisc-1wr.2's expenditure clause is the second.

   Encode it as a declaration, not a convention: each projection declares its
   scope set, and a tier-1 check asserts no declared set contains two scopes
   that a reconciliation check relates. Fail closed on ambiguity -- an
   undeclared pair is an error, not a pass.

C. Sankey KEEPS EXACTLY ONE SCOPE and errors on len(Scopes) != 1. sankey.json
   stays schema v1, metadata.scope stays a string, testdata/sankey.golden.json
   stays byte-identical, and the headline stays unambiguous because the
   document that publishes it has one grain. The finest-grain graph is a
   SECOND Projection type with its own key, its own document, and NO headline.

D. THE FINEST-GRAIN DOCUMENT SELECTS {revenue-by-fund, gf-department-object}
   AND NOT the spine. This is the bead's third possibility, and its stated
   failure mode does not bite in this form: the spine facts are still
   projected -- by sankey.json -- so they are neither dropped from the
   published corpus nor pushed into unprojectedScopes. What IS true is the
   weaker version: within the finest-grain document, the tier-2 fund-group
   figure is OUR fold of tier-3 links, not the city's printed cell, so a
   reader of that one file cannot check our arithmetic against p66-67. That
   is acceptable, and only because both documents ship: the printed figure is
   in sankey.json, and the equality between them is proved per cell at zero
   tolerance by revenue-detail-ties-to-spine, which reads Subject.Facts and
   needs no graph at all. It would NOT be acceptable if sankey.json were
   retired in favour of the tier document. Do not do that.

WHY THIS DOES NOT COST THE TWO CHECKS -- THE BEAD'S HORN (b) IS WRONG HERE

constraint-tier-vocabulary GOES NON-VACUOUS. The bead's argument -- "a
constraint tier is a property of a FUND while the spine graph's column is a
fund GROUP" -- is an argument against putting constraint_tier on the SPINE,
which nobody needs to do. The finest-grain document's tier-3 nodes ARE funds.
data/funds.yaml lists 112 of them and 111 carry a tier (measured:
restricted-by-law 95, committed 14, unknown 2, discretionary 1), and
registry.ConstraintTier (registry.go:261-263) already answers per fund. The
~71 funds pp.127-140 print (70 `Total <fund>` rows on pp.131-140 plus the
General Fund on pp.127-130) each get one, and check/graph.go:750-777 has
subjects for the first time.
   Two things travel with it. ConstraintTier is DERIVED
(registry.go:80-84, 158-160), so a tier-1 node needs derived: true plus a
rationale and a source_note or derived-nodes-justified fails -- the same bar
the two fund-balance nodes clear (sankey.go:129-146). And the layer is nearly
degenerate: one fund is discretionary and 95 are restricted-by-law, so tier 1
is four nodes with the General Fund alone on one of them. That is a true and
useful picture, but it is not a rich tier and the roadmap should not price it
as one.

aggregation-invariance GOES NON-VACUOUS TOO, and with real evidence on both
sides, PROVIDED the tier-3 node's parent is taken from data/funds.yaml `type:`
rather than copied off the fact's fund_group. Those are two independent
records of one claim: pp.131-140 print exactly six fund-type section headers
(measured: Enterprise / Capital / Debt Service / Special Revenue / Internal
Service / Permanent, one each) and the fact's fund_group comes from the
section a row sits under, while funds.yaml's `type:` is transcribed from the
appendix pp.253-257. Fold tier 3 into tier 2 by node.parent, compare against
the fact-derived fund_group sums, and mis-parenting Airport to capital moves
$4,739,507 (p0131:20 Total Airport FY 2025-26) and reddens the check. If
parent is copied from fund_group instead, the fold is a tautology -- say so
in fisc-1wr.1.1 when the fold is written.
   The bead assumed the only possible fold is finest-grain against the
published coarse total. That fold IS cross-scope, and it is already owned, per
cell and at zero tolerance, by revenue-detail-ties-to-spine. Rebuilding it as
a graph check buys nothing and costs the four-part redesign in (4).

WHAT CHANGES IN internal/check, AND WHO OWNS EACH

The exact-equality assumption lives in FOUR places, not three:
  1. internal/project/sankey.go:514  selectFacts
  2. internal/check/subject.go:531   factSlices
  3. internal/check/graph.go:795     factsFor (the check's own re-selection)
  4. internal/check/coverage.go:63   publishedProjectionBuilt
Any change to Options.Scope touches all four, and (3) is the one this bead's
acceptance criteria omit.

spineScope (subject.go:45) -- today `const spineScope = project.PublishedScope`,
one package-level string. It becomes a per-projection property: project.
Projection grows a declaration of the scope set it is of, and check reads it
from there. The doc comment at subject.go:39-45 stays TRUE and must not be
deleted -- "a reference rather than a copy" is still the point; there is just
one reference per projection instead of one for the package.
  OWNER: fisc-gxa.2. It attributes none of this to itself today and it is the
  bead that lands the second projection.

factSlices (subject.go:524-551) -- today it filters `f.Scope == spineScope`
and stamps that one scope onto every Options it returns. It becomes a grouping
over (fiscal year, basis, scope-set-of-the-projection). TWO TRAPS:
  - buildProjections (subject.go:488-521) builds the CARTESIAN PRODUCT
    len(ps) x len(slices). With a second projection and a second scope that
    would build the Sankey over revenue-by-fund. Today that hard-errors on the
    department guard only if a department fact is present; for pp.127-140 it
    would BUILD, silently, and produce exactly the doubled graph measured in
    (1). The product must stop being a product in the same change.
  - the len(slices) == 0 refusal (subject.go:494-501) must become PER
    PROJECTION and must name which projection wanted which scope. A single
    global refusal goes quiet the moment one projection has facts and another
    does not, which is the mistyped-scope failure the refusal exists to stop,
    one level up.
  OWNER: fisc-gxa.2.

publishedProjectionBuilt (coverage.go:38-84) -- today it asserts ONE triple
(project.PublishedFiscalYear, PublishedBasis, PublishedScope). With two
published documents it must assert one slice PER published document, and its
doc comment ("`fisc export` publishes exactly (...)") stops being true and
must be rewritten rather than extended. The published set moves from three
constants (project.go:63-67) to a declaration per projection.
  OWNER: fisc-gxa.2 for the check; the constants move with it.

factsAreProjected / unprojectedScopes (coverage.go:25, 107-131) -- UNCHANGED
by this decision, and that is the point of consistency with fisc-u2v. Its one
entry for revenue-by-fund lands with fisc-5gk.1, and retires by its own
stale-declaration branch the moment the finest-grain projection selects the
scope. Nothing here weakens or pre-empts that. Note the entry cannot be made
row-level: the map is keyed by SCOPE, so "exclude these 120 of 240
all-funds-gross facts" is inexpressible -- which is a second, independent
reason the finest-grain document must not try to swallow the spine.

cellKey -- internal/project/sankey.go:339-343 stays THREE fields, because
Sankey stays single-scope and single-grain. internal/check/graph.go:827-831
carries a deliberate second copy (graph.go:802-813) and also stays. The
finest-grain projection brings its own key and its own netting, and
counts-reconcile then needs one netting per projection rather than one for the
package.
  OWNER: fisc-ix2, which already names "the check package's duplicate
  netting" and is correct to.

MIXED GRAIN IS UNAVOIDABLE, WHICH IS A SECOND REASON fisc-gxa.2's "ONE GRAPH,
TIERS 0-5" IS NOT ACHIEVABLE AS WRITTEN

Expenditure has no tier-3 counterpart for most of the city. pp.167-170 are
General Fund only (p0167:3 "General Fund Expenditures by Major Category"), 11
departments and 23 divisions. pp.72-75 give a per-fund Expenses column but
only for major funds -- p0074 lists 17 named funds and then one line, "Total
Non-Major Funds", for everything else. So the finest-grain document is
tier 0->3 on the whole revenue side, tier 3->4->5 on the General Fund
expenditure side, and tier 2 on enterprise/capital/special-revenue/
internal-service expenditure. node.tier and node.parent must carry that, and
the client's "render tiers 0,1,2,3" toggle must handle a branch that bottoms
out early. Neither this bead nor fisc-gxa.2 says so.

INCIDENTAL FINDING, WORTH ITS OWN BEAD. pp.72-75 publish a citywide revenue
total that does NOT agree with pp.66-67. p0074:52 "Total All Funds:
$310,669,663" for FY 2026-27 against the spine's six columns summing to
302,443,043 (164,358,147 + 70,308,250 + 26,888,254 + 0 + 20,892,522 +
19,995,870) -- a delta of 8,226,620 whose cause is not established here. Two
published citywide totals that differ by $8.2M is the strongest possible
argument that a projection selects a SCHEDULE and not a subject, and it is
also a trap for anyone who maps pp.68-75 "because it is by fund". pp.68-75 are
in no bead today.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, STATED FAIRLY

fisc-gxa.2's default General Fund view is tiers 0,3,4 (+5 on drill-down). That
crosses pp.127-130 and pp.167-170 -- two schedules, two scopes -- so the
default view genuinely requires a projection that spans scopes, and anyone
arguing that a projection must select exactly one scope has to explain how
that view is drawn. This decision agrees with them and that is why (A) says
yes. What it refuses is only the pairing that restates the same money.

The harder version of the objection is about the READER, not the code: the
site's pitch is following one dollar from source to spend, and two documents
means the reader cannot see $157,873,470 arrive from 71 detail lines and leave
through 11 departments in one picture without a client-side join across two
fetches, which no check covers. That is real. It is answered by observing that
the join is not across the two DOCUMENTS -- the finest-grain document already
holds both sides of the General Fund, because revenue-by-fund and
gf-department-object are disjoint and travel together. The spine document is
the citywide overview and the tier document is the drill-down; they are two
views, not two halves of one view. If that turns out to be wrong when the
thing is drawn, the fallback is (4)'s four-part redesign, and it should be
re-opened here rather than improvised at the keyboard.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SOLVE

- The site fetches one document. site/app.js fetches only
  CONFIG.projections[CONFIG.primary]. internal/export already writes
  data/<stem>.json per projection (export.go:200) and page.go already
  emits the projections map plus a primary (page.go's buildPage), so the PACKAGER
  needs nothing -- but the second fetch, the toggle and the empty/error states
  are new client work, and fisc-gxa.3 is closed. That needs a bead.
- Nothing here says how a tier-3 fund node's LABEL is chosen, or what a fund
  with no funds.yaml entry does (fisc-nne: Police Evidence, p136, has none in
  any spelling). Blocking on fisc-5gk.1 as before.
- Nothing here decides p76's scope. fisc-5gk.3.1 still owns it and fisc-u2v
  says so.
- Nothing here decides whether tier 0 is the ten (eleven -- fisc-u2v defect 3)
  categories or the line items. fisc-u2v recommends the categories; this
  decision is compatible with either and does not settle it.
- graph-acyclic: a tier hierarchy with node.parent introduces a second edge
  kind the acyclicity check does not currently know about. Unexamined here.
- The four-fold cost of the multi-scope refusal itself: the check in (B) is
  new code with no owner named above. It should land with fisc-gxa.2, and if
  fisc-gxa.2 is split, it goes with whichever half changes Options.

VERIFICATION OF THIS NOTE'S OWN FIGURES

Pages, read directly:
  p0066.txt:13  Property Taxes (General Fund) FY 2025-26  64,143,762
  p0066.txt:23  TOTAL REVENUES: $157,873,470
  p0066.txt:32  TOTAL EXPENDITURES: $144,650,802
  p0127.txt:11-35  thirteen detail rows, summed = 64,143,762
  p0127.txt:37  Total Property Taxes ... $64,143,762
  p0131.txt:20  Total Airport ... $4,739,507
  p0167-p0170  eleven department TOTAL lines, summed = 144,650,802
  p0170.txt:23  General Fund Total Expenses ... $144,650,802
  p0172.txt  Total General Fund $144,650,802; four object rows = p66's
  p0074.txt:52 Total All Funds: ... $310,669,663
  pp.131-140  six fund-type section headers, one each; 70 `Total <fund>` rows
Repo state:
  facts/facts.jsonl -- 240 facts, all scope all-funds-gross, all fund 0, all
  department "", pages 66 (80) and 67 (160)
  testdata/sankey.golden.json -- nodes 25, links 58, headline gross revenue
  29,996,900,700
  data/funds.yaml -- 112 funds; constraint_tier restricted-by-law 95,
  committed 14, unknown 2, discretionary 1
Code runs: three scratch tests in internal/project, each with the patch
described at (1), (3) and (4), run and then REVERTED. Nothing in this note's
code figures is inferred from reading; `go test ./internal/project/
./internal/check/` was green under the (3) patch with the golden file
untouched, and the two error strings quoted are verbatim from the runs.

CONFIDENCE. High on the mechanics and the arithmetic -- those were run and
measured. Medium on (D), the two-document split, because it trades a reader
question for a code guarantee and the reader question is not answerable from
this repository. If the repo owner's view is that one picture is the product,
(4) is the price and it should be paid deliberately, in fisc-oxf, rather than
discovered.
2026-08-22 POINT D IS FLAGGED FOR THE OWNER AND NOT DECIDED. The decision note
above recommends that the finest-grain graph be a SECOND document with no
headline, rather than one graph carrying tiers 0-5.

Points A, B and C of that note are engineering conclusions backed by
measurement -- in particular that adding `fund` to cellKey still publishes a
doubled headline (36,411,276,900 against the golden 29,996,900,700) and that
headline-ties-to-facts reports GREEN on the wrong number, because it re-sums the
same facts the headline was accumulated from. Those stand however D goes.

D does not. It trades a reader question -- "is one picture, source to spend, the
product?" -- for a code guarantee, and that question is not answerable from this
repository. fisc-gxa.2's pitch is one picture; this answer gives two documents
and a client-side join that no check covers.

WAVES THAT DO NOT DEPEND ON IT: the revenue lane (fisc-5gk.1) and the
expenditure lane (fisc-5gk.2) are unaffected either way -- both publish facts at
their own scope and are reconciled by fact-level checks that read Subject.Facts
rather than any graph. Only the tier-hierarchy commit (fisc-gxa.2 + fisc-oxf(b)
+ fisc-1wr.1.1 + fisc-ix2) consumes the answer.

So the honest state is: decidable later at no cost to the coverage lanes, and
better decided against a chart that exists than against one that does not.
2026-08-23 REVIEWED AND CLOSED ON ITS ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. Points A, B and C
stand; point D is SPLIT OUT to fisc-l25 rather than closed with them.

WHY CLOSE. The three clauses this bead asks for are answered:
  - whether a projection may span scopes -- YES (A: Options.Scopes as a set,
    selectFacts tests membership);
  - what keeps netCells from summing them -- (B) a scope carrying an
    <x>-ties-to-spine check is BY THAT FACT ineligible to sit in a projection
    beside the spine scope, declared per projection and asserted by a tier-1
    check, failing closed on an undeclared pair. Explicitly NOT a new cellKey
    field, and (4) is the measurement proving a key alone cannot close it;
  - the internal/check changes named and owned -- and the note found a FOURTH
    site these acceptance criteria omitted.

RE-VERIFIED TODAY, independently, before closing. Every repo-state and page
figure in the note holds:
  facts/facts.jsonl -- 240 facts, ALL scope all-funds-gross, ALL fund 0, ALL
    department "", pages 66 (80) and 67 (160). So (3)'s claim that adding
    `fund` to cellKey is inert today is structurally true, not just observed.
  testdata/sankey.golden.json -- nodes 25, links 58,
    all_funds_gross_revenue_cents 29,996,900,700,
    transfer_residual_cents 3,808,673,700.
  data/funds.yaml -- constraint_tier restricted-by-law 95, committed 14,
    unknown 2, discretionary 1. Exactly as the note says, so the tier-1 layer
    really is four nodes with the General Fund alone on one, and the roadmap
    should not price it as a rich tier.
  The four exact-equality sites, read at the lines given: sankey.go:514,
    subject.go:531, graph.go:795, coverage.go:63. All four test
    f.Scope == o.Scope (or == spineScope). project.go:87 Scope is one string.
  pp.167-170 -- the ELEVEN department TOTAL lines, FY2025-26, sum to
    144,650,802: 230,858 + 4,866,242 + 2,836,845 + 8,056,553 + 4,103,812
    (p0167:60, whose heading is wrapped AND misspelled 'DEVELOPEMENT') +
    3,646,504 + 6,686,710 + 53,114,421 + 20,698,719 + 10,869,461 + 29,540,677.
    Equals p0170:23 and p0066.txt:32.
  p0074:52 Total All Funds 310,669,663 against the spine's six FY2026-27
    columns summing to 302,443,043 -- delta 8,226,620, filed as fisc-zs5.

TWO THINGS THIS BEAD SAID WERE NEEDED HAD NOT BEEN FILED, and both are now:
  fisc-l25 -- point D, the owner's product question. It is a real blocker on
    fisc-gxa.2 and is wired as one, so closing this bead does not silently
    remove it.
  fisc-f75 -- the second fetch, the toggle and the empty/error states. This
    bead's own 'WHAT THIS DOES NOT SOLVE' says 'That needs a bead'; fisc-gxa.3
    is closed and nothing else owned it.

AND fisc-gxa.2 HAD NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA AT ALL, which made 'named and owned'
half true -- the owner was named here and recorded nowhere the owner would read.
It now carries all four equality sites, the spineScope and buildProjections
changes, the per-projection len(slices)==0 refusal, point B's multi-scope check
(unowned until now), the single-scope Sankey guard with the golden file
byte-identical, the mixed-grain node.tier/node.parent requirement, and the
funds.yaml-not-fund_group parenting rule without which aggregation-invariance is
a tautology.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS: whether one picture is the product. See fisc-l25.
close_reason: Points A, B and C decided and independently re-verified 2026-08-23: a projection may select multiple scopes (Options.Scopes as a set), two scopes related by a reconciliation check may not sit in one projection, Sankey stays single-scope. All three acceptance clauses met; a fourth equality site (graph.go:795) was found beyond them and is now recorded on fisc-gxa.2 along with the rest. Point D split to fisc-l25 as an owner decision and wired as a real blocker on fisc-gxa.2; the client second-fetch work filed as fisc-f75.

title: transfer-legs-pair cannot be retired by mapping p76: no link can carry a transfer_id
description:
fisc-0ux names transfer-legs-pair as one of five vacuous checks and says fisc-4rh
plus fisc-5gk.3.1 retire it. Measured: THEY CANNOT, and the gap is unfiled work
in internal/project rather than anything either bead owns.

WHY. The check reads LINKS OF BUILT GRAPHS, not facts:
- internal/check/graph.go:632 iterates s.Projections[].Graph.Links and skips
  any link whose TransferID == "".
- internal/project/sankey.go:465 hardcodes TransferID: "" on EVERY link, and it
  is the only non-test site in the tree that sets the field.
- internal/check/subject.go factSlices builds projection options only for facts
  whose Scope == spineScope. Facts in any other scope are in NO graph at all.

So publishing p76 facts has two exits and both leave the check vacuous or worse:
at a non-spine scope they produce zero links, so nothing carries a transfer_id;
at the spine scope they double the city's transfers (fisc-aes).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY REQUIRED, and neither fisc-4rh nor fisc-5gk.3.1 says it:
(a) a projection that SELECTS the p76 scope -- which is fisc-aes's decision plus
    the multi-scope projection question (fisc-2ma);
(b) internal/project POPULATING Link.TransferID from the paired facts. fisc-4rh
    settled that the pairing id is derivable from the shared
    (doc_id, page, offset) -- the two legs cite the same printed figure -- but
    deriving it has to happen where links are built, and today that code writes
    the empty string unconditionally.

UNTIL BOTH LAND, the honest state is the one fisc-1wr.1.1 already demands:
transfer-legs-pair reports VACUOUS and is NOT quietly promoted. Recording this
because "fisc-5gk.3.1 retires it" was written into a landing plan as fact and
would have been discovered only when --strict stayed red.

Found in peer review of the landing plan, 2026-08-21.
acceptance_criteria: internal/project populates Link.TransferID for paired transfer facts; a projection selects the scope those facts carry; transfer-legs-pair reports Subjects > 0 and is proven failable by mutating one leg's value
notes:
2026-08-24 THE EDGE TO fisc-5gk.3.1 IS REMOVED, following this bead's own note
of the same day. Publishing p76 neither retires this check nor is blocked by it;
transfer-legs-pair stays declared vacuous against this bead throughout the p76
lane. Recorded here so nobody re-adds the edge from the older text above.

title: A fund number mis-assigned within its own fund type survives every check
description:
This is the recorded RESIDUAL RISK of the fisc-u2v decision, filed so it has an
id rather than living in a design note.

THE HOLE

A rule author writes `fund:` by hand. Nothing derives it from the printed fund
heading the rule anchors on. So if Airport's rows are filed under fund 601
instead of 501:

- the fund-group tie still holds -- both are enterprise, so the column sums are
  unchanged and fisc-u2v's revenue-detail-ties-to-spine passes;
- fact-funds-resolve (internal/check/vocabulary.go) passes, because it checks
  that the fund EXISTS and that its TYPE matches the fact's fund_group. Both
  are true of the wrong fund;
- CheckTotals passes, because the printed `Total <fund>` line never mentions the
  number.

Every check is green and the fact is filed under the wrong fund. That is the
plausible-wrong-value class this project exists to prevent.

NOT HYPOTHETICAL. p134 prints `Doolan Canyon Preserve Endow`, which truncates to
within one word of its same-type sibling `Doolan Canyon Open Space` -- funds 470
and 471, both permanent. pp.131-140 name roughly 70 funds; the pairs that differ
only in a trailing word are exactly where this lands.

TWO MITIGATIONS, both partial, and they compose

(a) Fund.Aliases (fisc-8dz) carrying the PRINTED heading verbatim with its page.
    That gives the rule author a resolvable string instead of a remembered
    number, and makes an ambiguous heading an error rather than a guess.

(b) A check that the set of fund numbers the rules USE equals the set of fund
    headings READ off the pages, and that each number is claimed by exactly one
    rule. (a) alone does not catch a number typed correctly for the wrong
    section; (b) alone does not catch two sections both resolving to one number.

Neither closes it completely: a heading and a number that are BOTH wrong in the
same direction still passes. Say so rather than claiming the mitigation is a
fix.

Found in the fisc-u2v design pass, 2026-08-21, stated there as "the one that
survives".
acceptance_criteria: each fund number is claimed by exactly one rule; the set of numbers used equals the set of headings read off the pages; a heading that resolves to no fund or to more than one is an error; the bead records what the mitigation still does not catch
close_reason:
Closed by rule-funds-match-their-headings, a tier-1 check, and the bead's own
hazard is demonstrated on the REAL corpus rather than only on a fixture.

MEASURED: filing p134's Doolan Canyon Preserve Endow under fund 471 instead of
470 -- its same-type sibling Doolan Canyon Open Space, the pair this bead names
-- and rebuilding:

  fact-funds-resolve            PASS  (471 exists and is type permanent)
  revenue-detail-ties-to-spine  PASS  (same fund group, every column sum
                                       unchanged, 134 cells, 0 differences)
  rule-funds-match-their-headings  FAIL

Which is exactly the three-line table in this bead's description, now with the
third line no longer empty.

TWO CLAUSES, and clause 2 is the one this bead asked for and a first draft of
the check dropped.

(1) THE NUMBER AGAINST THE PRINTED NAME, via registry.FundByLabel -- which
fisc-8dz built for this and which had ZERO callers outside its own test until
now. It reads PRINTED TOTALS rather than section anchors: six parts of
pp.127-140 anchor on a column-header fragment because their rows begin at the
top of a page, and resolving "FY 2026-27" as a fund name would have produced six
findings whose cheapest escape is inventing a fund alias for a column header.

And the printed total that names the fund is not always the rule's own. Writing
the check surfaced a shape the design had not: pp.131-140 are one fund per rule
and each prints `Total <fund>`, but pp.127-130 are ONE fund decomposed by
CATEGORY across ten rules whose printed totals are category names, and the fund
is named exactly once -- by the rollup `Total General Fund` covering all ten. So
the check asks whether SOME printed total governing the rule names its fund, and
a rule that falls out of that rollup's covers is reported.

(2) THE PAGES AGAINST THE RULES. Clause 1 only inspects rules that exist. The
first draft of this work claimed the arithmetic covers the rest -- that a
dropped fund section fails the spine tie. IT DOES NOT, for nine of the 69:
2022 COP Construction Fund, Transferable Development Cred, Doolan Canyon
Preserve Endow, Grant - Federal Grant Fund, Grant - HUD EDI Special Grant, FEMA
Funding, Grant - Local & Other Grants, Import Mitigation Fee and Human Services
Facility Fee all print zero in BOTH budget years, and the tie reconciles only
those two years. Dropping Transferable Development Cred leaves every FY2026 and
FY2027 cell identical and takes $4,723,774 of FY2023-24 with it --
TestDroppingAFundZeroInBothBudgetYearsIsInvisibleToTheTie asserts exactly that,
as a statement of the tie's BLIND SPOT rather than a defect in it.

So the check reads the pages its fund-bearing rules touch and requires every
printed fund total on them to be claimed. Only those pages, deliberately:
sweeping the whole corpus would report the appendix and fund-balance schedules,
which print fund totals nobody has mapped and nobody claimed to have.

WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT CATCH, as this bead asks: a total_row and a fund number
BOTH wrong in the same direction. Narrower than feared -- the section anchor
decides which rows are read, so a rule anchored on the wrong block maps
different figures and its printed total stops tying -- but not nothing, and no
check here sees it. Recorded in the check's doc comment.

Eight subtests, each of the two clauses proven failable.

title: data/funds.yaml has no entry for Police Evidence (p136)
description:
Budget Book p136 prints a fund section "Police Evidence" with real figures --
$25,000 in FY2025-26 and $31,000 in FY2026-27 -- and data/funds.yaml has NO
entry for it at all.

This is a different defect from the alias mismatches in fisc-8dz. Those are a
printed heading whose spelling differs from a fund the registry DOES carry
(fisc-8dz lists five on p76; six more were found on pp.131-140). This one is a
fund the registry does not carry in any spelling, so no alias channel can
resolve it.

WHY IT BLOCKS fisc-5gk.1

Every column on pp.131-140 carries `fund:`. A rule mapping p136 must write a
fund number for this section, and there is none to write. fact-funds-resolve
(internal/check/vocabulary.go) would report "fund N is not in data/funds.yaml,
so the fact joins to nothing" -- correct, and fail-closed, but it stops the
lane.

WHAT TO SETTLE

- the fund's number, from Budget Book pp.255-257 (the fund/department appendix).
  NOTE p253-254 is unreliable for pairing -- see the fund-names-come-from-p256
  memory.
- whether the registry is missing other funds this schedule names. The check
  that would answer it does not exist yet: nothing asserts that the set of fund
  headings read off pp.131-140 equals the set of numbers the rules use. That is
  its own bead.

Found in the fisc-u2v design pass, 2026-08-21, while verifying that every row
label and fund heading on pp.131-140 resolves. Every OTHER heading did.
