title: Sankey ribbon crossings: the pinned node order turns d3's crossing minimisation off
description:
site/app.js supplies .nodeSort(), and in d3-sankey v0.12.3 that gates off the re-sort that would reorder a column during relaxation. Order is therefore FUND_ORDER, then descending value, with transfers and fund-balance endpoints pinned to the bottom by nodeRank's 100/200 ranks -- a rule with nothing to do with where the ribbons go.

Measured on the committed sankey.json (12 sources -> 6 fund groups -> 7 uses, 58 links):
  today                        286 crossings, $1023M crossing ink
  exact optimum, funds fixed   177 crossings, $491M
  floor with funds free        168 crossings, $409M

Pinning FUND_ORDER for colour adjacency costs 9 crossings out of 177, so the palette ordering stays. The bottom-pinning of transfers/fund-balance is what costs: keeping it caps the win at 235.

Replace the value-descending fallback with SOURCE_ORDER and USE_ORDER measured constants, commit tools/sankey_order.py so the number is reproducible, and let a node click isolate its flows for the 177 crossings ordering cannot remove.
close_reason: Closed

title: Pin the three actions/*-pages actions by SHA
description:
pages.yml references actions/configure-pages@v5, actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4 and actions/deploy-pages@v4 by TAG, which is the only place this repository departs from its own supply-chain convention -- ci.yml pins every action to a commit with a trailing version comment (byob-security.5).

They were left as tags deliberately rather than guessed at. Resolving a SHA needs network egress and an authenticated gh, and neither was available in the session that wrote the file. A plausible-but-wrong 40-hex string is exactly the corruption shape this project refuses everywhere else, so an invented pin would have been worse than an honest tag.

WANTED
  gh api repos/actions/configure-pages/git/ref/tags/v5       --jq .object.sha
  gh api repos/actions/upload-pages-artifact/git/ref/tags/v4  --jq .object.sha
  gh api repos/actions/deploy-pages/git/ref/tags/v4           --jq .object.sha

then replace each @vN with @<sha> # vN.N.N, matching ci.yml's format exactly.

There is a TODO(pin) block at the top of .github/workflows/pages.yml carrying these same three commands; remove it in the same change.
close_reason:
Done. All three resolved and pinned, and the tags I had were wrong twice over.

  actions/configure-pages       45bfe0192ca1faeb007ade9deae92b16b8254a0d  v6.0.0
  actions/upload-pages-artifact fc324d3547104276b827a68afc52ff2a11cc49c9  v5.0.0
  actions/deploy-pages          cd2ce8fcbc39b97be8ca5fce6e763baed58fa128  v5.0.0

Two corrections this turned up:

The premise of this bead was wrong. It said resolving a pin needed network that
was unavailable. HTTPS to api.github.com and github.com both work; what failed
in the original session was SSH on port 22 (git ls-remote origin) and an
unauthenticated gh, and I generalised those into 'egress is blocked'. The API
endpoints are public and need no token.

The versions were a major behind. The file shipped configure-pages@v5,
upload-pages-artifact@v3 and deploy-pages@v4; current majors are v6, v5 and v5.
Also worth recording: code review flagged upload-pages-artifact@v4 as probably
not existing and I moved it to v3 on that basis -- v4 DOES exist
(7b1f4a764d45c48632c6b24a0339c27f5614fb0b), so the finding was wrong and the v3
edit was a downgrade made for a bad reason. Moot now at v5.

All three tags are lightweight, pointing straight at commits, so no ^{}
dereference was needed. Each SHA was confirmed twice, from the REST API and
again from git ls-remote, which do not share a code path. The TODO(pin) block
is gone from the file.

title: Row.Label cannot express a two-field row identity, so p76 can only be read by encoding the page's kerning
description:
A row's identity on Budget Book p76 is TWO printed fields with an arbitrary run
of spaces between them:

  Transfer From Low Income Hsng          to General Fund     257,012  -  -  -  (10)
  Transfer From Home Grant               to General Fund       8,932  8,706 ...

mapping.Row carries a single Label, matched by strings.Index as one substring
(resolve.go:460). Neither field alone works, and both failures are demonstrated
rather than argued:

- Label = the source only. The destination sits where the figures are expected
  and the read fails: `cannot parse amount "to"`.
- Label = the destination only. The source lands in the gap before the label,
  where checkGap refuses it as an unmapped row.

So the only label that resolves today is the two fields WITH THE EXACT SPACE RUN
between them -- 24 spaces on one row, 27 on the next -- which is the kerning of
one release encoded in a rule file. testdata/spine.yaml's own doctrine forbids
exactly this ("an anchor may not assume single spacing"), and it is right to:
the runs are typeset per row and per column half.

internal/mapping/testdata/transfers-p76.yaml does it anyway, deliberately and
with the reason in its header, because it is a reconciliation fixture pinned
against a byte-identical page copy. Nothing published may.

WANTED: a row whose label is two anchors with unconstrained whitespace between
them -- not a regex, and not a relaxation of the substring match, because the
gap has to stay checkable. Both parts are PUBLISHED text, so the fact's
row_label can still be the pair.

RELATED, and worth deciding together: fisc-0cs wants Row.Continuation for
wrapped labels. Both are the same shape of gap -- "a row's label is not one
contiguous substring" -- and p76 has one of each.
acceptance_criteria: a rule can name a row by two published anchors without asserting the whitespace between them; internal/mapping/testdata/transfers-p76.yaml is rewritten to use it and stops embedding space runs
close_reason:
Landed. Row.LabelTail names a row's second published anchor; the text between the two must be whitespace and nothing else, so the gap is unasserted but still checked. Row identity moves from Label to Row.Identity() (both anchors), because nine p76 rows share 'to General Fund' and several share 'Transfer From General Fund' -- neither field alone is unique. The fact's row_label is Row.PrintedLabel(), the pair joined by one space, since both halves are published text.

internal/mapping/testdata/transfers-p76.yaml is rewritten and no longer embeds any space run (grep for a label with two consecutive spaces returns 0), which was the acceptance criterion. Its header paragraph asserting the page is unpublishable for that reason was rewritten rather than left standing.

Found on the way: transfers_p76_test.go's own transferSource helper cut the label on a two-space run, so the reconciliation carried the same kerning dependency the rule file did and would have broken on a re-layout identically. It now reads Row.Label directly.

Proven failable by mutating the code twice: removing the whitespace-only gap check reddens the test that pairs row 1's source with row 2's destination; putting uniqueness back on Label alone reddens the two-rows-share-a-source test.

facts.jsonl byte-identical -- pp.66-67 declare no label_tail. fisc verify unchanged at 19 passed / 0 failed / 5 vacuous.

fisc-5gk.3.1 loses one of its five blockers.

title: Export FY2027: it is already projected and checked, only the export is pinned
description:
Half the fact store is built, checked, and then discarded at the export seam.

FY2027 is NOT unprojected -- that was a misreading. internal/check/subject.go
:523-556 (factSlices) derives one projection per (fiscal_year, basis) present in
the store, so a complete FY2027 sankey already exists and fisc verify already
checks it:

  PASS  facts-are-projected   240 facts, all of them in one of 2 projections
  PASS  graph-acyclic         116 links over 50 nodes in 2 projections, no cycle
  PASS  counts-reconcile      sankey FY2026 ...; sankey FY2027 ...

What FY2027 never is, is EXPORTED. pkg/cmd/export/data.go:59-61 hardcodes
project.PublishedFiscalYear (= 2026, internal/project/project.go:64), so the site
publishes one of the two projections that already pass.

SIZE: A DAY, AND IT IS NOT GO-ONLY. Sized before starting and then left, so the
figure below is measured rather than guessed. site/app.js:768 fetches exactly
one projection -- CONFIG.projections[CONFIG.primary] -- and internal/export/page.go
renders the headline tiles server-side from that projection's metadata
(page.go:271 PrimaryPath). Emitting a second data/sankey-2027.json therefore
ships an inert file the client never reads. A real year toggle needs:
buildProjections to loop over the published years rather than one
PublishedFiscalYear; FISC_CONFIG to carry which projection belongs to which
year; app.js to re-fetch and re-render on switch; and the tiles, caveats and
flow table -- all rendered once from the primary -- to re-render with it.

No new pages, no new fixtures, no schema bump, no mapping. Land it after
fisc-oxf if that is close, since schema_version 2 touches the same config seam.

THE CAVEATS TRAVEL WITH THE YEAR, and they are not the same size in both. From
p66/p67: FY2027 transfers out total 72,386,884 against transfers in 21,624,633,
a residual of 50,762,251 -- larger than the 38,086,737 already shipping for
FY2026. Whatever the tiles and caveats do on a year switch, they cannot keep
FY2026's figure on screen beside FY2027's chart.

CONSTRAINT, from internal/project/project.go's own doc comment: it must be TWO
projections, never one built over both years -- "a projection built over both
doubles every figure and still balances", the failure mode no internal
consistency check can catch. Same hazard family as fisc-u2v.

Found in peer review of the landing plan, 2026-08-18.
acceptance_criteria: the site publishes both FY2026 and FY2027 as separate projections; the client can switch years; no projection is built over both years; fisc verify still passes
notes: 2026-08-18 SIZED before starting: this is NOT Go-only, which the bead's 'half a day of export plumbing' undersells. site/app.js:768 fetches exactly one projection -- CONFIG.projections[CONFIG.primary] -- and internal/export/page.go renders the headline tiles server-side from that projection's metadata (page.go:271 PrimaryPath). So emitting a second data/sankey-2027.json would ship an inert file the client never reads. A real year toggle needs: buildProjections to loop over the published years rather than one PublishedFiscalYear; FISC_CONFIG to carry which projection belongs to which year; app.js to re-fetch and re-render on switch; and the tiles, caveats and flow table -- all currently rendered once from the primary -- to re-render with it. Treat as a day, and land it after fisc-oxf if that is close, since schema_version 2 touches the same config seam.

title: Band-driven cell selection: the sparse read, per-cell ErrAbsent, and the count relaxation
description:
fisc-yqv.2 landed geometry as a pure CROSS-CHECK: the -layout read is unchanged
and geometry only supplies a column index the read is checked against. That is
why turning it on moved no byte of facts.jsonl. It is also why a sparse row can
only be REFUSED, never read.

To read one, geometry has to SELECT the row's tokens -- take the words on the
row's printed line, assign each to a band, and let a band with no word be an
absent cell. Three things follow, and they are one change rather than three:

(1) positionalValues' exact len(toks) == ExpectedValues has to relax to <=, since
a sparse row legitimately produces fewer tokens. It must be gated on an explicit
per-part declaration -- do not relax it globally. A dense part keeps both guards
permanently. This is the guard that caught fisc-c00.

(2) With P5 relaxed, two checks become reachable that are dead today and were
deliberately left out rather than shipped unexercised: that no two rows read the
SAME printed line, and the line-count arm generally.

(3) A cell holding more than one word must be assembled, and the mechanic is
already settled -- take the RAW PAGE SLICE text[first.off : last.off+len(last.text)],
never a re-joined string. Reasons, all checked:
  - fisc verify's fact-offset-points-at-token asserts text[Offset:Offset+len(Token)]
    == Token, so a synthesized "$ -" would fail it while the real slice cannot.
  - "$21130 083" then reaches amount.Parse with its real spacing and splitDigits
    fires, which is the fisc-j5p shape from the other side.
  - CIP p40's "$            -" normalizes to "$ -" and parses as zero, which
    disposes of fisc-yun for free.
  - on a single-word cell the slice is byte-identical to today's token, so
    facts.jsonl does not move.

An empty band raises amount.ErrAbsent naming the cell, wrapped so errors.Is
works. That is NOT the same as reading fisc-8ln's rows: on CIP p40 six cells have
no mark in any substrate, so absent-vs-zero stays fisc-8ln's problem and needs
Rule.TotalColumn beside it.
acceptance_criteria: a sparse row resolves its printed figures to the right columns and raises ErrAbsent naming each cell it has none for; a dense part still gets the exact value count; facts.jsonl is unmoved
notes: 2026-08-18 NOT ON THE CRITICAL PATH for the pp.127-140 / pp.167-170 lanes, measured rather than assumed. All 18 pages in scope were checked against the -bbox geometry in peer review of the landing plan: ZERO rows carry 1-3 value tokens; every data row carries exactly 4, with '-' printed in every zero cell. The only short lines are the running footer. So there is no sparse row for band-driven selection to read, and the exact len(toks)==ExpectedValues guard does not need relaxing for this scope. This note exists because fisc-yun has one and this bead did not, which is one bd ready away from it being re-litigated. Revisit for CIP p40 (fisc-8ln) or any of fisc-gmx's 223 pages.

title: Substrate disagreement: 223 of 786 pages cannot carry the column guard
description:
fisc-yqv.2's guard requires the two substrates to describe the same page: the
same number of non-blank lines, and the same tokens in the same order on each.
Measured over the whole corpus, they do not.

124 of 786 pages disagree on LINE COUNT (59 CIP, 39 budget, 26 ACFR). A further
99 agree on line count and disagree on the TOKENS of some line (89 CIP, 7 budget,
3 ACFR). 223 of 786, 28 percent.

No page in current or near-term mapping scope is among them -- not 66, 67, 127,
128-140, 167-170, CIP 40 or CIP 29 -- and every one of them is REFUSED rather
than read approximately, which is correct. But "the guard is on" and "the page is
readable" will diverge sharply the moment CIP mapping starts, and 89 of the 99
token failures are CIP pages.

TWO CAUSES, both mechanical, and neither is what a first look suggests:

(1) LINE ASSIGNMENT -- 87 of the 89 CIP token failures. A run of words sits on
one line in -layout and on a different line in the geometry clustering. CIP p42
is the worked example: 'Park Fees $2,200,000 ...' is on the PROJECT line in
-layout and on the FUNDING line in geometry.

(2) A SUPERSCRIPT FOOTNOTE MARKER -- the cause on budget pp.68, 70, 186, 190,
192, 194. -layout emits the superscript on its own line; geometry clusters it
into the row. These are financial schedules ONE PAGE from the mapped spine
('Fund Balance by Major and Aggregate Non-Major Funds', 'Available Funds, Uses of
Funds, and Fund Balances'), so this is not a narrative-page problem.

Dot-leader splitting is a minor third case and a TOC phenomenon: budget 3-4,
ACFR 5-6, CIP 3-4 only.

Two pages admit NO tolerance at all: CIP p104 and p111, where the largest
intra-line y0 spread exceeds the smallest inter-line gap (10.57 against 4.43;
7.32 against 6.34). No half-median-height rule reproduces the -layout partition
there, so those need a different grouping or a rule that does not need one.

Do NOT respond by writing a corpus-wide test that asserts 1:1 correspondence. It
is false on 124 pages today.
acceptance_criteria: the two causes are confirmed on a named page each; a rule author can tell from the error which one they hit; the CIP coverage lanes have a cost estimate for it
notes: 2026-08-18 DEFERRED, landing plan. Cite this bead's own sentence rather than re-deriving the conclusion: 'No page in current or near-term mapping scope is among them -- not 66, 67, 127, 128-140, 167-170, CIP 40 or CIP 29.' 223 pages failing the guard matters only when someone maps one of them. Revisit when a coverage bead needs one.

title: data/departments.yaml: a registry for the department axis, and netCells must stop refusing one
description:
Nothing resolves a fact's 'department'. taxonomy.yaml covers categories and funds.yaml covers funds and fund groups; the department axis has no registry at all, so fisc verify's fact-vocabulary check can only report it as unresolvable.

Two separate defects fall out of that, both found in the fisc-1wr.1 peer review:

(1) internal/project's netCells (sankey.go:531-538) REFUSES a fact carrying a department outright. That is correct for the p66-67 spine, which crosses category against fund group and has no department axis -- but it means a department-bearing fact makes check.Load die before any check runs, exiting 1 with no report at all, which is strictly worse than a red check. The refusal needs to become a per-projection error the caller can report, or the projection needs to know the department tier.

(2) fisc-5gk.2 maps Budget Book pp.167-170, department x object category -- roughly 14 departments. Those facts need somewhere to resolve. Until this lands, fisc verify's department axis reports a non-pass with a stated reason rather than a fake pass, which is the honest interim but is exactly the shape that gets a gate commented out if it sits red for long (see fisc-1wr.4's note).

Shape to follow: funds.yaml and taxonomy.yaml both validate on load -- 'a registry that loaded is one whose invariants already hold' (internal/registry/registry.go:1-21). Slugs unique, label required, and the same derived/rationale/source_note discipline for anything editorial. Watch for a slug colliding with a taxonomy category slug; a fact's row_path is department + '/' + category, so a collision is genuinely ambiguous.

Source: the department names printed on pp.167-170 themselves, plus Budget Book pp.255-257 for the fund/department relationship (see the fund-names-come-from-p256 memory -- p253-254 is unreliable for pairing).
acceptance_criteria: every department a fact carries resolves in data/departments.yaml; loading validates; a department-bearing fact produces a reportable per-projection error or a real projection rather than exit 1 with no report; no department slug collides with a taxonomy category slug
notes:
2026-08-23 THE SLUG NAMESPACE IS DECIDED, and this bead's 2026-08-18 note is wrong about it in a way that would make the file unwritable.

THAT NOTE SAYS: 'two departments whose name and sole division's name differ only in case (FIRE DEPARTMENT / Fire Administration; GENERAL SERVICES / General Services), so slug collision is a live hazard within this file as well as against taxonomy.yaml.'

BOTH HALVES OF THE EXAMPLE ARE WRONG AND THE COUNT IS SHORT. Re-derived off the pages:

  FIRE DEPARTMENT / Fire Administration -- NOT a collision. Different words;
  the slugs fire-department and fire-administration are distinct. Same for
  LIBRARY DEPARTMENT / Library.

The real department/division collisions are FIVE, and three of them are EXACT rather than case-only:

  CITY COUNCIL            p0167:7   / City Council            p0167:9    exact
  CITY MANAGER            p0167:17  / City Manager            p0167:19   exact
  CITY ATTORNEY           p0167:33  / City Attorney           p0167:35   exact
  GENERAL SERVICES        p0167:63  / General Services        p0168:7    case
  ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES p0168:15  / Administrative Services p0168:17   case

CONSEQUENCE: 'slug uniqueness must span both tiers' cannot be satisfied. Five departments would have to be renamed to strings the city never prints, and an invented name in a registry whose whole claim is 'this is what the document says' is the defect this project exists to refuse.

DECIDED: TWO NAMESPACES, NOT ONE.

Row.Department carries the DIVISION slug (fisc-28s A-prime), so a fact only ever names a division. Divisions are therefore the slug space check.Vocabulary.Department(slug) resolves. The department tier is a separate key, referenced from each division by a parent field. Uniqueness is required WITHIN each tier and not across them, so city-council may name both a department and its sole division -- which is what the page prints.

WHAT DOES NOT RELAX. The cross-AXIS refusal stands: no division slug may equal a data/taxonomy.yaml category slug. That is a different claim -- fact.RowPath composes department + '/' + category, so a collision there is genuinely ambiguous, whereas a department and a division sharing a name is the document's own structure. factDepartmentsResolve already asserts it (vocabulary.go:246-250) and keeps doing so. Verified: no proposed division slug collides with any of the 25 taxonomy slugs.

ALSO CORRECTED, same re-derivation: Fire Administration has ONE object row (Services & Supplies, p0170:15) -- the department is a contract service and prints no wages line. Nothing may assume a division has two or three object rows, or that every division has a wages-and-benefits fact.

And the department name is not always the heading plus ' TOTAL': PUBLIC WORKS (p0169:47) prints PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT TOTAL (p0170:11). The rollup anchor cannot be derived from the heading.

Found in peer review of the landing plan, 2026-08-23.
close_reason: data/departments.yaml lands with 11 departments over 23 divisions, check.Vocabulary gains Division(slug), and factDepartmentsResolve reaches a verdict instead of erroring. The netCells refusal STAYS (fisc-brx decided it is the second guard); what changed is that buildProjections records a refusal and the new projections-build check reports it, so a mis-scoped department-bearing fact is a red check with a full report rather than exit 1 with none. Two-namespace decision recorded on the bead, correcting the 2026-08-18 note's collision list. Landed 16d35a1.

title: Tier 1 remainder: the checks that only become non-vacuous after the tier hierarchy lands
description:
fisc-1wr.1 lands in two pieces because three of its checks cannot be non-vacuous at spine-only coverage, and a check reported as passing when it had nothing to test is the exact thing the vacuous status exists to prevent.

Landing with the parent (Wave A): facts sorted; ids unique; every category assignable and every fund_group real; every link's value_cents equals the sum of its fact_ids; graph acyclic; every derived:true node carries rationale + source_note; counts reconcile.

Landing HERE, after fisc-gxa.2:
- AGGREGATION INVARIANCE -- the total at every tier depth equals the total at every other depth. Vacuous today because the shipped graph has one tier depth and there is nothing to fold. Becomes the load-bearing check the instant finest-grain links exist: it is what catches a double-parented or orphaned node.
- constraint_tier is one of the four declared values -- vacuous until any node carries one.

Still vacuous after this and expected to stay so: 'every transfer_id has two equal legs'. No link carries a transfer_id (sankey.go:290-294) and mapping p76 alone does not fix it -- see fisc-4rh.
acceptance_criteria: aggregation invariance runs over more than one tier depth and reports Subjects > 0; constraint-tier membership likewise; the transfer-leg check still reports VACUOUS and is not quietly promoted

title: Fixture expansion: generalise both copies of TestPageFixturesAreVerbatimCopies, add geometry fixtures
description:
testdata/pages/ fixtures are hand-copied from data/extracted/ and the guard that makes every other test in the mapping and build packages mean anything is a byte-comparison against the source. That guard exists TWICE -- internal/mapping/resolve_test.go:96 (hardcoding []int{66,67,127}) and pkg/cmd/build/build_test.go:121 (hardcoding []int{66,67}) -- and both hardcode a single doc id and a single substrate.

Three things it cannot currently express, all of which the PoC needs:
- a second document (CIP p40 for the column guard)
- a second substrate (geometry/pNNNN.json alongside pages/pNNNN.txt)
- the ~17 further page/geometry pairs fisc-5gk.1 (pp.128-140) and fisc-5gk.2 (pp.168-170) require

Make it a table of {doc, artifact path} and cover both substrates. The fixture work is a real cost inside the coverage lanes, not an afterthought -- conventions.md is explicit that a drifted fixture is THE bad case.
acceptance_criteria: one table-driven verbatim-copy test shape covering pages and geometry across all three documents; both existing copies converted; adding a fixture means adding a table row and nothing else
notes:

Note neither lane is blocked on the fixtures alone: fisc-5gk.1 still needs fisc-u2v, which is a decision.

The remaining ~17 page/geometry pairs for pp.128-140 and pp.168-170 are NOT lost: this bead's own 2026-08-18 note says they must land with the lane that needs them, each naming its failure mode per testdata/README.md, rather than being bulk-copied in advance. Keeping this open gated fisc-5gk.1 and fisc-5gk.2 on work those lanes own.

title: Row identity for the department x object pages: one rule per department, or Part.Department
description:
Row.Department is per-RULE, but on Budget Book pp.167-170 the department varies per PART while the category rows (Wages & Benefits, Services & Supplies, Total) repeat -- and parse.go:226 requires row labels to be unique within a rule. So a single rule CANNOT cover ten departments.

Option A -- one rule per department (~14 rules). Works with today's schema, no Go change. Fact ids stay distinct because rule_id is in MakeID's tuple. Cost: 14 near-identical rule blocks in the mapping file.

Option B -- a new Part.Department that qualifies its rows. Cleaner file, but mapping.Value must then carry the department through into fact.FromValues, which is a change to the value/fact seam.

Recommendation: A. Decide BEFORE fisc-0cs lands, because the choice determines what a p167 part's section/stop_at anchors look like and therefore what the continuation fixtures are testing.
acceptance_criteria: the decision is recorded here with its reasoning; fisc-5gk.2 and fisc-0cs both reference it; if B is chosen, the Value->Fact seam change is scoped in this bead
notes:
2026-08-18 DECIDED: neither A nor B as written. Take A-PRIME -- ONE RULE PER
DIVISION, 22 of them. No Go change. Evidence from reading pp.167-170.

WHY OPTION A AS WRITTEN IS IMPOSSIBLE, NOT MERELY VERBOSE

parse.go:227-235 builds rowIndex over r.Rows -- unique per RULE -- and every
Part of a rule shares that one row set. A department is not the unit that has a
unique row set: ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES (p168:15-35) contains three divisions,
Administrative Services, Finance and Human Resources, and each prints the SAME
three labels Wages & Benefits / Services & Supplies / Total. One rule per
department is three duplicate labels, refused at parse time. The bead's estimate
of "~14 rules" also undercounts: there are 11 departments and 22 divisions.

AND THE ROW SET IS NOT EVEN UNIFORM ACROSS DIVISIONS

- FIRE DEPARTMENT (p170:13-19) has one division, Fire Administration, printing
  only Services & Supplies and Total -- NO Wages & Benefits row.
- General Services (p167:63 - p168:13) prints a fourth label, Debt Services.

So a single shared row set spanning divisions fails on both. The division is the
smallest unit whose row set is self-consistent, which is what makes it the rule
boundary.

WHY NOT OPTION B

B (Part.Department qualifying its rows) would need the qualifier to be the
DIVISION, not the department -- the department is a grouping above it -- and it
still costs the mapping.Value -> fact.FromValues seam change the bead flags. A'
gets the same facts with no Go change. Fact ids stay distinct because rule_id is
in MakeID's tuple.

WHERE THE DEPARTMENT GOES

Row.Department (per rule) carries the DIVISION slug. The department/division
hierarchy lives in data/departments.yaml (fisc-o15), which has to model both
levels regardless -- see the design note added there on this date. The all-caps
department heading and the "<DEPARTMENT> TOTAL" line become the anchor context
and the stated total for the department's divisions taken together.

TWO SHAPES THE RULE AUTHOR WILL HIT

(1) ONE DIVISION SPANS A PAGE BREAK. General Services prints its Wages &
Benefits row as the last line of p167 and its Services & Supplies, Debt Services
and Total rows at the head of p168. That division's rule needs two Parts on two
pages, with the rows split between them. Every other division is single-page;
the department-level breaks (GENERAL SERVICES p167->p168, POLICE p168->p169,
PUBLIC WORKS p169->p170) fall between divisions except this one.

(2) THE CONTINUATION FRAGMENTS ARE DIVISION LABELS, NOT STRAY TEXT. This
sharpens fisc-0cs. Exactly four across the four pages, and each is the second
line of a wrapped DIVISION NAME:
    p0167:56  Devel              (Innovation & Economic Devel)
    p0169:16  Development Admin
    p0169:34  Services
    p0169:50  Administration
Correction to fisc-0cs's description: it says "more on p170" -- there are none
on p170. So the fragment is part of the row's own identity, which is an argument
for Row.Continuation over a bare checkGap relaxation: the two lines together are
the label.
close_reason: Decided A-prime: ONE RULE PER DIVISION, 22 of them, no Go change. Option A as written (one rule per department) is impossible rather than merely verbose -- parse.go:227-235 makes row labels unique per RULE and every Part shares one row set, while ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES holds three divisions each printing the same three labels. The row set is not uniform either: Fire Administration prints no Wages & Benefits row and General Services prints a fourth label, Debt Services, so the division is the smallest unit whose row set is self-consistent. Option B would need the qualifier to be the division anyway and still costs the Value->Fact seam change. Row.Department carries the division slug; the department/division hierarchy lives in data/departments.yaml (fisc-o15, sized on the same date: 11 departments, 22 divisions). Two shapes recorded for the rule author: General Services splits mid-division across the p167/p168 break and needs two Parts, and the four continuation fragments are wrapped division LABELS rather than stray text, which sharpened fisc-0cs toward Row.Continuation. Full reasoning in the notes.

title: sankey.json schema_version 2: finest-grain links, and page.go must refuse an unknown version
description:
fisc-gxa.2 changes what `links` MEANS: today a revenue-source -> fund-group link is the whole flow; after the tier migration it is a leaf the client must fold. A v1 consumer reading a v2 file draws a chart that is WRONG, not one that fails, so the version has to move and the reader has to gate on it.

Two halves:
(1) project.SchemaVersion 1 -> 2, and docs/sankey-contract.md updated to describe finest-grain links plus node.parent/node.tier.
(2) internal/export/page.go currently copies doc.SchemaVersion straight into FISC_CONFIG (page.go:212) with NO validation anywhere in the package -- while internal/corpus, internal/registry and internal/mapping all gate theirs. Close that gap in the same change.

The contract was frozen in its own commit precisely so producer, packager and consumer could be built concurrently against it. Changing it is a decision, not a bullet inside another bead -- same precedent as fisc-j8f (YAML) and fisc-zna (d3).
acceptance_criteria: project.SchemaVersion == 2; internal/export refuses a projection whose schema_version it does not understand, with a test; docs/sankey-contract.md describes the v2 shape; testdata/sankey.golden.json is NOT regenerated wholesale -- its diff touches only schema_version and the new Link.pages, and that is asserted by review of the diff
notes:
2026-08-21 DECIDED: SPLIT THE BEAD. The two halves have different readiness and
bundling them would publish a false contract.

(a) THE READER GATE LANDS NOW, independently of any version bump.

internal/export/page.go:212 copies doc.SchemaVersion straight into clientConfig
with no validation anywhere in the package -- while internal/registry/load.go
:115 and :180, internal/registry/sources.go:109, internal/corpus/corpus.go:164,
internal/geom/geom.go:137 and internal/mapping/parse.go:167-174 all gate theirs.
This is a pure gap-close: it changes no contract, so it has no reason to wait.

Worth recording that the gap is WIDER than this bead states. site/app.js reads
schema_version NOWHERE at runtime -- the string appears only at app.js:75 and :85
inside JSDoc @property typedefs. So project.go:47-49's promise, that
schema_version is the thing "a consumer reads first and refuses a document it
does not understand", is unimplemented on BOTH sides of the seam, not just the
packager's. Closing only the Go half leaves the client drawing a v2 file happily.

HOW TO GATE IT WITHOUT BREAKING THE SEAM. internal/export deliberately does not
import internal/project (export.go:4-9) and that separation is worth keeping. So
the guard is a constant in internal/export PLUS A TEST THAT PINS IT TO
project.SchemaVersion. The test is the thing that makes the duplication safe --
without it the two constants drift and the gate passes a document it should
refuse. The test may import both packages; the production code may not.

(b) THE VERSION BUMP LANDS WITH fisc-gxa.2, NOT BEFORE.

schema_version: 2 MEANS finest-grain links. Declaring it while internal/project
still emits the pre-aggregated three-layer graph would publish a contract the
producer does not satisfy -- the exact class of false claim this bead exists to
prevent, committed by the bead itself.

Note the scope correction already recorded on fisc-gxa.2 and easy to lose here:
node.parent and node.tier ALREADY EXIST in shipped v1 and are emitted on every
node. What v2 changes is what `links` MEANS and that the fields are POPULATED --
not that they exist.

SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT found while planning, and it belongs on this bead because
it constrains (b): aggregation-invariance (internal/check/graph.go:692-724)
HARD-ERRORS the instant any node carries a parent. So (b), fisc-gxa.2 and
fisc-1wr.1.1 are ONE COMMIT, not three in sequence. Landing the bump and the
population without the fold reddens fisc verify.

The acceptance criterion about testdata/sankey.golden.json stands and is the one
to hold the line on: its diff touches only schema_version and the new Link.pages.
A wholesale regeneration would make the golden file agree with whatever the code
now does, which is the opposite of what it is for.
2026-08-22 HALF (a) IS IN THE WORKING TREE, uncommitted (human reviews before commit).

Go: internal/export/page.go grows export.SchemaVersion = 1, ErrSchemaVersion and
checkSchemaVersion, called in buildPage BEFORE any field is read out of the
document. Refusal shape mirrors registry.schemaVersionErr: cmdutil.WithHint says
which way the mismatch runs (newer => upgrade the binary; zero/absent => may not
be a fisc projection). internal/export still does NOT import internal/project.

The pin: TestSchemaVersionIsPinnedToTheProducer (export_test.go) imports both and
asserts export.SchemaVersion == project.SchemaVersion.
TestClientSchemaVersionIsPinnedToTheProducer reads app.js out of site.FS() and
pins the literal 'const SCHEMA_VERSION = 1;'. Both mutation-proved: bumping the
Go const gave 'export.SchemaVersion is 2 but project.SchemaVersion is 1 ...';
bumping the JS const gave 'site/app.js does not declare "const SCHEMA_VERSION =
1;" ...'.

JS: site/app.js gets SCHEMA_VERSION and understands(got, what), called TWICE --
on CONFIG.schema_version before the fetch and on the fetched document's own
schema_version, because the packager stamping the config from one document is
not evidence about the bytes on the wire. fail() now also prepends a
role=alert .refusal banner to <main> (new rule in style.css), so a refusal is
visible above the chart instead of only in the provenance panel below it. Proved
in a throwaway node DOM stub for versions 2 and 0, and that v1 still proceeds to
the fetch.

NOT done, deliberately: project.SchemaVersion is still 1. That is half (b) and
lands in one commit with fisc-gxa.2 + fisc-1wr.1.1, per the split above.

Gates: facts.jsonl byte-identical; verify 19 passed / 0 failed / 5 vacuous /
1 skipped; golangci-lint 0 issues.
close_reason: Half (a) landed in f551754: internal/export gates schema_version with a constant pinned to project.SchemaVersion by a test, and site/app.js gained the client-side gate it never had. Half (b) -- the bump to 2, which MEANS finest-grain links -- deliberately did not land; it belongs in fisc-gxa.2's commit, per this bead's own 2026-08-21 split.

title: Printed dashes missing from the PDF text layer on some CIP rows
description:
On CIP p40 the rendered page PRINTS '-' in the intervening FY columns of rows PB200654 and PB202617, but those dashes are in NO substrate: absent from pdftotext -layout, -raw, default mode, and from the -bbox geometry. They are drawn as non-text in the PDF. Row PB200429 on the same page DOES carry its dashes, so this is per-row, not a flag choice. The old xberg artifacts lacked them too, so it is not a regression -- but it is a real limitation of the corpus that the fail-closed rule needs an answer for.

Why it matters: 'absent is not zero' is a load-bearing invariant. A printed '-' is a zero FACT; an empty cell means the line does not apply. On these rows the two are indistinguishable from any artifact, and extraction currently offers no channel to signal 'unrecognised' so a consumer can fail closed.

Options to weigh: (a) detect the gap via geometry -- a column position with no token between two tokens that do have positions -- and emit an explicit 'unknown' marker rather than nothing; (b) require rules over affected pages to declare the shape; (c) render-based detection. Do NOT resolve it by defaulting a missing token to zero.

Found in peer review of fisc-yqv.3.
acceptance_criteria: a rule over CIP p40 reads PB200654 correctly; no path silently treats an absent token as zero
notes:
2026-08-18 AC TIGHTENED when fisc-yqv.2 landed. It used to read "either reads
PB200654 correctly OR fails closed with a message naming the missing cell" --
and the column guard now satisfies the or-branch, which would have left "reads
correctly" as the obligation of no open bead. The or-branch is deleted; this bead
owns reading the row.

Interim state, verified by TestCIPp40SparseRowFailsClosedButDoesNotRead: the read
runs off the end of the row's two printed figures and into the row-label area and
is refused naming the row and the column. The test is named for what it proves.
Nothing is filed under the wrong year.

title: Continuation rows: wrapped labels land between a row's figures and the next label
description:
pdftotext -layout wraps long department names onto a second line that lands BETWEEN a row's last figure and the next row's label:

  Innovation & Economic Wages & Benefits   1,028,282  1,068,663  1,233,502  1,192,014
  Devel
                        Services & Supplies  1,610,950  2,592,436  2,870,310  2,829,666

Occurrences on the department pages: p167 'Devel'; p169 'Development Admin', 'Services', 'Administration'; more on p170.

checkGap (resolve.go:394) rejects any non-whitespace between rows, so these pages cannot be read. skip: true CANNOT express it -- a skipped row still consumes ncols tokens and these fragments have zero.

Needs either a Row.Continuation concept or a principled checkGap relaxation. Both are exactly the kind of change 'fail closed' makes expensive to get right, so it needs its own bead rather than being absorbed into a coverage lane.

xberg did not hit this because it fused everything onto one line -- which is also why it lost the rows. The two defects are the same defect from opposite sides.

BLOCKS fisc-5gk.2 (GF department x object, pp.167-170).
acceptance_criteria: pp.167-170 resolve with the correct row count and no relaxation of the unmapped-row check for non-continuation text
notes:
2026-08-18 A SECOND LANE NOW PAYS THIS. The bug is not confined to the department pages: Budget Book p0076.txt:351 prints 'Connection' on its own line, the wrapped tail of 'Transfer From Wastewater to LAVWMA / Wastewater Connection', landing between that row's figures and the next row's label -- the exact shape enumerated for pp.167-170. checkGap refuses it, so the p76 reconciliation (fisc-5gk.3) has to split the Enterprise section into two parts around it. That workaround is available to a reconciliation because part boundaries are declared; it is not a fix, and fisc-5gk.3.1 should not have to ship it. Row.Continuation would serve p76 as well as the department pages: here too the two lines together are the label.
2026-08-21 FRAGMENT INVENTORY CORRECTED, from peer review. Two errors, one of
which changes what Row.Continuation has to cover.

FIVE FRAGMENTS, NOT FOUR, and they are: p0167:56 `Devel`; p0167:62 `TOTAL`;
p0169:16 `Development Admin`; p0169:34 `Services`; p0169:50 `Administration`.

THERE ARE NONE ON p170. This bead's description says "more on p170" and
fisc-28s's notes already recorded that correction on 2026-08-18; it did not make
it into the description, so it keeps being re-imported by anything reading the
description alone. Fixed here.

THE ONE THAT MATTERS: p0167:62 `TOTAL` is the wrapped tail of
`INNOVATION & ECONOMIC DEVELOPEMENT TOTAL` -- a wrapped DEPARTMENT TOTAL line,
not a division label. Row.Continuation as this bead frames it ("wrapped labels
land between a row's figures and the next label", i.e. a row's own label
continuing) DOES NOT COVER IT: the fragment belongs to a total row, and under
fisc-28s's A-prime the department total is not any single rule's row. So the
design needs to say what happens to a continuation fragment whose parent line is
outside the rule -- skip it explicitly, or extend the concept to total rows.
Deciding that after the YAML is written is how it becomes a checkGap relaxation.

(Also note the department's name is misspelled DEVELOPEMENT on the page. That is
the city's typo and belongs in an alias, not a silent correction.)

SEPARATELY, the p76 occurrence in the 2026-08-18 note is at p0076.txt LINE 38,
not line 351. The file is 77 lines long.
close_reason:
Landed. Part.WrappedLabels declares, per part, the printed fragments a page wraps onto a line of their own; checkGap admits a gap whose trimmed text equals a declared fragment and refuses everything else exactly as before.

DECLARED ON THE PART, NOT THE ROW -- a correction to this bead's own framing, and the reason is p0167:62. 'TOTAL' there is the wrapped tail of 'INNOVATION & ECONOMIC DEVELOPEMENT TOTAL', a department total line, which under fisc-28s's one-rule-per-division belongs to no rule's row set. A Row.Continuation field could not have carried it; a part-level list carries both shapes.

NO RELAXATION, which is the acceptance criterion. Two refusal tests against one read test: the same real p167 block with no declaration still fails naming 'Devel', and declaring a different fragment does not admit it. Proven failable by mutating the code -- admitting any gap text reddens both.

A DECLARED FRAGMENT THE PAGE DOES NOT USE IS AN ERROR, the fisc-2sd direction: nothing else would catch a page that stopped wrapping, and the declaration is a claim about the document. Also proven failable.

Parse-time validation refuses blank, whitespace-carrying and duplicate entries.

Tested over testdata/pages/budget-p0167.txt, the real page. facts.jsonl byte-identical; no published rule declares one.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: 'pp.167-170 resolve with the correct row count' end to end. That needs the 23 division rules, which are fisc-5gk.2's work. This bead lands the mechanism and exercises it on the one block that motivated it. The five fragments are inventoried in this bead's 2026-08-21 note; three page breaks land mid-division (fisc-o15's note), so those rules need two Parts each.

title: Delete the table substrate and the markdown residue
description:
Pre-release clean cut. Zero rules use substrate: table, and no non-test Go code reads label_fingerprint/content_hash/bbox/row_page_lines outside ResolveTable.

DELETE:
- TableLocator (rule.go:210-238), ResolveTable + checkCentroid (resolve.go:650-745), corpus.Table/TablesOn/Centroid/FirstRow (~40% of internal/corpus), 382 table artifacts, 4 table fixtures, 2 tests.

title: StatedTotals cannot read a label-less totals row that shares a line
description:
Budget Book p67's expenditure totals row and its TRANSFER OUT: row extract onto
ONE physical line:

  ... $1,061,355 ... $26,544,515 28,584,740 36,047,736 - - 1,137,050 900,550 40,000 612,000

StatedTotals reads a label-less part's totals as the first MAXIMAL run of
consecutively parsable amounts on the anchor's line and requires that run to be
exactly one per column. Here the run is 16 amounts, not 8, so
CheckTotals(spine-expenditures, p67) returns ErrNotFound and eight columns of
the published spine go unchecked by the document's own total. No stop_at fixes
it from the rule file: blk.End is already at the first totals token; the problem
is the shape of the line after it. (The revenue half of p67 ties only because
its totals row happens to end its line.)

FIX: for a label-less part, blk.End is BY CONSTRUCTION the first token of the
totals row, so the totals are the first n consecutively parsable amounts from
that exact offset. The maximal-run rule exists to stop a totals LABEL containing
a bare number ("Total 2022 COP Construction Fund") from being read as a figure,
which can only happen on the labelled path -- so keep the maximal-run rule where
LabelsFrom == 0 and take the first n where it is set.

Then in internal/mapping/mappings_test.go: delete
TestP67ExpenditureTotalsCannotBeRead, set spineTiedColumns to 24, and drop
"spine-expenditures p67" from the unchecked list in TestPublishedSpineResolves.
Those eight columns are currently tied instead by
TestPublishedSpineBalancesPerFundGroup, which reconciles all six fund groups in
both years against the city's printed TOTAL SOURCES / TOTAL USES rows.
close_reason: Duplicate of fisc-gxt, filed independently for the same defect within minutes. Fixed there. Note the fix taken differs from the one proposed here: rather than dropping the maximal-run requirement for label-less parts, amountRun now also considers a run's $-PREFIXED prefix when the maximal run is the wrong width. That keeps the maximal-run guard on both paths and uses the distinction the document itself draws -- totals rows are $-marked, data rows bare -- instead of trusting blk.End's position.

API: Load(fsys fs.FS) (*Registry, error), Category(slug), Assignable(slug), FundGroup(name) checked against funds.yaml type values, Fund(number), ConstraintTier(fund). Consumers declare their own narrow interface (byob-interfaces.2, as internal/mapping/resolve.go does with 'type doc interface') rather than importing this package's concrete types.

title: Labelled read cannot handle a standalone $ token
description:
amount.Parse("$") is an error ('no digits, only currency or bracket characters'), and 246 of 786 corpus pages emit $ as its own whitespace-delimited token: 'Total Uses 6/30/24 $ 123,228,190 $ 14,507,398'. The labelled read takes the next N whitespace-delimited tokens after a row label, so on those pages it reads [$, 123,228,190, $, 14,507,398] and fails.

pp.66-67 contain zero standalone $ tokens, so fisc-mq4.2 is unaffected and the failure is closed, not silent. But the labelled read is described as the general text mode and is not yet general.

Do NOT fix by making amount.Parse accept a bare $ -- that would weaken the fail-closed grammar. The join belongs in the resolver's tokenizer, which knows it is looking for N amounts and can merge a currency-only token with the one that follows it.
acceptance_criteria: A page whose rows print '$ 1,234' resolves; amount.Parse still rejects a bare $; a token that is currency-only and NOT followed by an amount is still an error.
notes:
2026-08-18 A REAL PAGE NOW SHOWS IT, and it is committed. ACFR p177's FY2016 row prints '$ 60,193,384' -- the dollar sign as its OWN token before each of its eight figures, while the nine rows beneath it print bare numbers. So the standalone-$ shape is not hypothetical and not confined to pages out of scope: it makes ACFR p177 unreadable by the resolver, which is why internal/mapping/acfr_p177_test.go parses that page with strings.Fields instead of a rule and says so. The memory scope-pages-are-dense ('zero standalone $ tokens') was measured over Budget Book pp.127-140 and 167-170 and remains true of them; it was never a statement about the ACFR. Fixture: testdata/pages/acfr-p0177.txt.
2026-08-21 PEER REVIEW: THE OBVIOUS FIX BREAKS THE PROVENANCE CLAIM. Two things.

(1) THE JOIN MUST NOT FUSE THE TOKEN. This bead says "the join belongs in the
resolver's tokenizer, which knows it is looking for N amounts". If that join
SYNTHESIZES a token -- `$1,234,567` -- the fact's published Token and Offset
stop pointing at bytes that exist on the page. internal/mapping/resolve.go
:559-560 copies tk.off and tk.text straight onto the Value and thence onto the
fact, and fact-offset-points-at-token (internal/check/facts.go:198) asserts
text[Offset:Offset+len(Token)] == Token exactly. The page bytes at the `$` are
`"$      1,2"`, so every fact on every such row would fail that check.

This is not a corner: ACFR p163 has 59 standalone `$`, p165 39, p167 40, p169
20 -- i.e. precisely fisc-4ua.4's slice.

REQUIRED SHAPE: Token/Offset keep pointing at the printed NUMBER; the `$` is
consumed as a prefix by the caller deciding how many amounts it has, never
merged into the token. Add to acceptance:
TestOffsetStillPointsAtTheFigureWhenTheDollarIsItsOwnToken.

Note this ALSO disposes of the fisc-bau claim that a raw page slice
text[first.off : last.off+len(last.text)] handles `$            -` for free --
that works only because the slice is CONTIGUOUS PAGE BYTES. A join across a
whitespace run in a whitespace-splitting tokenizer is not the same operation.

(2) THREE CALLERS, THREE CONTRACTS, AND A NEWLINE HAZARD. tokens() feeds
labelledValues (takes toks[:ncols]), positionalValues (resolve.go:566-580,
asserts len(toks) == want EXACTLY) and StatedTotals (resolve.go:622, scans for a
maximal run). A blanket join changes all three. And `\n` is whitespace in
isSpace (resolve.go:846), so a line-terminal `$` would join to the FIRST TOKEN OF
THE NEXT LINE. Any fix has to be scoped to a caller that knows it is reading a
row, not applied in the splitter.

Also: stop_at: "$" is load-bearing at mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027
.yaml:191 and :279 -- both label-less p67 parts end at the first `$`, which is
also where StatedTotals starts (resolve.go:611-620). A plain substring search
today, so it is safe, but nothing says so and this bead is the change that would
break it.

(3) THE COUNT IS 236, NOT 246. Re-measured across five tokenisation definitions
and cross-checked against the -bbox substrate. The 246 figure also appears in
internal/amount/amount_test.go:150 and should be corrected there in the same
change. It is NOT an xberg-era leftover -- the comment post-dates the poppler
switch, so it was wrong when written.
close_reason:
Landed in dde657b. dropCurrencyMarks in internal/mapping/resolve.go drops a
token that is a currency mark and nothing else, in the resolver's labelled
read, where the caller knows it is looking for N amounts.

THE GRAMMAR IS UNTOUCHED, which the bead required: amount.Parse still rejects a
bare "$", and internal/amount's TestBareCurrencyMarkStaysARejection still pins
it. The resolver is now the one place that knows the mark can stand alone.

DROPPED, NOT JOINED -- and the bead's own suggested shape ("the join belongs in
the resolver's tokenizer") would have broken the provenance claim. Value carries
the token text and offset straight to the published fact, and
fact-offset-points-at-token asserts text[Offset:Offset+len(Token)] == Token
against the page. Page bytes at a detached mark are "$      1,2", so a
synthesized "$1,234" fails on every row it touches -- 158 ACFR statistical
pages, exactly fisc-4ua.4's slice. Found in peer review before implementation
and recorded on this bead on 2026-08-21.

A mark with no figure after it is an ERROR, per the acceptance criteria: that is
a read that has run off the end of the row, and shortening the token list would
hide the overrun the column guard exists to catch.

PROVEN FAILABLE BY MUTATING THE CODE, twice. Making the drop a no-op reddens all
three tests. JOINING the mark instead of dropping it reddens the two that read a
figure -- so the suite now refuses by name the fix this change rejected.

SCOPE: labelledValues only. positionalValues keeps its exact len(toks)==want
guard and StatedTotals its maximal-run scan; neither is touched, and pp.66-67
print no detached mark, so facts.jsonl is byte-identical and fisc verify is
unchanged at 19 passed / 0 failed / 5 vacuous.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT UNBLOCK, stated because the bead's BLOCKS edge implies it
does. fisc-4ua.4 still cannot read ACFR p177 end to end: its rows carry eleven
columns and the tenth is a percentage ("2.5%"), which amount.Parse rejects, and
a rule cannot stop short of it because checkGap requires the gap between one
row's last figure and the next row's label to be empty. Recorded on fisc-4ua.4.
That is why the end-to-end test is inline with p177's spacing copied, rather
than over the fixture.

Also corrected 246 -> 236 pages in internal/amount's sibling comment; the figure
was wrong when written, not stale.

title: Declared per-part allowance for the document's own rounding
description:
The spine ties exactly, but 'all totals tie exactly' is NOT a property of this corpus and must not be hardened into one. A correct label-anchored read of Budget Book p127 Total Property Taxes gives 58,179,467 against a printed 58,179,468. Ten more blocks are off by |delta| <= $5, every one in the FY2023-24 Actual column: pp. 111, 128, 129, 131, 135, 168, 172, 173, 181, 183. Verified by hand on p127 (the other three columns tie exactly) and p129/p172.

This is rounding in the DOCUMENT, not in the read. CheckTotals currently demands exact equality, so mapping stalls at p127 on a correct read.

Wanted: a per-part 'stated_total_delta' the rule author writes down and justifies -- never a silent tolerance, and never a global epsilon. The declaration is the point: it records that a human looked at the discrepancy and found it to be the city's rounding.
acceptance_criteria: A rule can declare an expected discrepancy for one part; CheckTotals accepts exactly that delta and no other; an undeclared discrepancy still fails; p127 maps with the delta declared.
close_reason:
Landed. stated_total_deltas on Part: a per-column, per-page declaration of a discrepancy in the DOCUMENT's own arithmetic. No global epsilon, no per-rule fuzz.

SHAPE. StatedTotalDelta{Column (1-based, matching how CheckTotals numbers columns when it reports a mismatch, so a failure message can be pasted into a declaration), Cents (STATED MINUS MAPPED, in cents always), Note (required)}. The parser refuses an out-of-range column, a duplicate column, a skipped column, a zero delta and a missing or whitespace-only note -- so a malformed declaration fails when the file is READ, not when it is applied.

BEHAVIOUR. CheckTotals accepts exactly the declared figure and nothing else. Three failure modes, told apart in the message: an undeclared discrepancy fails as before; a declared column off by a different amount fails naming both figures; and a declared column that now TIES EXACTLY also fails, telling the author to remove the declaration. That last one is the direction nothing else would catch -- if the city reissues the page with the arithmetic corrected, a tolerance would silently keep passing while the declaration became a false claim about the document.

THE ARITHMETIC, carried in the test rather than described. Budget Book p127's thirteen Property Taxes rows, from the committed fixture: FY2023-24 Actual 58,179,467 against a printed 58,179,468 (+1); FY2024-25 60,621,418, FY2025-26 64,143,762, FY2026-27 67,416,730, all exact. Three of four columns tying exactly is what makes the fourth the document's rounding rather than our read -- a misread row would not land on three columns and miss one by a dollar.

REPORTING. TotalsResult.Declared and Report.ColumnsTiedByDeclaration, printed whenever non-zero: '1 of those columns ties only to a declared delta in the document's own arithmetic'. A column that ties on the city's rounding must not be counted as one that ties exactly; that is the same principle as pkg/cmd/build/report.go's UNCHECKED lines.

TESTS. 5 test functions, 12 subtests, over the real p127 fixture rather than a synthetic page. All proven failable by mutation: neutering the CheckTotals branch reddens the three behaviour tests, neutering the parser loop reddens the two refusal tests. The report test caught a real grammar bug on the way in ('1 of those column tie'), now fixed by pluralising the verb rather than the noun.

facts.jsonl byte-identical -- the spine declares no deltas, so nothing moved. fisc verify 19 passed 0 failed. make pre-commit and lint clean.

fisc-5gk.1 and fisc-5gk.2 are no longer blocked by this.

title: Verify a label-less continuation part against its own totals
description:
Raised by code review of the rule schema and deferred, not fixed.

A rule's total_row is matched by LABEL, but a continuation part carries no labels at all -- Budget Book p67's totals row is positional like everything else on that page. So the single most valuable check available (the document checking our work) currently cannot run on exactly the pages that most need it, since a label-less page is also the one where a positional read is most fragile.

Resolve before or with the resolver. Options worth weighing: give Part its own optional total spec (a positional index, or 'the first line whose figures are $-prefixed', which is how p67 actually reads); or treat the continuation's totals row as an extra positional row with a reserved label. Whichever is chosen, the assertion must be per-column: p67 prints four fund-group totals ($27,145,882 / $0 / $28,465,560 / $18,969,834 for FY2026), and the M0 spike confirmed all four tie exactly.
close_reason: CheckTotals asserts per column and is production-callable, not test-only. A label-less part reads its stated totals from the stop_at boundary, which is how p67 prints them ('$' is both the block terminator and the first character of $27,145,882). StatedTotals takes the first maximal run of exactly one-amount-per-column within the anchor's line: maximal because totals labels contain bare numbers, exact because a doubled totals line must fail rather than guess, line-bound because the next row's figures would extend the run. All four p67 fund-group columns tie.

title: Use go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 for YAML parsing
description:
byob-release.10 says a dep outside the blessed set (cobra, go-cmp, modernc sqlite, goreleaser) needs its own decision bead. YAML is unavoidable: mappings/*.yaml, funds.yaml, taxonomy.yaml and sources.yaml are all hand-edited and carry #@cite comments, which rules out JSON.

DECISION: go.yaml.in/yaml/v3, pinned to v3.0.5.

Why not gopkg.in/yaml.v3: same code originally, but frozen at v3.0.1 (2022). go.yaml.in/yaml is the YAML organization's maintained continuation and a drop-in replacement.

Why not v4: v4.0.0-rc.5 is still a release candidate.

Note Python cannot parse YAML here at all -- PyPI is blocked in this sandbox and pyyaml is not installed. That is deliberate rather than a workaround: tools/extract.py discovers work from data/pdf/<doc-id>.pdf and records the source sha256 independently, so fisc verify cross-checking it against sources.yaml is a genuine check rather than two readers of one file. Do not add a YAML dependency to the Python side without revisiting that.
close_reason: go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 v3.0.5 added and in use by internal/mapping.

description: Every fact with its source link, and a downloadable CSV. This is the project's real differentiator over the city's own OpenGov page, and it is nearly free once the fact store exists. title: Ten-year trends from the ACFR Statistical Section
description: The richest and cleanest dataset in the corpus, and it needs no joint-distribution inference. ACFR pp.162-195, ~25 ten-year tables: fund balances p163-171, assessed value p173, demographics p180, principal employers p182, FTEs by function, capital assets p184, operating indicators p185, redevelopment debt coverage p194. Verified present by probe.
notes:
2026-08-18 THE SOURCE PAGE HAS A DEFECT, found committing it as a fixture. ACFR p177 (ten-year schedule of outstanding debt, Statistical Section) reconciles row by row against the city's own printed totals for nine of ten years; FY2024's total is short by 176,292, EXACTLY that row's Financed Purchases figure -- the column first used that year. A whole column missing from a total, not the <=$5 rounding fisc-2sd declares, so it cannot be handled with stated_total_deltas without a note saying which column the city dropped. Pinned by internal/mapping/acfr_p177_test.go against testdata/pages/acfr-p0177.txt. Also note the page is a live fisc-yun: its FY2016 row prints a standalone '$' before each figure, so the resolver cannot read it today.
2026-08-21 fisc-yun LANDED (dde657b) AND IT IS NOT ENOUGH FOR p177. The bead's
DEPENDS ON edge to fisc-yun implied the standalone-$ fix would make this page
readable. It does not, and the remaining obstacle is unowned.

p177's rows carry ELEVEN columns and the tenth is a PERCENTAGE -- "2.5%" --
which amount.Parse rejects as "not a recognized number", correctly. Verified.

A rule cannot simply stop at column nine either: labelledValues advances the
cursor to the end of the last MAPPED token, and checkGap then requires the text
between that point and the next row's label to be whitespace. The unmapped tail
"$ 88,896,362  2.5% $ 1,009" is not, so the read fails as an unmapped row.

Nor can the column be declared skip: true. parseRow calls amount.Parse BEFORE
it consults row.Skip || col.Skip (internal/mapping/resolve.go), so a skipped
column still has to parse. That ordering is deliberate -- a skipped column still
has to be a cell -- so this is not a bug to fix in passing.

SO THIS LANE OWNS A DECISION IT DID NOT KNOW IT HAD: how a rule reads a table
whose columns are not all amounts. Options, none free:
  (a) a column kind that is parsed by a different grammar (ratio/percent), which
      is a real extension of the rule schema;
  (b) a column declared as present-but-unparsed, which weakens "every cell is a
      cell" and needs to be fail-closed about what it will swallow;
  (c) a part that stops mid-row, which needs checkGap to know a row can end
      before its printed line does.
Decide before writing YAML for pp.162-194, because the statistical section is
full of ratios, per-capita figures and percentages -- that is what a statistical
section IS.

ALSO CORRECTED, from peer review: this bead says the ten-year tables are at
pp.162-195 and names fund balances at "p163-171". Measured: the statistical
section runs pp.162-194 (p195 is blank), and the fund-balance tables are
pp.167-169 -- "Fund Balances of Governmental Funds" p167, "Changes in Fund
Balances" pp.168-169. pp.163-166 are Net Position; pp.170-172 are sales tax.
p173 assessed value is right.

title: Reconcile the p76 transfer schedule against the spine (it IS extractable)
description:
The premise this bead was written on is FALSE, and re-reading the page is what
found it. It said the schedule is unextractable -- "four disjoint text blocks
with mismatched cardinalities (21 source labels on one line; destinations split
18/1/3; amounts across three lines)" -- and asked for hand transcription. That
was an xberg-era observation. The poppler migration (fisc-yqv) retired it and
nobody went back to look.

pdftotext -layout gives 22 clean rows, ONE PRINTED LINE EACH:

  Transfer From Wastewater   to Stormwater   -   440,000   460,000   460,000   (4)

The -bbox substrate agrees token for token; the lines rebuilt independently from
geometry give the same 22 rows, and there are no hidden rows behind the two wide
vertical gaps (y 426->447 and 460->481 are whitespace, not dropped text). This
is an ordinary labelled read, not a transcription.

WHAT TIES, SUMMED FROM GEOMETRY

  column              mapped        printed       delta
  FY2023-24 Actual    23,089,626    29,947,677    6,858,051
  FY2024-25 Revised   22,679,706    27,679,706    5,000,000
  FY2025-26 Budget    21,525,997    21,525,997    0
  FY2026-27 Budget    21,624,633    21,624,633    0

The two historical columns miss by MILLIONS, one of them by exactly $5,000,000.
That is not the <= $5 document-rounding class (see the memory
totals-tie-exactly-only-on-the-spine), so it is NOT a stated_total_deltas
candidate -- a declaration there would be a false claim about the document. Map
the two budget columns. The historical pair needs its own investigation and
must not be quietly declared away.

EVERY GROUP TIES TO THE SPINE

  IN  (p76 section total vs p66/p67 TRANSFER IN)   FY2026       FY2027
    General Fund                                   480,400      486,735    exact
    Enterprise Funds                            13,247,000   13,330,000    exact
    Debt Service Funds                           6,984,597    6,969,898    exact
    Special Revenue Funds                          814,000      838,000    exact
    Permanent Funds                                      0            0    no spine column
  OUT (p76 source total vs p66/p67 TRANSFER OUT)
    General Fund                                10,037,797   10,146,598    exact

THE RESIDUAL DOES NOT CLOSE. This bead's old note claimed it did. p76's grand
total IS the transfers-in side, exactly, so mapping the page pairs $21,525,997
of legs and leaves headline.transfer_residual_cents ($38,086,737) where it is.
What it does is LOCALISE it:

    Capital Funds        28,584,740   itemised nowhere on p76
    Enterprise Funds      9,353,147   out-flows with no listed destination
    Special Revenue         108,850
    Internal Service         40,000
                         ----------
                         38,086,737   == headline.transfer_residual_cents

That is worth more than closing it would have been: the residual is a property
of the CITY'S OWN SCHEDULE, not of this backlog. The shipped caveat said the
opposite; corrected alongside this bead.

SCOPE OF THIS BEAD: reconciliation only. NO FACTS PUBLISHED. Because every
group ties exactly, p76 rows ARE the spine's transfer money -- publishing them
at all-funds-gross doubles the city's transfers with every check green, which
is fisc-u2v's mechanism verbatim in the transfer lane. Publishing is fisc-5gk.3.1.

COSTS THIS BEAD NEVER MENTIONED, all live:
- registry.Fund has no Aliases field (Category does). p76 prints abbreviations
  -- "Low Income Hsng", "Traffic Imp Fee", "State Gas Tax" -- and several are
  ambiguous between an operating fund and its CIP twin. Blocks publishing only.
- p0076.txt:351 "Connection" is a wrapped label mid-section: a live fisc-0cs
  instance outside the department pages. The reconciliation splits the
  Enterprise section into two parts around it.
- Footnote markers "(10)" are PARENTHESISED NEGATIVES to amount.Parse. Nothing
  reads them today only because labelledValues truncates to ncols.
acceptance_criteria: the 22 rows resolve through the real resolver; both budget columns sum to the page's printed grand total exactly; each section total equals the spine's TRANSFER IN cell and General Fund sources equal TRANSFER OUT; the residual is shown to be the document's, not the backlog's; facts.jsonl byte-identical
notes:
2026-08-18 RECONCILIATION LANDED. internal/mapping/testdata/transfers-p76.yaml -- six rules, 22 rows, 88 values -- resolves through the REAL resolver against testdata/pages/budget-p0076.txt, and internal/mapping/transfers_p76_test.go compares it against the PUBLISHED spine rules rather than against typed-in figures. Five tests, all proven failable by mutation: dropping a row reddens the read, mis-slugging one column's fund_group reddens the per-group tie, un-skipping the footnote column yields 110 values instead of 88 (which is also the proof that amount.Parse reads '(10)' as negative ten dollars). facts.jsonl byte-identical; nothing is published.

WHAT IT COST, and this is the new finding: the read only works with KERNING-EXACT row labels. A row's identity here is two printed fields with an arbitrary space run between them, and Row.Label is one substring -- source-only fails with 'cannot parse amount "to"', destination-only fails checkGap. Filed as fisc-ffy, which now blocks fisc-5gk.3.1. The fixture embeds the space runs deliberately, with the reason in its header, and is safe only because TestFixturesAreVerbatimCopies pins the page byte for byte.

The shipped caveat and docs/sankey-contract.md no longer tell readers the residual is waiting on this mapping.
close_reason:
Landed in 45235d3. internal/mapping/testdata/transfers-p76.yaml (six rules, 22 rows, 88 values) resolves through the real resolver against a byte-pinned fixture; internal/mapping/transfers_p76_test.go (5 tests, all proven failable by mutation) compares it against the PUBLISHED spine rules rather than typed-in figures.

WHAT IT PROVED. Both budget columns tie to the printed grand total to the cent. Every destination fund group ties to the spine's TRANSFER IN cell exactly and the General Fund's out-flows tie to TRANSFER OUT exactly. p76's grand total IS the transfers-in side, so the $38,086,737 residual is the city's own and mapping the page cannot close it -- the shipped caveat, docs/sankey-contract.md, internal/check/graph.go's doc comment and the published spine's note all said otherwise and were corrected in the same commit.

WHAT IT COST. The read works only with kerning-exact row labels (fisc-ffy), the footnote markers need a skipped column because amount.Parse reads '(10)' as negative ten dollars, and the Enterprise section is read as two rules around a wrapped label (fisc-0cs). Publishing is fisc-5gk.3.1 and remains blocked on fisc-u2v, fisc-4rh, fisc-0cs, fisc-8dz and fisc-ffy.

FY2023-24 Actual: 2,543,421 + 1,129,921 = 3,673,342 mapped against a printed
$3,673,343, so the declaration is +1. fisc-o15's note says "p168 Finance -1".

(2) THE COUNT IS UNSETTLED AND THE TWO MEASUREMENTS DISAGREE. An independent
pass over pp.168-170 during the fisc-1wr.2 rewrite found SIX discrepant totals,

total_row of (see the cross-rule rollup bead), so they may need a rollup
assertion or a stated reason rather than a delta -- which is a different
mechanism, not a different number.

WHAT MAKES THE TWO MEASUREMENTS DIFFER, and it is worth knowing before
enumerating: the document is internally consistent at the DIVISION-TOTAL level
and not at the object-row level. p168's ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES TOTAL is
$6,311,564. The three printed division Totals sum to 6,311,564 EXACTLY. The six
OBJECT rows -- which are what become facts -- sum to 6,311,563. Finance's own $1
is absorbed by its printed Total and reappears one level up.

So a delta measured against printed subtotals and a delta measured against the
mapped object rows are DIFFERENT NUMBERS on the same page, and only the second
is what stated_total_deltas declares.

ACTION FOR THIS LANE: enumerate every discrepancy by summing OBJECT ROWS against
each printed total, in the stated-minus-mapped direction, with the enumeration
committed as a test that reads the pages rather than as a list in a bead. Both

title: pages.yml deploy
description:
On push to main: checkout WITHOUT LFS (the site does not need the PDFs), fisc build, fisc export -o dist --clean, upload-pages-artifact, deploy-pages. Actions pinned by SHA.

Keeping LFS out of CI matters: data/pdf/** is the ONLY thing in LFS (3 files, ~67MB) and GitHub's free tier is 1GB/month of bandwidth, so ~14 LFS checkouts exhaust it. data/extracted/ is ordinary git, so a no-LFS checkout still carries everything fisc reads.

Consequence for the frontend, in two parts:
- The PDFs ARE in LFS, so raw.githubusercontent.com serves pointer text for them. PDF deep links must therefore target the city's canonical URL with #page=N.
- The extracted page text is NOT in LFS and raw would serve it correctly. Citations still point at the github.com BLOB view, for a different reason: the blob view has line numbers, history and the rest of the document beside it, and the artifacts are pages/pNNNN.txt -- .txt, not .md, since fisc-yqv -- precisely so that view renders them verbatim instead of collapsing the runs of spaces that ARE the column grid.
notes:
2026-08-17 (from lane A4, fisc-1wr.5): `fisc verify --full` now exists and is the only thing in the project that reads data/pdf/. It recomputes each PDF's sha256 and compares it against BOTH data/sources.yaml and the extraction manifest. A monthly scheduled workflow for it is this bead's, deliberately not added in A4.

Two things that job must get right: it needs `lfs: true` AND must not inherit GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE (ci.yml sets it workflow-wide, so a new workflow file is cleaner than a job in ci.yml), because a pointer-only checkout makes the check report ERROR ('an unsmudged Git LFS pointer ... run `git lfs pull`') rather than a false failure -- correct, but it means the job would never actually hash anything. And ~67 MB per run against GitHub's 1 GB/month free LFS bandwidth is why it is monthly rather than per-push: ci.yml's header note has the arithmetic.
2026-08-18 DEFERRED, landing plan. There is no git remote on this repository, so there is nowhere to deploy and ci.yml has never executed (see fisc-0ux). This bead is not actionable until the owner creates the remote; it was sitting in bd ready as though it were. title: internal/project: projection interface + sankey
description:
One file per projection behind a common interface (byob-interfaces.1), with site/data holding one JSON per projection. PUT THE SEAM IN NOW, while there is exactly one projection -- retrofitting after three exist is the expensive version.

Sankey specifics: link.kind in {external, internal_transfer, internal_service}; the headline total sums ONLY external links, because naively summing the expenditure column gives $313,708,146 when the city spends $254,095,412 (a 23% inflation from transfers counted twice). Transfers are paired transfer-out/transfer-in synthetic nodes sharing a transfer_id, which keeps the graph acyclic. Explicit fund-balance-draw / fund-balance-contribution nodes rather than silent padding. Contra-revenue (ERAF -$15,857,875, RPTTF -$1,891,804 in FY26, ~26% of gross property tax) nets into its parent with sign: contra -- a Sankey cannot render a negative link.
notes:
AMENDED 2026-08-16, before implementation, so the contract A3 codes against and the bead a reviewer reads agree.

1. link.kind gains a FOURTH value: {external, internal_transfer, internal_service, fund_balance}. A fund-balance draw or contribution is not external money and must not enter the headline, and labelling it internal_transfer would be false -- it is not a transfer between funds, it is a fund drawing on or adding to its own accumulated balance. Explicit fund-balance-draw / fund-balance-contribution nodes were already required by this bead; they need a link kind of their own.

2. internal_service must actually be USED, not merely defined. Internal Service Fund revenue is $18,969,834 of charges billed to other City departments, and the matching $25,077,367 of ISF spending sits inside the $254,095,412 citywide figure. The scope is all-funds-GROSS. So the projection emits BOTH all_funds_gross_revenue_cents/_expenditure_cents AND external_revenue_cents/_expenditure_cents computed net of internal_service links. Naming a key 'external' for a number that includes internal charges would reproduce, at 6.3%, the same class of error this bead exists to prevent at 23%.

3. Node ids derive from taxonomy.yaml slugs. 'ADDITION TO RESERVES' is fund-balance/reserve-increase (that string is its document_term); do not invent a new slug for it.

4. fund-balance/draw and fund-balance/contribution are OUR sign-decomposition of the published 'CHANGE IN WORKING CAPITAL' row. They are an inference and carry derived: true with a rationale and source_note. The published stock rows (fund-balance/beginning, /ending) are facts but are excluded from the graph as stocks rather than flows, and metadata.caveats must say so.

5. Output path is <output>/data/<projection>.json, so 'fisc export -o dist' writes dist/data/ and 'fisc export -o site' writes site/data/ -- one code path. The .gitignore comment claiming site/data/ is written by 'fisc build' is stale and is corrected in the same change.

6. Ship the transfer-unmatched residual node NOW, not with the coverage ratchet. Transfers out $59,612,734 vs transfers in $21,525,997 is a $38.1M gap because the p76 schedule (fisc-5gk.3) is unmapped, so transfer_id is empty on every link and this bead's 'paired legs sharing a transfer_id' property is currently vacuous. fisc-1wr.4's second paragraph specifies exactly this residual node. A caveat string cannot go stale-red; a residual node can.

title: Automate the four break-it scenarios as CI tests
description:
These are the acceptance test for the provenance claim, and they target the failure modes that actually matter rather than the ones that are easy to trigger:

Assert on behavior, not call counts (byob-testing.3).
