title: checkCounterpart's identical-legs guard compares the row's fund group, which every published rule leaves empty
description:
internal/mapping/parse.go, checkCounterpart, the arm that refuses a
counterpart identical to its near leg. It compares cp.FundGroup against the
ROW s FundGroup:

    row.Category == cp.Category && row.Fund == cp.Fund && row.FundGroup == cp.FundGroup

On every published rule the row declares `fund:` and NOTHING ELSE -- the fund
GROUP comes from the column, because a p76 section is one receiving group and
the column is where that lives. So row.FundGroup is "" on all 22 p76 rows, the
third clause is false against any real counterpart, and the arm never fires.

Confirmed: a counterpart duplicating its near leg parses cleanly and fails much
later, in `fisc build`, as `id ... claimed twice: rule X ... rule X`. That is
CheckUniqueIDs doing the work, and parse.go:993-999 already names it as the
backstop -- but the arm s own comment claims to catch this case at parse time,
and its test passes only because the fixture row sets a FundGroup no published
rule uses.

The fix is not obvious and that is why this is a bead rather than a patch: a row
applies to every column of every part, so "the row s effective fund group" is not
one value at the point checkCounterpart runs. Either compare against the parts
columns (all of them, refusing if any collides), or drop the arm and let
CheckUniqueIDs own it -- in which case its error message should say what
happened, because "claimed twice: rule X ... rule X" does not read as "your
counterpart duplicates its own near leg".

Found by /code-review of the p76 lane, 2026-08-24. The guard dates from c5d11ef;
p76 is the first published user of counterparts and the first to expose it.
acceptance_criteria: a counterpart identical to its near leg is refused with a message that says so, at whichever stage owns the check; the test uses a row shaped like a published one (fund on the row, group on the column)

title: revenue-detail's hand-off arm grants on presence, never on amount
description:
internal/check/revenuedetail.go:272 (arm 2 of resolveRevenueExceptions).

The hand-off for the one declared exception -- (transfer_in, transfers/in,
general), which pp.127-130 do not print -- is granted when the covering scope
carries a fact for that slice at all: covers[k] > 0. It never compares the
AMOUNT. So the report line flips from arm 4s "NOT RECONCILED ... $480,400
checked against no detail" to arm 2s "reconciled by scope transfers-by-fund
instead" with no arithmetic added by that flip.

MITIGATED, NOT MOOT, since transfers-detail-ties-to-spine landed. That check
does compare the amount -- p76s General Fund in-legs sum to 480,400 / 486,735
against the spines own cell, clause (a), zero tolerance -- so the money IS
checked, by a different check. What remains wrong is that revenue-detail says
"reconciled by scope X" on the strength of a fact existing, and would go on
saying it if X published one cent under that key. The claim and the evidence for
it live in different places and nothing couples them.

Options: have arm 2 compare covers[k] against the spine cell itself; or reword
the arm so it says "handed off to X" rather than "reconciled by X", and let the
covering check be the one that says reconciled. The second is cheaper and is
probably right -- a check should not assert another checks conclusion -- but it
weakens the report line a reader currently trusts.

Found by /code-review of the p76 lane, 2026-08-24.
acceptance_criteria: either arm 2 compares the amount, or its wording stops claiming a reconciliation it did not perform; a test covers the case where the covering scope carries a fact of the wrong value

title: rule-funds-match-their-headings claims a total only for fund-bearing rules, and contradicts itself on a mismatch
description:
Two defects in internal/check/rulefunds.go, both reproduced by running the
check, both found by /code-review of the p76 lane on 2026-08-24.

(1) A MAPPED SECTION IS REPORTED AS UNCLAIMED. Run (rulefunds.go:109-124) does:

    fund, mixed := declaredFund(ru)
    ... mixed finding ...
    if fund == 0 { continue }
    setPage(pages, ...); set(claimed, f.DocID, ru.TotalRow); subjects++

so set(claimed, ...) sits BELOW the early continue. A rule that maps a fund
section with fund_group-only columns and no fund: declares no fund, returns 0,
and never claims its printed total -- and clause 2s unclaimedFundTotals then
reports "no rule or rollup declares that total" about a section that IS mapped.
Reproduced. Move the set above the continue: claiming a total is a statement
that SOME rule reads that heading, which is true whether or not the rule
declares a fund number.

(2) THE MISMATCH ARM PRODUCES TWO FINDINGS THAT CONTRADICT EACH OTHER.
rulefunds.go:152: when an anchor resolves to a DIFFERENT fund than the rule
declares, the mismatch finding fires but `named` is not set, so the !named arm
fires too. Reproduced on the diffs own "a fund swapped for another of the same
type" case:

  finding 1: ... "Total Water Utility Fund" governs it, which is fund 500
  finding 2: ... is anchored to nothing on the page   [while listing that total]

Both are about the same rule and the second is false. Set named = true in the
mismatch arm, or skip the !named arm once any anchor resolved.

Neither is a wrong-answer-about-the-corpus defect today -- the committed corpus
declares a fund on every column of every fund-bearing rule -- but (1) becomes
live the moment a schedule declares its fund per ROW, which is exactly what
Budget Book p76 does (fisc-bhe, fisc-5gk.3.1).
acceptance_criteria: a rule with fund_group-only columns claims its printed total; a fund mismatch produces exactly one finding; a test covers each, reproduced against the real check rather than a fixture assertion alone

title: verify's help promises --strict fails on any vacuous check, and it has not since 40943db
description:
Three places in pkg/cmd/verify/verify.go still describe the pre-40943db
exit-code contract, and the exit-code contract is the thing that text exists to
state.

  :18-20   package doc     "--strict is what turns those into a failure"
  :103-105 command Long    "A vacuous check ... exits 0 today because most of the
                            budget is still unmapped, and fails under --strict."
  :136-137 the flag itself "Fail if any check had nothing to check"
  (:110-117 the Example block repeats the flags wording)

MEASURED ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS: `fisc verify --strict` reports 27 passed,
0 failed, 3 VACUOUS, 1 skipped -- and EXITS 0, printing "every one is declared
with the bead that retires it, so --strict passes".

The real contract is Report.Failed() (internal/check/report.go:174-181), and it
has three arms, none of which is the one the help gives:
  - Counts.Fail > 0 || Counts.Error > 0
  - len(StaleDeclarations()) > 0  -- REGARDLESS of --strict
  - r.Strict && len(r.Undeclared) > 0

So --strict fails on an UNDECLARED vacuous check, and a declaration that has
stopped being true fails whether or not --strict was passed. Both halves are
missing from the help, and the second is the one a reader cannot guess.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A DOC NIT. ci.yml runs the --strict step with no
--full, and that texts promise is what a contributor reads to predict whether
their commit will redden CI. Also stale: README.md:58 says "26 checks over the
fact store and the graph"; All() returns 31.

Found by /code-review of HEAD~4..HEAD, 2026-08-24.
acceptance_criteria: all three sites in verify.go state that --strict fails on an UNDECLARED vacuous check and that a stale declaration fails regardless of --strict; README.md's check count is correct or stops naming one; a test pins the help text against the behaviour

title: fact.FromValues guards the far leg's column path but not its row path
description:
internal/fact/fact.go:250-262 guards the NEAR leg on both paths, naming
which one is missing:

  case rowPath == "":    missing = "row path (the row has neither category nor department)"
  case columnPath == "": missing = "column path (the column has no fund and the rule no scope)"

The counterpart branch added in c5d11ef guards only the far legs COLUMN path
(fact.go:304, "counterpart has no addressable column path"). RowPath(cpRow) is
computed at :314 (into MakeID) and :328 (into the RowPath field) with no
equivalent arm. cpRow.Category comes from cp.Category and cpRow.Department is
inherited from the near row, so a far leg whose counterpart declares no category
and whose row declares no department publishes row_path: "" AND AN ID HASHED
OVER IT -- an unaddressable fact rather than an error, which is the exact
failure the near-leg guard exists to prevent.

LATENT, NOT LIVE. checkCounterpart (internal/mapping/parse.go:955-972) refuses
an empty counterpart category and an empty fund_group, so nothing reachable
through the parser can produce it. The hole is open to any direct FromValues
caller -- tests today, and any future non-parse producer. Do not describe it on
the bead or in a commit message as a live defect.

THE ASYMMETRY IS ALSO IN THE WORDING. The :304 guard tests the raw cpCol fields
rather than the computed path, so its message can never take the near-legs
"has no addressable <what>" shape. Fix both: guard RowPath(cpRow) and columnPath
in one switch, worded like the near legs.

Found by /code-review of HEAD~4..HEAD, 2026-08-24.
acceptance_criteria: FromValues refuses a counterpart whose row path is empty, with a message naming which path is missing; a test constructs one directly (the parser cannot); the near and far guards read the same way

title: Four p76 rows cannot declare a fund the registry can check, and two cannot declare one at all
description:
Publishing p76 means declaring a fund at both ends of 22 rows. Four of them
cannot be declared the way the other eighteen can, and this was not on any bead.

(1) THE LAVWMA ROW HAS NO DESTINATION FUND. p0076.txt prints "Transfer From
    Wastewater  to LAVWMA / Wastewater" with "Connection" wrapped onto the next
    line. LAVWMA is a joint powers authority, not a City fund, and data/funds.yaml
    has no entry and no alias for it. internal/registry/fundlabel_test.go already
    asserts that this one of p76's thirteen destination strings FAILS by name --
    deliberately, because the alternative is silently picking Wastewater
    Connection Fees (623).

    So the near leg of that row has no fund number. Options: declare fund_group
    without a fund (ColumnPath then emits the group alone, which is addressable);
    add a funds.yaml entry for a non-fund payee, which would be a lie about the
    appendix; or omit the row, which loses money the page prints. Note the
    FY2026 and FY2027 figures are both "-", so the facts are published zeros --
    which makes this cheap to get wrong and cheap to get right.

(2) THREE ROWS PRINT NO SOURCE ANCHOR. "to Wastewater Replacement", "to 2022
    COPS" and "to Downtown LMD" continue their "Transfer From" from the row
    above. c5d11ef's Row.Counterpart means the rule DECLARES the payer rather
    than a reader inferring it, which solves the reading problem -- but it also
    means those three declared funds have no printed anchor on their own line to
    be checked against. So whatever fisc-bhe lands has to skip them or
    re-implement the carry-forward, and three of 22 rows are unguarded on the
    side where the operating/CIP ambiguity lives.

    The carry-forward itself is currently only in Go, at
    internal/mapping/transfers_p76_test.go, which fails hard if a row has no
    payer above it in its own block.

Found in peer review of the p76 landing plan, 2026-08-24.
close_reason: Landed in ced45b4. p76 publishes 88 facts at scope transfers-by-fund (22 rows x 2 budget years x 2 legs) and transfers-detail-ties-to-spine reconciles them in three clauses: IN exact with no constant, OUT-major with the printed to-CIP figures added back, OUT-non-major with capital+special-revenue+permanent collapsed. Doubling proven by measurement rather than argued: republished at all-funds-gross the GF in-leg goes 480,400 -> 960,800 while three graph checks stay green. Only the two budget columns are published. See each bead's own note for what it owed.

title: A row-level fund is invisible to rule-funds-match-their-headings
description:
4192ae4 landed "a hand-typed fund number is checked against the name the page
prints", which is the guard against a mistyped fund: internal/check/rulefunds.go
re-derives a rule's fund from the printed "Total <fund>" heading via
registry.FundByLabel and compares.

IT READS COLUMNS ONLY. declaredFund takes c.Fund from Parts[].Columns, so the
Row.Fund and Row.Counterpart.Fund that c5d11ef added are invisible to it, and a
page whose fund dimension is per-row does not enter its sweep at all.

THAT MATTERS MOST EXACTLY WHERE IT IS MISSING. p76's payer side is where the
operating/CIP twin ambiguity lives: fisc-8dz records five abbreviations that
each match an operating fund AND its CIP twin (Low Income Hsng, Traffic Imp Fee,
Host Comm Impact, Measure D, State Gas Tax). A leg keyed to the wrong twin moves
money between the capital and special-revenue columns -- the one pair
transfers-detail-ties-to-spine clause (c) cannot split, so the tie would stay
green. The equal-legs check would not see it either: both legs would still be
equal.

WHAT THE CHECK WOULD BE. p76 does not print "Total <fund>" headings; its fund
names are in the ROW ANCHORS. "Transfer From Low Income Hsng" ->
FundByLabel("Low Income Hsng") -> 200 must equal the declared counterpart fund.
So this is a NEW check reading row labels, not a clause added to the existing
one, and it makes the expected check count 29 rather than 28.

TWO ROWS IT CANNOT COVER, and they are named on their own bead: the LAVWMA row
has no fund to resolve to, and the three continuation rows print no source
anchor at all.

Found in peer review of the p76 landing plan, 2026-08-24, which claimed 4192ae4
already covered this.
notes:
2026-08-24 THE CHECK COUNT IN THE DESCRIPTION IS WRONG. It says landing this
'makes the expected check count 29 rather than 28'. check.All() returns 31
today (internal/check/check.go:161-197), and fisc verify reports 27 passed +
0 failed + 3 vacuous + 1 skipped = 31. The count goes 31 -> 32. The ratchets
that pin it are internal/check/checks_test.go:30-83 (the exhaustive want map),
:85 (Counts{Pass:17, Vacuous:13, Skipped:1}) and :102-104, plus
subject_test.go:224-291. README.md's '26 checks' was stale too and now names no
count at all -- the command prints one.

title: firstDifferingColumn returns an index that is out of range for the shorter slice, and the caller indexes both
description:
internal/mapping/resolve.go:1414-1421:

  func firstDifferingColumn(a, b []Column) int {
        if len(a) != len(b) {
                return min(len(a), len(b))
        }
        ...

and the only caller, resolve.go:1023, indexes BOTH slices at the returned value
to build its message:

  columnIdentity(effectiveColumns(first, bearers[0])[i])
  columnIdentity(effectiveColumns(rule, bearer)[i])

With len(a)=3 and len(b)=5 the helper returns 3, and a[3] panics. min() picks
the length of the SHORTER slice, which is one past its last valid index. The
defensive branch turns a would-be error into a crash.

UNREACHABLE TODAY and that is the whole point of the branch. CheckRollup's
width guard (resolve.go:1013-1020) refuses a length mismatch before this is
called, so the only way in is a second caller. The doc comment says exactly
that: "unreachable from CheckRollup, whose width guard runs before this, but the
helper reads as general and the next caller would inherit the same
one-caller-away hole fisc-t9h is about". The branch was added to be safe for
that next caller and is not.

TWO WAYS TO FIX, and they are different claims:

(a) Return -1 on a length mismatch and let the caller keep owning the width
    check. Honest, and it means the helper answers only the question its name
    asks.
(b) Return an index the caller can use, which means the helper must also tell
    the caller the slices differ in LENGTH rather than in content -- a second
    return value, or a sentinel the caller must handle.

Prefer (a) plus a doc comment saying the caller owns the width, because (b)
invites the caller to print "column 4 of a 3-column rule".

Either way the fix needs a test with a genuine length mismatch reaching the
helper, which today means calling it directly: the guard above means no rollup
can produce one.

Found by /code-review of the fisc-5gk.1 lane, 2026-08-24. Landed in a3adb0e.
acceptance_criteria: a length mismatch reaching firstDifferingColumn cannot panic the caller; a test calls it directly with slices of different lengths; the doc comment says who owns the width check

title: Factor the detail-ties-to-spine machinery at the second instance, before fisc-5gk.1 needs it
description:
internal/check/detail.go holds one <kind>-detail-ties-to-spine check
(expenditure-by-department, landed a430cec) and its arithmetic is entirely
generic. fisc-5gk.1 is the second instance and fisc-5gk.3.1 is already specified
as the third, so the shape is known rather than guessed and this is where the
memory principles-dry-kiss-solid says to abstract.

TWO THINGS BLOCK A NAIVE COPY, and they are the reason this is its own bead.

(1) detailKey is (year, basis, category) and gets away with it ONLY because
expenditureDetailFundGroup = "general" collapses that axis to a constant.
pp.127-140 span all six fund groups, so the revenue check needs the fund group
in the KEY.

(2) But the fund group must stay a FILTER for expenditure. Turn the pin into a
key component instead and the expenditure check meets the other five groups'
spine expenditure -- detail.go:27-28 measures that at ~$109M in FY2026 -- and
goes red over a correct corpus. Drop it from the key because "the pin handles
it" and the revenue check compares six groups under one key and ties on a sum
that happens to match, which is worse because it reports green.

So: the restriction FILTERS, the key ALWAYS carries the fund group, and the
expenditure check's keys all come out "general" by construction.

Landing it as its own commit rather than inside fisc-5gk.1 keeps a 7,000-line
coverage commit from also carrying a refactor of the check it depends on.
acceptance_criteria: the shared machinery is one file and the checks stay one per file with their own doc comments; facts.jsonl byte-identical and fisc verify output byte-identical before and after; a test pins that the restriction filters and the key carries the fund group, proven failable by mutating each direction
close_reason:
Landed. internal/check/detailtie.go carries detailRestriction, cellSum,
detailKey, detailSums, reconciledPairs, compareDetail, unionKeys and
describePairs; detail.go keeps the expenditure check and, more to the point, the
argument for ITS restriction, which is what is worth reading about it and does
not generalise.

detailKey is now (year, basis, fundGroup, category) and detailRestriction
carries {Kinds, FundGroup}. FundGroup filters; the key always carries the group.
Both directions of getting that backwards are pinned by
TestTheRestrictionFiltersAndTheKeyCarriesTheFundGroup and proven failable:
deleting the filter clause reddens it at "1 finding over 2 cells" (the fixture's
added enterprise expenditure cell being compared against a General Fund detail),
and dropping fundGroup from detailKey.String() reddens
TestTheDetailKeyNamesItsFundGroup.

PROVEN BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING RATHER THAN ASSUMED: facts.jsonl byte-identical, and
`fisc verify` output byte-identical against a binary built from the pre-refactor
detail.go -- diffed, not eyeballed. 24 passed / 0 failed / 4 vacuous / 1 skipped
either side. make pre-commit clean including golangci-lint, 0 issues.

One doc correction carried in: detail.go said "The corpus-wide exception budget
across the three detail scopes is zero". fisc-u2v declares one, for the General
Fund Transfers In row pp.127-130 do not print, so the budget is one and it is
not this schedule's. Also names the second compliant form of an exception that
fisc-u2v's 2026-08-23 correction allows -- saying in words that a cell is
unreconciled when no scope covers it -- which detail.go's comment omitted.

title: other-financing-sources is grounded after all: two citywide schedules exclude p139's $500
description:
data/taxonomy.yaml:266-289 carries `other-financing-sources` with `derived: true`
and a source_note that is explicitly UNGROUNDED: "which of the ten p66 categories
absorbs this line in the citywide roll-up is not printed anywhere in the
document ... Do not assert a parent for this entry until a schedule says so."

TWO SCHEDULES NOW SAY SO, and they agree. The answer is that it is absorbed by
NONE of them -- the citywide roll-ups exclude the line entirely.

THE ONE MEASURABLE INSTANCE. p0139.txt:56, Police Donations fund:

  Oth Financing Source            -            500              -             -

It is zero in FY2023-24, FY2025-26 and FY2026-27, so FY2024-25 revised is the
only column in which it can be tested -- and pp.66-67 print no revised column,
which is why the spine could never answer this.

THE EVIDENCE. Summing the 38 printed `Total <fund>` lines in the Special Revenue
run on pp.135-139 gives FY2024-25 = 19,666,619. Both citywide schedules print
19,666,119, exactly $500 less:

  p0063.txt:20  Special Revenue Funds   17,656,560  19,666,119  29,279,560  21,730,522
  p0192.txt:11  Special Revenue Funds   Revenues 18,980,619 + Transfers In 685,500
                                        = 19,666,119

Two pages produced by different roll-ups, agreeing to the cent, both omitting the
row. Every other special-revenue column ties exactly (FY2025-26, FY2026-27) or
within fisc-2sd's rounding (FY2023-24, +2), which is what makes the $500 the
line rather than noise.

WHAT TO DO WITH IT, and the options differ in strength:

(a) Update the source_note. It currently says the question is unanswerable from
    this document; that is no longer true and a stale UNGROUNDED marker is the
    same class of defect as a stale unprojectedScopes entry -- a declaration that
    has stopped describing the corpus.
(b) Do NOT give it a parent. The evidence says it is EXCLUDED from the roll-up,
    not that it belongs under one of the ten. Asserting a parent would be the
    inference the entry was written to refuse; recording exclusion is the finding.
(c) Note the consequence for fisc-5gk.1: the eleventh category is a detail-side
    key with NO spine counterpart in either budget year (both zero), so
    revenue-detail-ties-to-spine disposes of it as a zero-vs-absent cell. It
    would only ever bite if the city budgeted the line, and this bead is where
    the reader learns what happens then.

Found while settling fisc-wev, 2026-08-24, by summing pp.131-140 by fund group
against p0063 Table 2.
acceptance_criteria: data/taxonomy.yaml's other-financing-sources source_note records that p0063 Table 2 and p0192 both exclude the line, with the $500 and both citations; the entry still asserts no parent, and says why exclusion is not a parent; the consequence for revenue-detail-ties-to-spine is stated

title: General Fund CIP Reserves has no section on pp.131-140, and it is why the FY2024-25 capital column does not tie
description:
pp.131-140 (REVENUE SOURCES BY FUNDS / OTHER FUNDS) print sections for 69 funds
and reproduce p0063.txt:16-21's Table 2 exactly, by fund group, in FY2025-26 and
FY2026-27. FY2024-25 has one real discrepancy and this is it.

MEASURED, summing the 13 printed `Total <fund>` lines in the Capital Funds run
(p132:46 through p134:35) against p63:

  capital funds   pp.132-134 sum   p63 Table 2    diff
  FY2023-24         19,743,053     19,743,054       -1   (fisc-2sd rounding)
  FY2024-25         30,713,648     34,839,275   -4,125,627
  FY2025-26         27,145,882     27,145,882      tie
  FY2026-27         26,888,254     26,888,254      tie

THE MONEY HAS A NAME AND A PAGE. p0194.txt:29 prints

  General Fund CIP Reserves   $34,954,363   $  -   $4,125,627   $39,079,990

and p0192.txt:14 carries it into the citywide capital line as
`Revenues 30,713,648 | Transfers In 4,125,627 | Total Sources 34,839,275`. Our
sum of the 13 fund totals is 30,713,648 -- p192's REVENUES figure to the cent.

SO THE OMISSION IS STRUCTURAL, NOT AN EXTRACTION DEFECT. p63's Table 2 is
captioned "Total Sources" and its own overview line (p0063.txt:5-7) defines that
as "revenues, transfers-in, and debt proceeds". Every OTHER fund group's sections
on pp.131-140 print their own Transfers In rows, which is why they tie: their
fund totals already include transfers. NO capital fund on pp.132-134 prints a
Transfers In row at all -- verified, zero occurrences in that run -- and the one
capital transfer the city budgets in FY2024-25 goes to a fund the schedule gives
no section to.

p0198.txt:14 and p0204.txt:14 print `-` in that column, which is exactly why
FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 tie.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN NOTED. fisc-u2v's decision rests on pp.127-140 being
a COMPLETE, EXACT, ALTERNATIVE DECOMPOSITION of the spine's revenue side, and it
is -- for the two budget columns, which is all the spine prints. This bead
records the one column where that completeness claim is FALSE, with the amount
and the page, so a future reader of a four-column corroboration test knows why it
is written over two columns and not four. A test asserting four-column equality
against p63 WILL fail; that is the document, not the read.

Found while settling fisc-wev, 2026-08-24, by summing pp.131-140 by fund group.
acceptance_criteria: the FY2024-25 capital discrepancy is explained by General Fund CIP Reserves' 4,125,627 with its page cited; any corroboration test against p0063 Table 2 is written over the columns that tie and says in words why the others do not; no stated_total_deltas entry absorbs it
notes:
2026-08-24 NO CHECK AND NO FIXTURE IS OWED FOR p63, and the reason is this
project's own rule rather than expedience.

A landing plan for fisc-5gk.1 proposed committing p0063 and p0186 as fixtures and
writing a corroboration test asserting pp.131-140 tie to Table 2 by fund group.
Dropped, because p63 Table 2 IS pp.66-67's TOTAL SOURCES restated by fund type:
enterprise FY2026 is 80,761,261 = the spine's revenue 67,514,261 plus its
transfers in 13,247,000. So a p63 test would be a second statement of the claim
revenue-detail-ties-to-spine already makes, and fisc-u2v's own reasoning about
the 21,045,597 overlap applies verbatim -- "no scope-to-scope check is owed,
transitivity through the spine gives it, and a second statement of the same claim
is a second place for it to drift".

The one thing p63 has that the spine does not is a PERMANENT FUNDS row, and the
lane does not need p63 for it: p134 is committed as a fixture and carries Doolan
Canyon Preserve Endow directly, which is what fisc-u8o's evidence should read.

So the measurement stays where it is -- on fisc-wev, on this bead, and on
fisc-94b -- as a finding about the document, and does not become a test. What
this bead still owes is the wording: any future corroboration against Table 2
must be written over the columns that tie and say in words why FY2024-25 does
not.

title: make pre-commit does not run the linter, so CI is the first place a violation shows
description:
THE GAP. Makefile's pre-commit target is `fmt vet test` (Makefile:79). `make lint` exists and is a separate target nothing depends on, and docs/agents + CLAUDE.md tell a contributor to symlink pre-commit into .git/hooks/pre-commit. So the hook that runs before every commit does not run golangci-lint, and CI is the first place a violation appears.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: lint was red on main across at least three commits -- 5bd6f15, ee05b55 and 65c16275 -- with four issues (three govet/shadow, one gocritic/offBy1), and nobody saw it until CI was looked at. Fixed in 03cde8e; the process gap is this bead.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST 'ADD lint TO pre-commit'. Two real costs, which is why this is a bead and not a one-line change:
  - golangci-lint is not required to build or test this project. Today a contributor with Go and nothing else can run make pre-commit; adding lint makes an external binary mandatory to commit. The lint target already warns rather than fails when the local version differs from .golangci-version, which is the same instinct.
  - It is slower than fmt+vet+test on a cold cache.

OPTIONS, none obviously right:
  (a) pre-commit gains lint, and the target degrades to a warning when golangci-lint is absent from PATH rather than failing the commit.
  (b) A separate `make pre-push` that runs lint, matching where the cost is worth paying.
  (c) Leave it, and make the CI lint job's failure louder -- it is already a required check, so the real defect may be that nobody reads a red run.

Whatever is chosen, docs/agents/workflow.md's cadence section has to say it, because the symlink instruction is what makes pre-commit the contract.

Found while fixing the CI lint failure, 2026-08-23.
close_reason: Option (a) landed in d73b284: pre-commit gains a lint-if-available target that warns and continues when golangci-lint is absent, while make lint itself keeps hard-failing for CI. Both paths exercised. Docs corrected in CLAUDE.md (which held the stale 'fmt, vet, test' gloss) and workflow.md's Commits section; the cadence section the bead named is about /code-review and mentions neither.

title: CheckRollup's failure message prints 'off by' with the sign inverted from its own comment
description:
internal/mapping/resolve.go:999-1004. The comment says:

    // STATED MINUS SUMMED, the same direction StatedTotalDelta is written
    // in, so a failure reads like every other totals failure here.

and the guard follows it: `if diff := stated[i] - sums[i]; diff != 0`. But `diff` is used ONLY for the zero test -- the message then prints `off by %s` with `sums[i]-stated[i]`, the opposite direction.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A COSMETIC SLIP. The comment's stated purpose is that the number in the failure can be pasted into a declaration. CheckTotals earns that (resolve.go:824-826 computes stated-minus-mapped and reports it in that direction); CheckRollup prints the negation of what it computed, so an author pasting it declares a delta of the wrong sign and gets a second failure reading 'declares a delta of -N but the difference is +N'.

It is latent today: every one of the twelve rollups on the coverage lanes' pages ties at zero, so the branch has never printed. It fires the first time a rollup does not tie, which is exactly when the operator is least able to second-guess the sign.

FIX: print `diff`. It is already in scope.

TEST: the failability test has to pin the SIGN, not just the failure -- assert the message contains the stated-minus-summed value for a rollup deliberately short by a known amount. A test that only asserts 'it failed' passes either way, which is why this survived fisc-3bl's review.

Found in peer review of the fisc-o15 / fisc-5gk.2 landing plan, 2026-08-23, and verified against the source.
notes:
2026-08-24 THE PREMISE IS WRONG, and correcting it makes the bead bigger rather
than smaller. Found while fixing it; verified against the source and by test.

THIS BEAD SAYS: "CheckTotals earns that (resolve.go:824-826 computes
stated-minus-mapped and reports it in that direction); CheckRollup prints the
negation of what it computed."

IT DOES NOT. compareTotals carries the IDENTICAL inversion --
internal/mapping/resolve.go:1220 computes `diff := stated[c] - sums[c]` under a
comment reading "STATED MINUS MAPPED, the same direction StatedTotalDelta.Cents
is written in, so a failure message can be pasted into a declaration", and
:1230 then prints `sums[c]-stated[c]`. Its own THIRD branch, three lines further
down at :1238, prints `diff` correctly, so one function reported one quantity in
two directions. CheckRollup did not deviate from CheckTotals; it copied it.
(The cited :824-826 is the tail of CheckSpanningTotals, not compareTotals.)

AND THE RATIONALE APPLIES ONLY TO THE SITE THIS BEAD EXONERATES. Rollup
(internal/mapping/rule.go:142-177) has no stated_total_deltas field -- a rollup
delta cannot be declared anywhere -- so the "author pastes it in and declares
the wrong sign" hazard is unreachable through CheckRollup and fully reachable
through compareTotals.

MEASURED, on the real fixture. p127 column 1 maps 58,179,467 against a printed
58,179,468, and the undeclared failure read "off by -$1.00" while the declaration
that ties is delta_cents: 100. An author pasting the message got back
"declared delta -$1.00 but the difference is $1.00" -- the second branch
contradicting the first. The number in the failure was the one number that could
not be pasted in.

FIXED AT BOTH SITES, with sign-pinning tests at both, each proven red against the
prior code before landing: TestTheUndeclaredFailureStatesTheDeltaToPasteIn
(statedtotaldelta_test.go) and the extended
TestARollupFailsWhenARuleIsMissingFromCovers (rollup_test.go). The rollup test
already existed and named both totals while shrugging at the number between
them, which is how this survived fisc-3bl's review -- the bead predicted that
shape of test and it was already in the tree.
close_reason: Landed in a3adb0e. fisc-7fe fixed element-wise on the EFFECTIVE basis (the Column.Basis override half was found in review of the fix); fisc-7a6 fixed at both sites, its premise corrected on the bead first; fisc-t9h guarded before both rules[0] indexes. Each test proven red against the prior code. Kind/scope left uncompared and filed separately.

title: Rollup.Covers and Row.Department are two declarations nothing couples
description:
File.Rollups names the rules a printed <DEPARTMENT> TOTAL covers; Row.Department names the division each row belongs to. NOTHING RELATES THE TWO.

A rollup may cover div-city-clerk while every row of that rule carries department: city-manager, and no check notices: CheckRollup sums the covered rules' stated totals and ties, factDepartmentsResolve only asks whether each department slug resolves, and the object-category sums are unchanged by moving a division between departments.

That is the same hole fisc-b9j closed one axis over -- it proved a division filed under the wrong department is caught by nothing else, and the answer was the department rollup. This is the rollup's own version of it: the rollup asserts the ARITHMETIC of the department grouping while the department grouping ITSELF is declared twice, independently, in two places that need not agree.

internal/mapping/departmentaxis_test.go:214-218 records a neighbouring residual risk but not this one.

SHAPE TO CONSIDER: an optional Rollup.Department, plus a parse-time check that every row of every covered rule carries it. Optional because p130's Total General Fund and p140's Total Sources are rollups with no department axis at all.

Found in peer review of the fisc-o15 / fisc-5gk.2 landing plan, 2026-08-23.

title: Nothing asserts a published id recomputes from its published fields
description:
Nothing asserts that a published fact's id is the id its own published fields
produce. That is the invariant the whole fisc-28h decision rests on, and it is
checked today only for one synthetic row in internal/fact's tests.

THE PROPERTY: for every line of facts/facts.jsonl,

  id == MakeID(doc_id, rule_id, row_path, row_label, column_path,
               fiscal_year, basis)

VERIFIED TRUE over all 240 committed facts during the fisc-28h review, with 0
mismatches. So the check goes green the day it lands and is a ratchet rather
than a repair.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW SPECIFICALLY. fisc-28h chose to hash row_label's published
form (PrintedLabel()) over the resolver's internal Identity(), and the DECIDING
argument was exactly this recomputability: a reader holding one line of the
audit trail must be able to re-derive its id from that line. Identity() is not
a published field and cannot be recovered from row_label -- "A B" could be one
anchor or two.

An argument that load-bearing should be enforced, not just recorded. Nothing
stops a future change re-pointing MakeID at a field the record does not carry,
and the symptom would be silent: ids that no longer address anything, on a file
whose entire purpose is to be addressable.

NOTE WHAT IT IS NOT. fact-ids-unique already asserts no two facts share an id.
This is the other half -- that an id is the RIGHT one for its record. Uniqueness
would survive re-pointing MakeID at any injective function of anything.

SIZE: ~15 lines in internal/check/facts.go, beside fact-ids-unique. Both sides
are already in the fact store, so no mapping or registry change.
acceptance_criteria: a check re-derives every fact's id from its own published fields and compares; it reports Subjects > 0 over the committed store and passes; it is proven failable by re-pointing MakeID at a non-published field
close_reason: fact-ids-recompute lands in internal/check/facts.go, registered beside fact-ids-unique. 436 subjects, green on the committed corpus. Failability proven by mutating row_label, the mutation facts-sorted / fact-ids-unique / fact-token-reparses all miss; the test asserts those three stay green too.

title: fact-kind-matches-category: an empty kind or category is named by no check, and the pass summary is unpinned
description:
Three small gaps found by adversarial review of fisc-f0k, kept out of that
commit because none of them blocks it and bundling would have hidden them.

(1) A FACT WITH AN EMPTY KIND OR CATEGORY IS NAMED BY NO CHECK.
factKindMatchesCategory skips on f.Kind == "" or f.Category == "", and
factVocabulary explicitly declines both. buildProjections does refuse -- "sankey:
fact ... has no category" -- so it fails loudly, but as a LOAD ERROR rather than
a named finding, and internal/check/subject.go distinguishes those on purpose.
Meanwhile the subject count silently drops (240 -> 239) while the PASS line still
reads "each kind one its category declares". A check that quietly shrinks its own
denominator is the shape fisc-u2v's coverage.go incident warns about.

(2) THE PASS SUMMARY IS NOT PINNED. Nothing asserts factKindMatchesCategory's
pass Summary, so the kind/category pair count could be replaced by 0 and no test
would fail. Compare TestUnsortedFactStoreFails, which pins a summary byte for
byte. The vacuous `nothing:` string is never exercised either -- the check is
absent from TestVacuousChecksSayWhatIsAbsent's map, which pins the other five.
And the three `continue` branches have no test asserting the check stays silent
while the subject count drops, which is exactly the behaviour (1) is about.

(3) A COMMENT THAT DOES NOT MATCH ITS CODE. factKindMatchesCategory's doc says
"one typo must not redden two checks with two different fixes", but the exclusion
tests `!ok` (category undefined) rather than `!Assignable`. So
`category: taxes` + `kind: expenditure` reddens BOTH fact-vocabulary and
fact-kind-matches-category for one fix -- the case the comment says it avoids.
Either the comment or the condition is wrong.

None of these is a correctness bug in the published figures. (1) is the one worth
doing first: it is a real reporting hole and it generalises beyond this check.
acceptance_criteria: a fact with an empty kind or category produces a named finding rather than only a load error; the pass summary and the vacuous string are pinned by tests; the doc comment and the exclusion condition agree

title: Nothing asserts a transfer's DIRECTION agrees with its transfers/in or transfers/out category
description:
fisc-f0k landed fact-kind-matches-category, which asserts a fact's kind is among
its category's declared `kinds:`. It closes the fisc-u2v route-3 case (a Transfers
In row mapped `kind: revenue` under `category: transfers/in`) and it CANNOT close
the direction case, for a reason recorded in data/taxonomy.yaml itself.

All four transfer categories declare `kinds: [transfer]` -- not transfer_in /
transfer_out. The `transfers` rollup's rationale says why: "Direction has to live
in the category because a transfer's `kind` is only 'transfer'; a rule that wrote
`category: transfers` would produce a figure whose sign cannot be recovered."

So the taxonomy carries direction on the CATEGORY axis and the kind is only the
family. fact-kind-matches-category therefore accepts either direction against a
declared `transfer` (internal/check/vocabulary.go, declaresKind and
taxonomyTransferKind), and

    category: transfers/in  +  kind: transfer_out

resolves clean today, exactly as `transfers/in + revenue` did before fisc-f0k.

WHY IT IS NOT THE SAME BUG AND NEEDS ITS OWN CHECK

The two errors have different arithmetic. Counting a transfer as revenue moves
money between the two totals p66 adds SEPARATELY (TOTAL REVENUES vs TRANSFER IN),
which is what inflated enterprise revenue to 80,761,261 against 67,514,261.
Getting the direction wrong moves money between TRANSFER IN and TRANSFER OUT,
which p66 also prints separately (480,400 in / 10,037,797 out for the General
Fund FY2025-26) and which internal/project draws as opposite-facing links.

The check is a different shape too: it is not "kind in kinds" but a claimed
correspondence between the transfers/* slug and the kind's direction, which is
knowledge this repo would be ASSERTING rather than reading out of a file. That
makes it a decision about where the correspondence is recorded -- a field on the
taxonomy entry, or a table in Go with its own evidence -- not a third clause.

Note the interaction with fisc-iki, which wants `kinds:` members validated
against the five mapping.Kind values at load time. `transfer` is NOT one of the
five, so fisc-iki as written would reject data/taxonomy.yaml today. Whoever takes
either bead has to settle whether the file's vocabulary is the five kinds or the
four families; declaresKind accepts both spellings so that this bead can be
decided without a flag day. internal/check's own fixture taxonomy already writes
`kinds: [transfer_in]`, so both spellings are live and both are tested.

Found while implementing fisc-f0k, 2026-08-22.
acceptance_criteria: a fact with kind transfer_out under category transfers/in is a finding naming the row; proven failable by input mutation; the residual-hole paragraph in factKindMatchesCategory's doc comment is updated to point at the check that closed it
close_reason:
Closed by correcting data/taxonomy.yaml rather than by a second check.

The premise this bead was filed on was itself the defect. All four transfer
categories declared `kinds: [transfer]`, and the `transfers` rationale
asserted 'a transfer's `kind` is only "transfer"'. That clause was FALSE WHEN
WRITTEN, not stale: mapping.Kind has five values and `transfer` is not one of
them, and transfer_in/transfer_out landed in 2e514fb (2026-08-15 21:40),
which predates 0c43404 (2026-08-16 03:21), the only commit that has ever
touched data/taxonomy.yaml. internal/check's fixture taxonomy already wrote
`kinds: [transfer_in]`; production was the outlier, not the fixture.

So fact-kind-matches-category had been widened (taxonomyTransferKind,
declaresKind's transfer arm) to accommodate a data defect, and the direction
hole was a consequence of the widening. Corrected the file:
transfers/in -> [transfer_in]; transfers/out and transfers/out-to-cip ->
[transfer_out]; the transfers rollup -> [transfer_in, transfer_out]. Deleted
the widening; declaresKind is now slices.Contains. Direction falls out of the
same literal comparison, so this needed no second check and no new knowledge
asserted in Go.

Proven failable by input mutation over the committed store: setting
fisc-f-ced7f6603e29 to kind transfer_out while leaving category transfers/in
now reports

  fisc-f-ced7f6603e29: livermore-budget-fy2026-2027 p66 "TRANSFER IN:": kind
  "transfer_out" is not one data/taxonomy.yaml declares for category
  "transfers/in", which declares transfer_in

The identical mutation was reproduced against the pre-correction tree in a
throwaway copy and PASSED there (20 passed / 0 failed), which is the bead.

facts/facts.jsonl is byte-identical; verify is 20 passed / 0 failed /
5 vacuous / 1 skipped, with fact-kind-matches-category PASS over all 240
facts and 20 kind/category pairs.

title: The $38,086,737 transfer residual is a printed column, not an unexplained gap: cite p73
description:
The site ships a caveat describing the $38,086,737 FY2025-26 transfer residual as
the city's own unexplained gap. IT HAS A PRINTED HOME and should be cited rather
than apologised for.

MEASURED and confirmed by hand off the page:

  p0073.txt:9   column header  "Transfers Out to CIP"
  p0073.txt:58  $301,180,035 | $21,525,997 | $38,086,737 | $4,699,425 | ...

So the residual is not a discrepancy at all -- it is a NAMED COLUMN of the
city's own sources-and-uses schedule. p76's grand total is Transfers Out
EXCLUDING transfers to CIP; the spine's TRANSFER OUT row includes them; the
difference is exactly the column the city prints between them.

FY2026-27 likewise: p0075.txt:58 prints 21,624,633 and 50,762,251, and 50,762,251
is the FY2027 residual fisc-kwq already flagged as larger than FY2026's.

data/taxonomy.yaml already carries a `transfers/out-to-cip` slug, so the
vocabulary for saying this exists.

WHAT THIS REPLACES. fisc-5gk.3's close reason established that the residual is
the document's own and decomposes as Capital 28,584,740 + Enterprise 9,353,147 +
SpecRev 108,850 + ISF 40,000. That decomposition was DERIVED. This is the same
quantity PUBLISHED, under a heading, which is a materially stronger claim and
the kind this project is supposed to prefer.

THE CAVEAT THAT MUST SURVIVE, and it is why this is not a one-line edit: the
per-fund-group SPLIT is not recoverable for FY2026-27. p76 itemises 1,018,035 of
special-revenue-sourced transfers against p67's SR TRANSFER OUT of 900,550,
which would require a to-CIP of -117,485. The AGGREGATE ties exactly
(1,018,035 + 35,930,251 = 36,948,286 = capital 36,047,736 + SR 900,550), so the
citywide claim holds in both years and only the capital-vs-SR split is an
FY2026-only inference. fisc-5gk.3's per-group residual table must be qualified
as such rather than carried forward.

DO NOT restate the published caveat until the FY2027 split is understood or the
caveat is written to claim only the aggregate.

Found in the fisc-aes / fisc-brx scope decision pass, 2026-08-22.
acceptance_criteria: the published caveat cites p73's 'Transfers Out to CIP' column instead of describing the residual as unexplained; the claim it makes is the AGGREGATE, because the FY2026-27 per-fund-group split is not recoverable; fisc-5gk.3's per-group table is qualified as FY2026-only
notes:
2026-08-24 THE FALSE-TABLE HALF IS DONE (19bb265); THE SITE CAVEAT HALF IS NOT.

This bead said the residual "has a printed home and should be cited rather than
apologised for", and warned "DO NOT restate the published caveat until the
FY2027 split is understood or the caveat is written to claim only the aggregate".

WHAT LANDED. docs/sankey-contract.md now cites p0073.txt:58 / p0075.txt:58,
carries the corrected decomposition, and says which of its rows are printed and
which are derived. The mapping note claiming the city "itemises nowhere" is
corrected. And the arithmetic exists:
TestP76SourcesDecomposeTheResidualByFundType asserts
spine_TRANSFER_OUT == p76_paid + to_CIP per group in both years, with the to-CIP
terms summing to the printed 38,086,737 and 50,762,251.

THE FY2027 SPLIT IS NOW UNDERSTOOD, and this bead's own statement of it was
wrong in the same way fisc-aes's was. It says the split "would require a to-CIP
of -117,485" and is "not recoverable". Both years split cleanly; 1,018,035 is
the NON-MAJOR total, not the special-revenue part. See the correction on
fisc-aes. So the caveat may claim MORE than this bead allowed -- but the reason
to state the aggregate is still good and is now the right one:
published-is-not-derived, because pp.72-75 print non-major to-CIP as one
aggregate.

WHAT REMAINS.
- internal/project/sankey.go transferCaveat still says the gap "is the city's
  rather than this project's" without naming the column, and still opens with
  "the p76 transfer schedule is not yet mapped (fisc-5gk.3)" -- which is the
  wrong bead for what it describes even today (fisc-9gh) and goes false when
  p76 lands.
- internal/export/page.go's shipped headline note says "The schedule that would
  pair them is not mapped yet, so no link carries a transfer id." The causal
  claim is wrong now and the first clause goes false with fisc-5gk.3.1.
- The to-CIP constants themselves. They are not yet declared anywhere the check
  can read; fisc-j2l owns the table. Note they are NOT at p0073.txt:58 per
  group: general is :13, internal-service :53, non-major :56, and ENTERPRISE IS
  NOT PRINTED AT ALL -- it is :24 + :30 + :37 + :44, and those pages carry no
  row labels, which are on the facing pages p0072/p0074.
- pp.73 and 75 are not fixtures (testdata/pages/ holds 66, 67, 76, 127-140,
  167-170), so anything reading them needs a fixture commit first.

title: [bug] pp.68-75 publish a third citywide revenue total, $8,226,620 above the spine
description:
Budget Book pp.68-75 print a per-fund SOURCES AND USES schedule that is a THIRD
citywide total, and it does not agree with the spine.

MEASURED off data/extracted:

  p0074.txt:52  Total All Funds:  $318,509,884  $310,669,663  $72,386,884  $701,566,431

The four columns are beginning balance, revenues, transfers in, total sources --
confirmed by arithmetic: 318,509,884 + 310,669,663 + 72,386,884 = 701,566,431
exactly.

The spine's FY2026-27 revenue, summing the six TOTAL REVENUES: cells on
pp.66-67, is 302,443,043 (164,358,147 + 70,308,250 + 26,888,254 + 0 +
20,892,522 + 19,995,870).

  310,669,663 - 302,443,043 = 8,226,620

TWO PUBLISHED CITYWIDE REVENUE TOTALS, $8,226,620 APART, and nothing in the
repo records it.

WHAT IS ALREADY EXPLAINED ON THESE PAGES, so the delta is not just "a different
basis": the transfers column reconciles exactly. p74's Transfers In 72,386,884 =
p76's FY2026-27 grand total 21,624,633 + p0075.txt:58's Transfers Out to CIP
50,762,251. So pp.73-75 and p76 are the same money and agree; it is the REVENUE
column that does not.

WHY THIS NEEDS AN ID RATHER THAN A NOTE. pp.68-75 are unmapped AND unbeaded --
no bead in the tracker proposes mapping them. They are per-fund and they carry
revenue, so they are precisely what someone reaches for after fisc-5gk.1 lands,
on the reasoning "it's by fund, it goes in revenue-by-fund". That would be
caught -- fisc-u2v's tie requires the scope's per-cell sums to EQUAL the spine's,
so an $8.2M over-inclusion fails immediately -- but it would be caught as a
mysterious red check rather than as a known property of the document.

Related and probably the same investigation: p140's Total Sources is short of
its own pages by ~$57M (separate bead), and the two may share a cause, since
both are SOURCES totals rather than REVENUES totals and the
headline-ties-to-revenues-not-sources memory records that the city means
different things by the two words.

DO NOT map pp.68-75 into any existing scope until this is explained.

Found while reviewing the fisc-gkv decision pass, 2026-08-22, and confirmed by
hand off the pages.
acceptance_criteria: the $8,226,620 gap between p074's Total All Funds revenue and the pp.66-67 spine is explained from published figures, or recorded as unexplained with the measurement; the bead states whether pp.68-75 may ever share a scope with the spine or the detail

title: [bug] wrapped_labels is accepted but inert on a labels_from part, with no stale-declaration error
description:
wrapped_labels is read and staleness-checked only in labelledValues. On a part
that takes its row identity positionally via labels_from, the declaration is
ACCEPTED and DOES NOTHING, and no stale-declaration error fires.

That contradicts the field's own contract. This repo's declarations are claims
that fail when they stop being true -- StatedTotalDelta fails when a declared
delta now ties exactly, OmittedRows fails the count assertion, and fisc-u2v's
unprojectedScopes entry is being built to fail when the scope becomes projected.
A declaration that is inert on half the part types is the one shape that cannot
fail, so it records an author's belief that nothing ever checks.

Budget Book p67 is a labels_from part today, so this is reachable in the shipped
rule file, not only in principle.

WANTED: either wrapped_labels is rejected at parse time on a labels_from part
(with a message saying why it cannot apply), or it is honoured there. Rejecting
is probably right -- a wrapped label is a property of the part that CARRIES the
label, and a labels_from part by definition carries none -- but say so rather
than leaving it silently accepted.

Found by /code-review over the 8 commits ahead of origin/main, 2026-08-22.
acceptance_criteria: wrapped_labels on a labels_from part is either refused at parse time with a reason or honoured; a test covers the chosen behaviour; the declaration cannot be silently inert
notes:
2026-08-22 CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY, and on the PRODUCTION mapping rather than a
fixture. From /code-review over the wave-1 diff.

Adding `wrapped_labels: ["This Fragment Is Not On The Page"]` to the p67 part of
mappings/livermore-budget-fy2026-2027.yaml BUILDS CLEANLY with byte-identical
facts. The same declaration on the p66 part errors. p67 takes its row identity
positionally via labels_from, so it routes to positionalValues, which never
reads or validates the field, and the parser does not refuse the combination.

FIVE PRODUCTION PARTS USE labels_from, so the stale-declaration guard is off for
all of them -- not a hypothetical reachable only by a future page.

This is the fail-open the bead predicted, now measured. The fix direction is
unchanged: refuse it at parse time on a labels_from part, since a wrapped label
is a property of the part that CARRIES the label and a labels_from part carries
none.
close_reason: Landed in 664d638 as one fix, per fisc-2jk's own framing. ekj refused at parse time on a labels_from part, with the bead's recorded p67 measurement re-run against the fix; 2jk's i==0 gap now consults WrappedLabels and marks it used, keeping the column-header permissiveness for a stated reason. Both proven red first.

title: Nothing asserts a fact's kind is among its category's declared kinds
description:
data/taxonomy.yaml declares `kinds:` on every category -- the set of
mapping.Kind values a fact in that category may carry. Nothing checks it.

internal/check/vocabulary.go's factVocabulary (Run, ~:44-72) checks exactly two
things per fact: that Category is Assignable, and that FundGroup is a type some
fund in data/funds.yaml is recorded under. It never consults the category's
`kinds:` list. So:

  category: transfers/in  +  kind: revenue

resolves clean today. Both halves are individually valid and the pair is not.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW rather than in the abstract

The fisc-u2v design pass found eleven funds on pp.131-140 whose printed
`Total <fund>` covers revenue rows AND a Transfers In row (Stormwater,
Wastewater, Wastewater Replacement, Water, Water Replacement, 2022 COPS,
Horizons, Downtown LMD, Workers Comp Insurance, Facilities Rehab Pgm, +1).
fisc-uli's Row.Kind is what lets a rule split them. The failure mode if a rule
author gets a Row.Kind wrong -- or omits it and lets Rule.Kind apply -- is a
Transfers In row classified `kind: revenue` under `category: transfers/in`.

That inflates enterprise revenue to 80,761,261 against the spine's 67,514,261,
so fisc-u2v's revenue-detail-ties-to-spine WOULD catch it. This bead is the
cheaper, more local guard: it fails at the fact, naming the row, instead of at a
fund-group aggregate.

SHAPE

registry.Category already carries Kinds (internal/registry/registry.go). The
check is a third clause inside factVocabulary, or its own Check if the message
deserves its own id. Note fisc-iki is adjacent but different: that bead is about
`kinds:` MEMBERS not being validated against the five mapping.Kind values at
LOAD time. This one is about facts not being validated against the list at
VERIFY time. Both are real; neither subsumes the other.

Found in the fisc-u2v design pass, 2026-08-21.
acceptance_criteria: a fact whose kind is not in its category's declared kinds is a finding naming the row; the check reports Subjects > 0 against the committed store; proven failable by input mutation
close_reason: Landed in 5bd6f15, f0e120b and 6216eda respectively. See each commit message for what was proven and what was not.

title: The chart's crossing claims are only checkable out of tree: no harness runs site/app.js's layout
description:
site/app.js asserts 394 crossings before and 195 after, and restackLinks() asserts 14 stale-stacked pairs on FY2026 and 108 under the order it replaced. Nothing in the tree can check any of that: the numbers come from laying the graph out under node with the vendored d3-sankey, and the repo has no JS runner.

A harness exists and works: load dist/vendor/d3*.min.js into a vm context, lift FUND_ORDER, nodeRank and restackLinks verbatim out of site/app.js, lay the graph out, count sign flips between each band's link endpoints. Node and nothing else -- no npm, no bundler -- so it stays off the deploy path the way tools/extract.py stays off the build path. It also checks the geometry restackLinks touches: node fill error and extent overflow both came out at 0.000000px. A second harness drives the node activation handlers through the ten input sequences mouse, keyboard and assistive tech produce.

Same question as before: whether a second scripting runtime in the repo is worth it, or whether the claims should be trimmed to what can be checked without one. Note the comment also cites the exact optimum (177 crossings, $491M ink) as the ceiling the barycentre heuristic gives up 18 crossings against; that came from a subset-DP search that no longer lives in the tree either.

title: Pages deploy races ci.yml: a red CI can arrive after the site is live
description:
pages.yml and ci.yml both trigger on push to main, so they run in PARALLEL. The
deploy usually wins. A push that breaks site/app.js, fails a Go test, or fails
lint still publishes, and the red CI shows up afterwards.

Partially mitigated already, deliberately. The build job re-runs the two checks
that bear on whether the PUBLISHED FIGURES are trustworthy:
  - fisc verify (the corpus checks)
  - the facts.jsonl rebuild-and-cmp (the figures are the ones the rules produce)
Those are duplicated from ci.yml rather than trusted to the race, because
publishing unreproducible figures is the failure this project exists to
prevent. Everything else -- lint, vet, tidy, go test -- is NOT duplicated, and
that is the remaining hole.

WANTED, one of:

(a) Gate on ci.yml with a workflow_run trigger on workflow "CI", type
    "completed", branch main, plus a job-level condition that the triggering
    run's conclusion was success.

    NOTE THE FOOTGUN: a workflow_run job checks out the DEFAULT BRANCH, not the
    commit that triggered it, so the checkout must pin ref to the event's
    head_sha or the deploy publishes the wrong tree. workflow_dispatch needs a
    separate path, since that field is absent there.

(b) Fold the deploy into ci.yml as a job that needs lint, test, vet, facts and
    verify. Simpler and race-free, but ci.yml is read-only by design and its
    header says so, so the deploy's write scopes would have to be scoped to
    that one job.

(b) is probably right and is a smaller change than it looks. Deferred rather
than done because the first deploy has not run yet, and gating an untested
workflow on another workflow makes the first failure harder to read, not
easier.

Raised in /code-review of the WIP-banner + Pages-deploy change, 2026-08-18.
close_reason:
Done, and by option (b) -- the deploy moved into ci.yml as `pages-build` and
`pages-deploy` at the foot of the file, and pages.yml is deleted.

The race is gone by construction rather than by mitigation. Two workflows both
triggered by `push: main` are two concurrent runs with no ordering; the deploy
had fewer jobs, so it would routinely publish before the tests finished. As
jobs in the same workflow they just `needs:` the gates.

That also DELETED the duplication this bead recorded as a partial mitigation.
pages.yml re-ran `fisc verify` and the facts rebuild-and-cmp because a separate
workflow could not depend on ci.yml's versions. `needs: [lint, format, build,
test, vet, tidy, facts, verify]` gives the real thing, so both duplicated steps
are gone -- the export job now only builds and packages.

Details worth keeping:

- `if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` on
  pages-build. ci.yml also runs on pull_request, and without this a fork PR
  would reach the write scopes. pages-deploy needs pages-build, and a skipped
  dependency skips the dependent, so one guard covers both.

- govulncheck is deliberately NOT in the needs list. Its verdict depends on a
  database fetched at run time rather than on the commit, so the same tree can
  be green today and red tomorrow. The published artefact is static HTML, CSS
  and vendored d3 -- no Go ships -- so nothing it reports can reach a visitor,
  and gating publication on it would make republishing fail for reasons
  unrelated to the site.

- pages-deploy carries its own `concurrency: {group: pages, cancel-in-progress:
  false}`. The workflow-wide group is per-ref and does not cancel on main,
  which is right for CI but would let two quick pushes race for a single Pages
  deployment.

- Job-level permissions REPLACE the workflow block rather than extend it, so
  pages-deploy grants exactly pages:write and id-token:write and no contents:
  deploy-pages reads the uploaded artefact, not the repository. pages-build
  keeps the inherited contents:read floor.

ci.yml's header said "No job here writes to the repository or publishes
anything; the Pages deploy is a separate workflow with its own narrower grant."
That is now false in its first half and stale in its second, and was rewritten.

title: Monthly scheduled fisc verify --full workflow
description:
The second artifact fisc-gxa.5 owned, split out so closing the Pages deploy does not strand it.

fisc verify --full is the only thing in the project that reads data/pdf/: it recomputes each PDF's sha256 and compares it against BOTH data/sources.yaml and the extraction manifest. Nothing runs it today -- ci.yml reports that check as SKIPPED on every run, and pages.yml does the same, both deliberately.

Two things the job must get right, from fisc-gxa.5's notes:

- It needs lfs: true AND must not inherit GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE. Both ci.yml and pages.yml set that env workflow-wide, so this belongs in a NEW workflow file rather than as a job in either. A pointer-only checkout makes the check report ERROR ('an unsmudged Git LFS pointer ... run git lfs pull') rather than a false failure -- correct, but it means the job would never actually hash anything.

- Monthly, not per-push: ~67 MB per run against GitHub's 1 GB/month free LFS bandwidth. ci.yml's header note has the arithmetic.

Blocked in practice on the same thing pages.yml is: nothing has been pushed to the remote yet, so no workflow has ever executed.
notes:
2026-08-19 THE 'NOTHING HAS BEEN PUSHED' CLAUSE IS DEAD: origin/main == HEAD (256167b) and ci.yml has run. Also pages.yml no longer exists -- 77ceee0 folded the deploy into ci.yml as the pages-build/pages-deploy jobs -- so the reason for a NEW workflow file is now ci.yml alone: it sets GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE workflow-wide (ci.yml:59) and every checkout sets lfs: false with the ~67 MB note. The conclusion is unchanged (new file, lfs: true, monthly, no inherited smudge-skip); only its premise needed correcting. This bead is now genuinely actionable rather than blocked in practice.
2026-08-22: .github/workflows/verify-full.yml added (uncommitted, left in the tree). New file rather than a ci.yml job, because ci.yml sets GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE workflow-wide and workflow-level env cannot be unset by a job -- so this file deliberately has NO env block at all, and its single checkout is the only one in the repo with lfs: true. Triggers: cron '17 6 1 * *' (~67 MB/month against the 1 GB free tier, ci.yml's arithmetic reproduced in the header) plus workflow_dispatch. permissions: contents: read. Both action SHAs (checkout v7.0.1 3d3c42e5..., setup-go v7.0.0 b7ad1dad...) are already pinned in ci.yml; no new third-party action introduced. Steps: make build, a guard that fails if 'git lfs ls-files' shows pointers rather than smudged objects, then ./bin/fisc verify --full (not --strict, same reason as ci.yml's verify job).

Verified locally: parses clean under the repo's own go.yaml.in/yaml/v3 (PyYAML is absent here, which is python-has-no-yaml-by-design working as intended); the guard's grep fires on a synthetic pointer line and not on this tree; and ./bin/fisc verify --full exits 0 here with source-pdfs-match-both-records PASS over 6 records, because this checkout has all 3 LFS objects smudged. NOT verified: nothing has actually executed on GitHub -- the schedule, the dispatch button, whether actions/checkout's lfs: true smudges as expected on a runner, and the real bandwidth spend are all unproven until the file lands on main and a run happens.
close_reason: Landed in 5bd6f15, f0e120b and 6216eda respectively. See each commit message for what was proven and what was not.

title: data/funds.yaml needs an alias channel: schedules name funds in prose, and the short forms are ambiguous
description:
registry.Category carries Aliases []Alias (internal/registry/registry.go:121);
registry.Fund carries only number and name (:161-162). Every schedule that
names a fund in prose rather than by number therefore has no way to resolve it.

p76 is the first page to need it and it needs it fail-closed, because the
abbreviations are AMBIGUOUS, not merely short. data/funds.yaml holds an
operating fund and a CIP twin under near-identical names, and p76 prints the
short form of both parents:

  p76 label            candidates in data/funds.yaml
  Low Income Hsng      "Low Income Housing Fund" | "CIP Low Income Housing"
  Traffic Imp Fee      "Traffic Impact Fee (TIF)" | "CIP Traffic Impact Fee"
  Host Comm Impact     "Host Community Impact Fee" | "CIP Host Community Impact Fee"
  Measure D            "County Measure D" | "CIP County Measure D"
  State Gas Tax        "State - Gas Tax" | "CIP State Gas Tax"

A prefix or fuzzy match picks one of each pair silently, which is the plausible-
wrong-value class this project exists to prevent. Wanted: an explicit alias per
fund, PUBLISHED (the string the city prints) with the page it was read from, and
an unresolved or ambiguous label is an error rather than a best guess.

Note the source typo already recorded in the memory fund-names-come-from-p256:
p253 and p255 both print fund 291 as "Community Beneift Fund". Aliases are where
that gets stated rather than silently corrected.
acceptance_criteria: a fund can declare published aliases with their source page; an ambiguous or unresolved fund label is an error, never a best guess; p76's 16 source labels and 12 destination labels all resolve or fail by name
notes:
Implemented: registry.Fund gains Aliases []Alias (term + pages + optional note), Registry.FundByLabel(label) (Fund, error) resolves a printed label by EXACT match on a name or an alias, and *UnknownFundError names the label. Ambiguity is rejected at LOAD (a label two funds claim, or an alias equal to any fund name) rather than at lookup, so a loaded registry is one whose labels are already a function.

The five p76 CIP-twin pairs are settled by arithmetic, recorded in the funds.yaml header: the Uses of Funds pages (pp.187, 193, 199, 205) print Transfers Out per fund group and exclude transfers to CIP. CIP funds transfer out nothing in any of the four years; the capital funds Transfers Out (181,971 / 210,500 / 211,150 / 217,485) is exactly p76 Traffic Imp Fee + State Gas Tax + Measure D each year; the special revenue funds Transfers Out (1,083,617 / 1,259,206 / 817,050 / 800,550) is exactly Low Income Hsng + Home Grant + State Grant + Downtown Revital + CASP Fee + Downtown LMD + Other LMDs + Open Space + Host Comm Impact each year. So 200/510/282/550/560, not 812/823/820/828/834, and Open Space is 300, not the permanent fund 471.

20 aliases added. p76: all 16 source labels and all 12 destination labels resolve; the 13th destination string, "LAVWMA / Wastewater" (wrapped, names a JPA), fails by name and is asserted to. CASP Fee -> 286 is the one binding whose last step is inference (glossary p262) and its note says so.

fisc-u2v six confirmed off the pages, plus 291s "Community Beneift Fund" recorded as the appendix alias (pp.253, 255) rather than corrected. Uncommitted: the agent was told not to commit.
close_reason: Landed in 9725429. fisc-nne's premise was wrong: Police Evidence IS in funds.yaml, as fund 211 Asset Seizure - County under a different printed name, proven by slot, by figure agreement across pp.186/192/198/204 and by the group rollup. Recorded as an alias, not a 113th fund.

title: Publish p76 transfers as paired facts (blocked on the scope and pairing decisions)
description:
The publishing half of the p76 lane, split out of fisc-5gk.3 once that bead
turned out to be a reconciliation rather than a transcription.

Publishing p76's 22 rows as facts is NOT the small step it looks like, because
the reconciliation proves those rows are the SAME MONEY as the spine: every
destination fund group's section total equals p66/p67's TRANSFER IN cell
exactly, and General Fund's out-flows equal TRANSFER OUT exactly. So a rule
written at scope: all-funds-gross DOUBLES the city's transfers and every check
stays green -- fisc-u2v's mechanism verbatim, one lane over. See the memory
detail-pages-double-the-spine.

WHAT HAS TO BE DECIDED
- The scope axis, the same question as fisc-u2v but for transfers rather than
  revenue detail, and it must reconcile AGAINST the spine rather than sum with it.
- How one row carries TWO endpoints. fact.Fact has a single `fund` field, so a
  (from-fund, to-fund) pair does not fit. The natural shape is two facts per
  printed row -- a transfer_out keyed to the source fund and a transfer_in keyed
  to the destination -- sharing a pairing id and citing the same token/offset.
  That is fisc-4rh's decision, not this bead's to make alone.
- Fund identity: p76 prints abbreviations ("Low Income Hsng", "Traffic Imp Fee",
  "Host Comm Impact") and several are ambiguous between an operating fund and
  its CIP twin. Needs the alias channel.
- fisc-0cs: the Enterprise section carries a wrapped label ("Connection",
  p0076.txt:351) mid-block. The reconciliation works around it by splitting the
  part; a published rule should not have to.

WHAT IT BUYS. Paired legs for $21,525,997 of transfers, which un-vacuums
fisc-1wr.1's "every transfer_id has two equal legs" check -- recorded as vacuous
in docs/sankey-contract.md today. It does NOT close the $38,086,737 residual;
that is the document's, and fisc-5gk.3 proves it.
acceptance_criteria: p76 transfer facts publish without double-counting the spine's TRANSFER IN/OUT rows; the rule carries scope: transfers-by-fund and every column declares a fund_group (fisc-aes); unprojectedScopes gains its transfers-by-fund entry in this same commit; transfers-detail-ties-to-spine lands as a tier-1 union-of-keys check with zero IN-side exceptions; a test asserts the GF transfer-in leg publishes 480,400 and NOT 960,800; BOTH budget years land together, because revenue-detail-ties-to-spine's per-slice hand-off turns arm 3 and goes RED on a one-year hand-off
notes:
2026-08-24 THE transfer_id CLAUSE IS GONE FROM THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, moved to
fisc-9gh with the evidence: internal/project's cellKey is
(kind, category, fundGroup) and netCells never reads f.Fund, so publishing these
facts nets 22 legs into 9 cells and no link could carry a pairing. It was
unachievable by this bead and would have been discovered when --strict stayed
red.

Added instead: BOTH BUDGET YEARS MUST LAND TOGETHER. revenue-detail-ties-to-spine
hands off (transfer_in, transfers/in, general) to this scope PER SLICE
(internal/check/revenuedetail.go, tested at checks_test.go "partial hand-off").
Cover FY2026 only and arm 3 fires -- "the hand-off has failed" -- and that check
goes RED rather than merely staying quiet.

WHAT LANDED TOWARD THIS BEAD (c5d11ef). The engine could not emit two facts from
one figure at all: mapping.Resolver yields one Value per token and
fact.FromValues built one Fact per Value, an unbranched chain. fisc-4rh decided
the shape and checked it against MakeID but nothing checked the mechanism.
mapping.Row now carries Fund, FundGroup and Counterpart, and FromValues is the
fan-out. That also disposes of fisc-4rh (2): the three continuation rows declare
their payer instead of a reader inferring it.

NOTE WHAT THE PLACEMENT COSTS, because it changes what this bead owes. The
fan-out is downstream of CheckTotals, so a counterpart cannot break a schedule's
tie to its own printed total -- and cannot be caught by it either. Proven on the
page: TestTheDocumentCannotCheckACounterpart redeclares every p76 payer as fund
999 and the resolver's values and the FY2026 column total are unchanged. So the
payer side is checked ONLY by the reconciliation against pp.66-67 and by
fisc-bhe's row-label check. Neither is optional.

STILL BLOCKING, filed 2026-08-24 out of the same review: fisc-wfi (a published
part has no channel for p76's headerless footnote column, and
TestPublishedPartsDeclareColumnHeaders is a ratchet), fisc-9m7 (p76's single
grand total -- a Rollup is refused twice by parse.go), fisc-j2l (clauses (b) and
(c) need a fund-group SET, a constant TABLE per (fund_group, fiscal_year), and
key collapsing for the joint clause). Also fisc-30j: the LAVWMA row has no
destination fund and three rows print no source anchor.

Re-merge the Enterprise split when writing the YAML: the fixture reads that
section as two rules around the wrapped "Connection" label, and fisc-0cs has
since landed Part.WrappedLabels. Verified the gap trims to exactly "Connection".
2026-08-24 THE fisc-9gh EDGE IS DROPPED. It was created 2026-08-21, and fisc-9gh's
own 2026-08-24 note had already moved the transfer_id clause OFF this bead --
publishing p76 cannot deliver leg-level pairing, because internal/project's
cellKey is (kind, category, fund_group) and netCells never reads f.Fund. What
fisc-9gh now needs is fund on the cell key (fisc-gxa.2), which is gated behind
the fisc-l25 product decision. So this bead was blocked on work it does not
need and cannot cause. Verified against the code before removing the edge, not
inferred from the note.
close_reason: Landed in ced45b4, together with transfers-detail-ties-to-spine. Every acceptance criterion met and measured: 88 facts at scope transfers-by-fund; the GF transfer-in leg publishes 480,400 and not 960,800 (proven by republishing at all-funds-gross and rebuilding -- it does become 960,800, and link-values-tie-to-facts, counts-reconcile and headline-transfer-residual all stay GREEN); unprojectedScopes gained its entry in the same commit; the tier-1 union-of-keys check landed with zero IN-side exceptions; BOTH budget years landed together, so revenue-detail-ties-to-spine's per-slice hand-off turns arm 2 rather than arm 3. The Enterprise split was re-merged via wrapped_labels, so it is five published rules and parts_unchecked goes 6 -> 11. Only the two budget columns are published: the historical pair miss p76's own grand total by 6,858,051 and 5,000,000, and the spine prints no column to tie them to. Still owed on the payer side, and named in the declaration verify prints: fisc-bhe.

title: CI has never executed: the facts rebuild and verify gates are untested assumptions
description:
.github/workflows/ci.yml is 260 lines across 9 jobs and HAS NEVER EXECUTED,
because this repository has no git remote. Two of those jobs assert properties
that are therefore untested assumptions rather than facts:

- `facts` rebuilds facts.jsonl and byte-compares it against the committed file
  (fisc-1wr.6). "The rebuild is byte-identical at HEAD" has never been checked
  by anything but the author's local run.
- `verify` runs ./bin/fisc verify.

Worth running both once by hand. Use CI's own form -- do NOT run `fisc build`
with its default output, which overwrites the committed audit trail:

  ./bin/fisc build --output bin/facts-rebuilt.jsonl
  cmp facts/facts.jsonl bin/facts-rebuilt.jsonl

(fisc export does not re-run the mapping engine at all -- pkg/cmd/export/data.go
:20-33 reads the committed facts -- so a rebuild is never needed just to refresh
the site.)

Related, and worth stating in the same place: the gate is partly hollow today.
fisc verify reports 5 VACUOUS checks, ci.yml deliberately does not pass --strict,
and fisc-4rh records that transfer-legs-pair can never fail as built. A large
verification surface and a partly-vacuous gate are the same picture and should be
read together.

Found in peer review of the landing plan, 2026-08-18.
acceptance_criteria: the rebuild-and-compare and fisc verify have each been run once by hand at HEAD and the result recorded here; the vacuous-check count is stated
notes:
2026-08-21 THE FIVE-VACUOUS-CHECKS TABLE IS OPTIMISTIC ON THREE OF FIVE, and a
landing plan was built on it before that was measured. Correcting the close
reason's claim that "Every one of the five is retired by a bead already in the
graph, and four of the five by the two coverage lanes."

WHAT ACTUALLY RETIRES EACH:

- fact-funds-resolve -- YES, fisc-5gk.1. It skips facts with Fund == 0
  (internal/check/vocabulary.go) and goes non-vacuous the moment pp.131-140 emit
  a real fund number. Correct as recorded.

- fact-departments-resolve -- NO, not by fisc-5gk.2 alone. The check has no
  registry branch: once subjects > 0 it falls through to an unconditional
  fmt.Errorf (vocabulary.go:186-193), and check.Vocabulary
  (subject.go:47-68) has no Department method to call. Shipping
  data/departments.yaml changes nothing. Worse, Report.Failed()
  (report.go:158-163) is true on Counts.Error WITHOUT --strict, so mapping
  pp.167-170 turns fisc verify RED rather than moving a vacuous to a pass. The
  Go change is now recorded on fisc-o15 as that bead's real deliverable.

- transfer-legs-pair -- NO. internal/project/sankey.go:465 hardcodes
  TransferID: "" on every link and is the only non-test site that sets it, and
  factSlices builds projections only for spineScope. Mapping p76 cannot reach
  the check either way. Filed as fisc-9gh, plus fisc-aes for the missing scope
  decision.

- aggregation-invariance and constraint-tier-vocabulary -- NOT under
  fisc-u2v's scope axis. Tier-3 and tier-4 nodes exist only if a projection
  draws the detail facts, which the scope decision deliberately keeps out of the
  spine graph; and one Options.Scope cannot span two scopes. Filed as fisc-gkv.
  Note the live run already says the second half of this out loud:
  "vacuous until a node carries a parent, AND UNIMPLEMENTED AFTER THAT
  (fisc-1wr.1.1)".

A SIXTH CHECK GOES RED, which the table does not contemplate because it only
counts vacuous ones. counts-reconcile carries its own warning at
internal/check/graph.go:802-813: the check package holds a SECOND implementation
of internal/project's cell netting, and "if the projection changes how it groups
or nets cells, the stock and zero counts derived here stop accounting for
